72451.title: mgr/cephadm: run one OSD create per host at a time
72451.author: tchaikov
72451.body:
"orch daemon add osd" runs `create_from_spec(force_apply=True)` while the serve loop may be applying an OSD spec to the same host. The first daemon add makes this likely, since `create_osds()` saves `osd.default` and kicks the serve loop just before its own create. On a v20.2.3 cluster the two "ceph-volume lvm batch" runs started 8 ms apart on the same disk, and the mgr deployed the OSD twice. Which run wins is down to timing, so the result is not reproducible. Later adds can race the same way with osd.default or osd.all-available-devices.

Keep the set of hosts with an OSD create in flight in `OSDService`. `create_osds()` reserves its hosts before saving the spec and holds them until its create returns, waiting if another create runs there. The serve loop does not wait. It skips a reserved host without recording the apply, so `osdspec_needs_apply()` still asks for it, and it is kicked when the host is released. By then the disk is in use, so ceph-volume skips it and exits 0. A `threading.Condition` guards the set, which the mgr command threads share with the cephadm event loop. The set lives only in memory; after an mgr failover the serve loop applies osd.default again and deploys any OSD that was prepared but not deployed, as before.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81505

72452.title: rgw/kmip: add socket I/O timeout for KMIP connections
72452.author: supriti
72452.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81490

Adds rgw_crypt_kmip_socket_io_timeout_sec (0-300 s, default 0 = no
timeout) to set SO_RCVTIMEO/SO_SNDTIMEO on KMIP connections, so a KMIP
server that stops answering no longer blocks requests indefinitely.

A connection that may be out of step (I/O failure, undecodable or
mismatched reply) is now closed instead of reused, so a late reply
can't be read by the next request.

Tested with a proxy holding PyKMIP's reply: unset waits as before;
with 5 s the request fails after ~5.7 s and the next request succeeds
on a new connection.

72453.title: python-common: keep per-path crush_device_class in DeviceSelection.to_json()
72453.author: tchaikov
72453.body:
6c6cb2f5130 let a `DeviceSelection` path carry its own `crush_device_class`, but `to_json()` still writes only the path strings. So "ceph orch ls --export" never shows the class, and cephadm's SpecStore, which persists specs with `to_json()`, loses it at the next mgr restart. An OSD created from the spec after that, e.g. one replaced with "ceph orch osd rm --replace", gets the spec level class or the one the OSD detects itself, and CRUSH rules for the intended class no longer pick it.

Write a path that has a class as the dict from_json() accepts, and keep the others as plain strings, so specs without per-path classes serialize as before.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81605

72454.title: tentacle: qa/cephadm: fix test_set_mon_crush_locations test
72454.author: kginonredhat
72454.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74523

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/67436
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74523

## Summary

`task/test_set_mon_crush_locations` fails because it still requires `mon dump --format json` to report `crush_location` as the string `{datacenter=a}`.

`mon: add time_added to mon_info_t` (`c5239a4c46d` on tentacle) switched `MonMap::dump()` over to `mon_info_t::dump()`. That encodes the crush-location map with `encode_json`, so JSON now looks like:

```json
"crush_location": [{"key": "datacenter", "val": "a"}]
```

`jq` then compares that array to the string `{datacenter=a}` and exits 1, even when the location was applied. Plain `ceph mon dump` still prints `{datacenter=a}`. The sample in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/67436 is a mon whose location was set correctly and would still fail the old check.

This is a clean `git cherry-pick -x` of 456eb5d2f65. It only updates the workunit to look up `crush_location[].key` and `.val`. No daemon or mgr code changes.

Umbrella already contains 456eb5d2f65. Squid has the same mismatch after its own `time_added` backport (`48ecc59c530`) and is updated in a separate PR.

## Test plan

- [ ] `rados/cephadm` workunit `task/test_set_mon_crush_locations` passes on tentacle
- [ ] `ceph mon dump --format json` shows `crush_location` key `datacenter` / val `a` for mon.a, and the rack entries for mon.b and mon.c

72465.title: mgr/cephadm: reconfigure NFS daemons on placement change
72465.author: Shubhaj1810
72465.body:
## Description

NFS daemons were not updating `CEPH_NODES_LIST` when NFS service placement changed.

The placement-derived Ceph node IPs were not part of the NFS daemon dependencies, so existing daemons did not enter the reconfiguration path after placement changes. Only newly deployed daemons received the updated node list.

This change:

- tracks resolved Ceph node IPs in NFS dependencies
- detects placement-only changes
- updates `ganesha.conf` through the normal reconfiguration path
- sends `SIGHUP` to `ganesha.nfsd` instead of restarting the container when `ceph_nodes` is the only changed dependency
- preserves the existing redeploy behavior for stronger dependency changes

## Before

NFS was initially deployed on `ceph-node-00` and `ceph-node-01`:

```text
nfs.nfs-cluster1.0.0.ceph-node-00
nfs.nfs-cluster1.1.0.ceph-node-01
```

Both daemons had:

```text
CEPH_NODES_LIST {
    Ceph_Nodes = 192.168.100.100, 192.168.100.101;
}
```

After adding `ceph-node-02` to the placement, the new daemon received:

```text
CEPH_NODES_LIST {
    Ceph_Nodes = 192.168.100.100, 192.168.100.101, 192.168.100.102;
}
```

while the existing daemons continued to contain only:

```text
192.168.100.100, 192.168.100.101
```

and required redeployment to obtain the updated configuration.

## After

With the fix applied, placement was expanded from:

```text
ceph-node-00
ceph-node-01
```

to:

```text
ceph-node-00
ceph-node-01
ceph-node-02
```

The existing daemon container IDs remained unchanged:

```text
ceph-node-00 → 28bb2c8ca26b
ceph-node-01 → 2efa2f239426
```

and a new daemon was created on `ceph-node-02`:

```text
ceph-node-02 → f2ea1b78cd5f
```

All three daemons received the updated configuration:

```text
CEPH_NODES_LIST {
    Ceph_Nodes = 192.168.100.100, 192.168.100.101, 192.168.100.102;
}
```

This was verified on the existing daemons and the newly deployed daemon.  

Placement was then shrunk back to `ceph-node-00` and `ceph-node-01`. The `ceph-node-02` daemon was removed, while the existing daemon container IDs remained unchanged. 

The remaining daemons correctly received:

```text
CEPH_NODES_LIST {
    Ceph_Nodes = 192.168.100.100, 192.168.100.101;
}
```

Also validated manually on a live 3-node cluster:

- initial 2-node NFS deployment
- placement expansion 2 → 3
- existing daemon reconfiguration without redeployment
- placement shrink 3 → 2
- existing daemon reconfiguration without redeployment

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81517
Signed-off-by: Shubha Jain [SHUBHA.JAIN1@ibm.com]

72470.title: rgw: reject unrecognized query params in s3 requests
72470.author: cbodley
72470.body:
s3 uses query parameters to represent "subresources" and routes those requests to different rest apis. rgw supports lots of these subresources, but not all of them - and aws continues to add more

rgw does this routing in RGWOp factory functions like RGWHandler_REST_Bucket_S3::op_put(), where we check query parameters for the subresources we support, then fall back to the default resource like RGWCreateBucket_ObjStore_S3

the risk of this strategy is that requests for subresources we don't support get incorrectly mapped to the default bucket/object resource. this can result in data loss when a PUT request falls back to PutObject and overwrites an existing object, or when a DELETE request falls back to DeleteBucket and removes a bucket prematurely

to mitigate this risk, both for current subresources that we don't support and for subresources added to aws in the future, we can't fall back to the default resource if the request conains any unrecognized query parameters

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80921

72471.title: seastore/omap: ensure only 1 live _fastinfo in log chain
72471.author: shraddhaag
72471.body: ## Issue With each transaction (which can be a batch of multiple client operations): Expected behaviour: the old `_fastinfo` is marked removed and a new one is appended at the end of the newest node. There should always be only 1 live `_fastinfo`. Observed behaviour: if a new log node is created in the current transaction, the new log entries are only appended to, not overwritten. The old `_fastinfo` in this case is not marked removed. This means we have multiple live `_fastinfo`. Because of this, these nodes couldn't be freed and we have a memory leak. As the log nodes weren't getting free, the chain kept growing longer. This resulted in increased time in traversing the chain, which finally led to sharp decrease in total IOPS and the shard starvation issue. ## Fix For the new log nodes, overwrite the old `_fastinfo` with the new entry for each pair. This helps save space as well as prevents the memory leak. For the old nodes, mark the `_fastinfo` as removed so they can be freed as well. The main case: overwrite instead of append in the new log nodes. Rare case 1: If multiple new log nodes are created in the same transaction, the `_fastinfo`at then end of each new node will be marked as removed. This only happens when the `_fastinfo` entry in the old node could not overwritten due to size misfit. Rare case 2: If all writes go to the new log node, the `_fastinfo` in the committed node is now marked removed. This only happens when the `_fastinfo` entry in the old node could not overwritten due to size misfit. Rare case 3: If all writes go to the new log node and each log entry is too big to fit in a single node, the single log spans multiple new nodes. In this case, the `_fastinfo` in the old node is marked removed. Note: to mark the old `_fastinfo` removed in O(1), I added a new function `remove_last_entry`. This works for both committed nodes and new `inital_pending` nodes. ## Testing Added unit tests which cover each of the above scenarios for both of the seastore backends. All tests are passing. Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81486

72472.title: mgr: do not abort or pin PG stats on corrupted daemon reports
72472.author: lumir-sliva
72472.body:
A daemon can send the mgr a message that decodes fine at the messenger level but carries garbage inside. In the tracker below, one host corrupts msgr2 secure-mode payloads in whole 16-byte AES blocks, which still pass GCM, so the mgr gets well-formed MPGStats / MMgrOpen / MMgrReport with bogus contents. Two things in the mgr turn that into a cluster-wide problem:

- `DaemonServer::handle_open()` and `handle_report()` decode the config blob, and `handle_report()` the packed perf counters, without catching `buffer::error`. One corrupted MMgrOpen aborts the mgr in `ms_dispatch`; the daemon reconnects to the next mgr and can take that one down too.
- `ClusterState::ingest_pgstats()` skips reports older than what it holds. One corrupted `pg_stat_t` with a huge `reported_epoch:reported_seq` makes every later genuine report look older, so the PG sits in a garbage state (`stale+creating+...+snaptrim_error`) until the mgr fails over, while its primary reports `active+clean`.

This series:
- decodes the config before touching any daemon state, and drops the session when it or the perf counters don't decode: mark the connection down and forget it in `osd_cons` / `daemon_connections` (a local `mark_down()` doesn't go through `ms_handle_reset()`). The daemon reconnects and resends;
- ignores a `pg_stat_t` whose `reported_epoch` is beyond the epoch of the MPGStats carrying it, i.e. beyond the sender's own osdmap;
- lets a newer report from the OSD that sent the stored stats replace them even if the stored pair is higher. Only primaries report and one OSD's reports arrive in order, so that covers a corrupted `reported_seq`. Late reports from a previous primary are still skipped;
- adds unit tests for both cases and for the late-report case, in a separate commit so the fixes pick cleanly to squid and tentacle, which don't have `test_clusterstate.cc`.

Testing:
- `unittest_mgr_clusterstate`: the two new pin tests fail on main, 12/12 pass with the series.
- vstart on main, with one OSD's `EVP_EncryptUpdate` interposed to corrupt the odd 16-byte block before encryption. Without the series the mgr aborted 17 times in 8 minutes in `handle_open`, and a PG was pinned within a minute until `ceph mgr fail`. With it, 10 minutes of the same load gave no abort and no pinned PG; the mgr log shows `dropping session ... cannot decode its config`, `... but the osd is at e64, ignoring` and `had 1.32 from osd.0 at 64:44466389293371572, taking its 64:185`.

Not covered here: a garbage metric type in MMgrReport still hits `ceph_abort()` in `UnknownMetricPayload`'s DENC. I'll send that separately.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68550

72473.title: mgr: fail decoding an unknown metric type instead of aborting
72473.author: lumir-sliva
72473.body:
MetricReportMessage (in MMgrReport, decoded by the mgr) and MetricConfigMessage (in MMgrConfigure, decoded by OSDs and MDSs) turn a type they don't know into `UnknownMetricPayload` / `UnknownConfigPayload`, whose decoder calls `ceph_abort()`. Senders only encode types the peer supports (`should_encode()`), so an unknown type only shows up when the message got corrupted, and then a single message takes down the mgr, or an OSD or MDS.

The decoders now throw `buffer::malformed_input` for an unknown type. `decode_message()` handles that like any other malformed message: the messenger drops it and resets the connection, and the daemon's mgr session reconnects (the mgr resends MMgrConfigure on open).

Follow-up to #72472, same tracker: one host there corrupts msgr2 secure-mode payloads in 16-byte blocks that still pass GCM.

Testing: the new `unittest_mgr_metrictypes` garbles the type field of an encoded report and config message. On main the binary aborts at `MetricTypes.h:85` / `:259`; with this change both decodes throw `malformed_input`. `ceph-mgr` and `ceph-osd` build.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68550

72479.title: include/container_ios: include <ostream>, not <iosfwd>
72479.author: dvanders
72479.body:
`include/container_ios.h` defines `operator<<` overloads on `std::ostream` but only includes `<iosfwd>`. libstdc++ and older libc++ pull `<ostream>` in through `<iomanip>`; newer libc++ doesn't, and `librbd/ConfigWatcher.cc` fails on macOS:

```
container_ios.h:95:7: error: invalid operands to binary expression
('std::ostream' (aka 'basic_ostream<char>') and 'const char[2]')
```

Reproduced with Apple clang 21 and `-D_LIBCPP_REMOVE_TRANSITIVE_INCLUDES` on a file that includes only this header; including `<ostream>` fixes it. Reported by @bstillwell while building the macOS series.

72480.title: os/bluestore/Writer: don't leave reused released space marked unused
72480.author: ming1
72480.body:
With `bluestore_write_v2=true`, a deferred write may reuse space released earlier in the same transaction, while the rest of that AU stays marked unused. A later small write there goes direct, and an older deferred write still queued for the same disk bytes then overwrites it: the object fails its csum after an OSD restart.

Mark only freshly allocated space unused, so writes into a reused AU are deferred too and queued after the older one. The unit test reproduces the csum error with write_v2 and passes with the fix.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80982

72490.title: os/bluestore: reserve bdev label copies added by online expand
72490.author: ming1
72490.body:
An online expand (`bluefs-bdev-expand` on a running OSD) writes bdev label copies into the new space but gives the whole new range to the allocator. Object data can then be allocated over a label copy, and the next label write corrupts it. Give the new range to the allocator without the label blocks.

With bitmap based allocators that is not enough: `BitmapAllocator::expand()` already marks the new space free without accounting for it, so the label blocks stay allocatable, and the hybrid allocator ends up with the new space free twice after a spillover. Leave the new space allocated in `expand()`; callers free it with `init_add_free()`.

Unit tests cover bitmap and hybrid expand; the online expand test runs with the avl, bitmap, hybrid and hybrid_btree2 allocators.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80951

72502.title: qa/rados: reduce osd dispatch delay injection probability to 1%
72502.author: aainscow
72502.body:
`msgr-failures/osd-dispatch-delay` sets `osd_debug_inject_dispatch_delay_probability` to 0.1 with a 0.1 s duration. As well as `ms_fast_dispatch`, the delay is injected twice per item in `ShardedOpWQ::_process()` (`OSD.cc`, before and after `pg->lock()`), so every op queue item pays an expected 20 ms sleep. That includes client ops, sub-op replies, peering events and `NullEvt`s.

The compression objectstore facets limit OSDs to 1 shard × 2 threads (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/72879). Combined with the injection, that caps each OSD at about 95 queue items/s.

## What goes wrong

pggrow thrashing on wide EC pools pushes arrivals past that cap:
- every map epoch queues a `NullEvt` to each of the 80–170 PGs on an OSD, and the thrasher toggles `noscrub`/`nodeep-scrub` about every 2 s, each toggle being an epoch;
- pool splits add bursts of notifies.

Peering events are served strictly ahead of client work (WPQ strict queue, mClock immediate class), so the backlog never drains. Client ops and EC sub-read replies then starve for more than 10 minutes.

Evidence from the debug-20 logs of two failures in one QA batch:
- **Runs:** `skanta-2026-10-03_10:12:06-rados-wip-bharath19-testing-20261002.123021-main-distro-default-trial/604392` (read, WPQ) and `…/603575` (write, mClock).
- **Throughput:** about 95 items/s, all of it peering class, for 11–13 minutes, with no client items dequeued in that window.
- **Backlog:** peaked at 6,000–6,700 items, about a minute of queue wait per item.
- **Worker time:** 99.6% in the injected sleep, with about 0.05 ms of real work per item.
- **Model check:** a fixed-capacity model fed only with the measured arrivals reproduces the measured backlog to within about 5%.

## History

Before `rados_osd_op_timeout` was set (#71861), this showed up as `wait_for_recovery` timeouts (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75216). Across all k=10 m=4 thrash-erasure-code jobs on trial200 from January to October 2026:

| dispatch-delay | compression=yes | jobs | `wait_for_recovery` failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| no | no | 60 | 0% |
| no | yes | 61 | 3% |
| yes | no | 72 | 0% |
| yes | yes | 159 | 49% |

With the client timeout it now shows up as `ceph_test_rados` `-ETIMEDOUT` (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81135).

## This change

Lower the probability to 0.01. Replaying the measured arrivals from both runs against the capacity implied by 1% gives:
- about 580–720 items/s of capacity;
- 24–35% utilisation at the worst 10 s burst;
- no backlog.

The perturbation still happens, at roughly 2 sleeps/s per OSD at 100 items/s. This file also feeds `rados/thrash` and the other `thrash-erasure-code*` suites through their `msgr-failures` symlinks.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81629

72503.title: osd/OSDMap: skip calc_pg_upmaps when an up OSD has no weight
72503.author: aainscow
72503.body:
The mgr balancer in upmap mode can abort ceph-mgr with
`OSDMap.cc: FAILED ceph_assert(osd_weight.count(oid))` in `OSDMap::calc_deviations()`
(https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/48896). This happens when CRUSH maps a PG to an OSD
whose CRUSH weight is 0.

**How it happens.** straw2 returns the first item of a bucket when every item in it has
weight 0. The chosen leaf is then checked only against the OSD's reweight (in/out), not
its CRUSH weight. Take a rule with several `take` steps, such as the legacy stretch-mode
rule `take site1; chooseleaf ...; emit; take site2; chooseleaf ...; emit`. If every OSD
of one site is crush-reweighted to 0 while it is still in, the first OSD of that site
goes into every up set. `build_pool_pgs_info()` counts the PGs on that OSD, but
`get_osds_weight()` leaves the OSD out of the weight map. The other site keeps
`osd_weight_total` above 0, so the existing early return does not fire, and
`calc_deviations()` asserts. With one OSD per `take`, the PGs stay full size and
active+clean, so the balancer aborts the active mgr on every run. The same core shows up
now and then in `qa/standalone/mon-stretch/mon-stretch-uneven-crush-weights.sh`, which
sets both OSDs of one zone to CRUSH weight 0.

**When it can happen.** Zero CRUSH weight alone is not enough. Adding OSDs at weight 0, or draining an OSD or a host, does not trigger it with the rules Ceph creates (`take default` followed by `chooseleaf` over hosts): straw2 never picks a zero-weight item while any sibling has weight. It also needs a manually created CRUSH rule whose `take` reaches only zero-weight items. Examples are a rule with one `take` per site (as written for stretch clusters) while a whole site is crush-reweighted to 0 but still in, or, from reading straw2 but not tested, a device-class rule whose class has only zero-weight OSDs.

**Fix.** `calc_pg_upmaps()` logs an error and returns without changes when an OSD in an
up set has no weight under the pool's rule. Upmaps cannot move those PGs to a weighted
OSD in the same subtree. `total_pgs` also counts the copies on the unweighted OSD, so
the targets for the rest of the pool would be wrong too. The mgr balancer and
`osdmaptool --upmap` call `calc_pg_upmaps()` for one pool at a time, so other pools are
still balanced.

**Relation to https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/53736** (closed without merging). That
PR kept zero-weight OSDs in the weight map. As its author found while writing a test,
this only moves the abort to `ceph_assert(target > 0)`: a zero weight gives a zero
target, and `calc_deviations()` divides by the target. He also could not find how a
zero-weight OSD gets into an up set, so there was no reproducer. This PR leaves the
weight map and both asserts as they are. Instead it skips the pool when its mapping does
not follow its weights, and the new unit test reproduces the trigger.

One commit, `osd/OSDMap: skip calc_pg_upmaps when an up OSD has no weight`, with the fix and
`OSDMapTest.BUG_48896`. The test builds a two-datacenter rule with one `take` per datacenter, sets
both OSDs of dc-0 to CRUSH weight 0 (still in), and checks that every PG still maps to osd.0. It
then runs `calc_pg_upmaps()` and checks that no PG is upmapped to a zero-weight OSD.

Testing (Debug build):
- `unittest_osdmap --gtest_filter=OSDMapTest.BUG_48896` without the `OSDMap.cc` change aborts with
  `FAILED ceph_assert(osd_weight.count(oid))` in `calc_deviations()`. With the fix it
  passes.
- Full `unittest_osdmap` with the fix: all 46 tests pass. Only the new test reaches the new
  early return.

72504.title: mon: fix use-after-free of MonSession in handle_auth_request
72504.author: aainscow
72504.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81565



Monitor::handle_auth_request()'s new-session branch hands the only reference to a freshly created
MonSession to the connection (con->set_priv(RefCountedPtr{s, false})) and then keeps using the bare
`s` pointer (start_session, the session dout, the later s->authenticated check and
ms_handle_fast_authentication).

handle_auth_request runs on an msgr-worker thread with the connection lock dropped
(ProtocolV2::_handle_auth_request). When the monitor shuts down (Monitor::shutdown ->
messenger->shutdown -> mark_down_all), a connection that is still authenticating is stopped from
the shutdown thread and its reset is delivered on the dispatch thread. Monitor::ms_handle_reset()
then drops the connection's reference and returns early because the monitor is shutting down,
which destroys the MonSession and its auth_handler. ms_handle_reset never takes auth_lock, and it
drops the reference before taking any lock, so nothing serialises the free against the concurrent
handle_auth_request. The worker then uses the freed session and auth_handler in start_session.

This was seen once as a ceph-mon SIGSEGV 12 ms after SIGTERM in msgr-worker, with the faulting PC
in the heap (a call through a freed object), in a teuthology run of
rados:thrash-erasure-code-stretch.

The more-input branch of the same function already holds the reference in a function-scope
RefCountedPtr and bails if it is null ("this can happen if the async ms_handle_reset event races
with the unlocked call into handle_auth_request"); the new-session branch did not. The fix keeps a
reference across the whole window there too.

How it was confirmed: a temporary local check (not included here) that aborted the mon whenever
the connection was the only owner of the new session right after set_priv fired on the first
client authentication without this change, and never with it (3 runs each). The mon unit tests

72507.title: mgr/devicehealth: give each serve pass its own db retry budget
72507.author: lumir-sliva
72507.body:
devicehealth fails with "Module 'devicehealth' has failed: disk I/O error" (or "unknown operation") every few days on long-running mgrs, and only a mgr failover clears it.

`MgrModuleRecoverDB` reopens the database up to `MAX_DBCLEANUP_RETRIES` (3) times when the wrapped call raises `sqlite3.DatabaseError`, which is what libcephsqlite raises once its lock renewal fails or its client is blocklisted, e.g. after the `.mgr` PG was unavailable for longer than `cephsqlite_lock_renewal_timeout`. devicehealth applied the decorator to `_do_serve()`, the loop that runs for the whole life of the module, while the retry count only lives as long as one call of the wrapped function. So the module could recover from three lost databases per mgr activation, however far apart, and the fourth failed it for good.

This moves the loop body into `_serve_once()` and decorates that instead, so the budget covers consecutive failures within one pass. A database that stays unusable still fails the module after 3 reopens.

Reproduced on vstart by repeatedly blocklisting the mgr's libcephsqlite client (`ceph mgr dump` -> `active_clients`), with `mgr/devicehealth/sleep_interval 2` and `scrape_frequency 4` so the module writes every few seconds:

```
main:
loss 1: blocklisted libcephsqlite client 10.162.0.2:0/2004544131, errors caught: 1, module running
loss 2: blocklisted libcephsqlite client 10.162.0.2:0/1237131041, errors caught: 2, module running
loss 3: blocklisted libcephsqlite client 10.162.0.2:0/1461716975, errors caught: 3, module running
loss 4: blocklisted libcephsqlite client 10.162.0.2:0/2254942036, errors caught: 4, Module 'devicehealth' has failed: disk I/O error

with this change:
loss 1 ... loss 10: module running; scraping continues afterwards
```

The new unit test fails without the change (`OperationalError: disk I/O error` on the 4th spaced failure) and passes with it.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/72958

72508.title: rgw/compression: use compression type fixed at multipart upload init
72508.author: kchheda3
72508.body:
If the placement target's compression type changes (e.g. `radosgw-admin zone placement modify --compression ...` followed by a period commit) while a multipart upload is in progress, parts uploaded before the change are stored with the old compression type and later parts with the new one. CompleteMultipartUpload rejects the mix with `InvalidPart`, so a server-side config change breaks client uploads.

This resolves the compression type once at InitiateMultipartUpload and stores it in `multipart_upload_info`, the same way the checksum type is already handled. Every UploadPart (including UploadPartCopy) then uses the stored type instead of the live placement config.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79629

72522.title: tools/contrib: sync upmap-remapped.py with cernceph/ceph-scripts
72522.author: dvanders
72522.body:
Bring `src/tools/contrib/upmap-remapped.py` up to date with `tools/upmap/upmap-remapped.py` of [cernceph/ceph-scripts](https://github.com/cernceph/ceph-scripts) at f08c004d102e ([cernceph/ceph-scripts#51](https://github.com/cernceph/ceph-scripts/pull/51)). The file here is a straight copy of that version.

The fix that matters most: on erasure-coded pools the old ordering loop never terminates when the mappings form a cycle longer than two (e.g. `0->2, 2->7, 7->0`), which a pg split or new hardware can produce. The script then spins at 100% CPU and prints nothing. The new code emits the mappings as ordered chains and leaves cycles out, so those pgs stay remapped and backfill.

Checked by running `gen_upmap` from both versions on these EC cases:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 3-cycle `0->2, 2->7, 7->0` | hangs | `[]` |
| cycle plus a chain | hangs | the chain, in order |
| 2-way swap | `[]` | `[]` |
| chain `1->2, 2->3` | `[(2, 3), (1, 2)]` | `[(2, 3), (1, 2)]` |

The rest of that series is error handling and cleanup: replicated pools never map onto an osd already in the up set, degraded+remapped pgs with mismatched set lengths are skipped instead of failing an assert, unknown pools are skipped, mon commands get a timeout and their failures are reported, argparse, and the librados connection is closed on every exit. The output format (the `ceph osd pg-upmap-items` lines and the peering waits) is unchanged.

72534.title: mgr/cephadm: seed OSD ok-to-stop with the OSDs still pending upgrade
72534.author: FredNass
72534.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81587

## Problem

When upgrading OSDs, cephadm runs `osd ok-to-stop <id> --max N` with a single OSD (N = `mgr/cephadm/max_parallel_osd_upgrades`) and upgrades the OSDs it gets back. The mgr grows that set in `DaemonServer::_maximize_ok_to_stop_set()` by walking up the CRUSH tree and adding sibling OSDs in ascending id order, without knowing which of them already run the target version.

After the first pass, the batch is therefore made of the requested OSD plus the lowest-numbered OSDs under the same parent, which are already upgraded. On a host with 40 OSDs and N=16, the first pass upgrades osd.0-15 and every following pass a single OSD: **25 passes instead of 3**.

## Fix

Seed `osd ok-to-stop` with the OSDs on the same host that still need to be upgraded, capped at `max_parallel_osd_upgrades`, so the batch the mgr returns is made of OSDs that actually need upgrading. If that set cannot be stopped together, drop OSDs from the end and retry, down to the single OSD cephadm used to request (no shrinking on `-EAGAIN`, where a smaller set would not help). PG safety is still decided by the mgr.

This only changes the default (non CRUSH bucket scoped) upgrade path.

## Tests

New unit tests in `src/pybind/mgr/cephadm/tests/test_upgrade.py`, with a fake `osd ok-to-stop` mimicking `_maximize_ok_to_stop_set()`:
- 40 OSDs / N=16 → 3 passes (`[0-15]`, `[16-31]`, `[32-39]`)
- `max_parallel_osd_upgrades` is respected
- the seed shrinks until the set is ok to stop
- batches stay on one host
- peer selection skips other hosts, non-OSDs, the OSD itself and OSDs already on the target image
- no shrink on `-EAGAIN`

72535.title: cls/rbd: reject updates to removed group snapshots
72535.author: pkalever
72535.body:
Problem:

group_snap_set() creates a new group snapshot and its snap_order key when the snapshot is in the INCOMPLETE state.

It also accepted an update in the COMPLETE state when the snapshot key did not exist. This created only the snapshot key because the snap_order key is created only for a new INCOMPLETE snapshot. The incomplete metadata caused group snapshot listing to fail with EINVAL.

Solution:

Before updating a snapshot outside the INCOMPLETE state, require its snapshot key to exist. Log an error and return EINVAL when the key is missing. Updates to existing snapshots continue to work.

Extend the group snapshot removal test to verify that a removed snapshot cannot be added again directly in the COMPLETE state.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81590

72537.title: crimson/os/seastore,osd: report the real reason mkfs could not create a device
72537.author: ronen-fr
72537.body:
check_create_device() mapped every creation failure except EEXIST to input_output_error, and OSD::mkfs() turned that into ceph_abort(). An ENOSPC - the common case, since a seastore OSD creates one device file per cache and data device under the same mount point - surfaced as a SIGABRT, a core dump and the single line:

  OSD::mkfs error creating empty object store in /var/lib/ceph/osd/ceph-0: \
    Input/output error

Keep the condition instead: map ENOSPC, EACCES/EPERM and ENOENT to the matching errors (adding enospc to Device::access_ertr so it reaches the OSD), and on ENOSPC log the requested size against the space actually available. Have OSD::mkfs log and throw rather than abort, so mkfs exits non-zero instead of dumping core.

Also remove the partially created device file on failure: the open is exclusive|create, so a leftover file makes the next mkfs take the EEXIST "already exists" path and succeed with a device that was never fully allocated.

72541.author: bluikko
72541.body:
Don't change CI approval labels if pusher has write permission to the repo.

When someone with a write access to the repository pushes into a PR authored by someone with no write access, the already added `ci-approved` label is removed and `needs-ci-approval` is readded.

If someone else than the PR author pushed to the PR, permission level of the pusher should be checked (probably) instead of the PR author.

72544.title: osd/SnapMapper: stop rescanning purged_snaps per mapping key
72544.author: Antek74
72544.body:
`Scrubber::run()` opened a fresh `omap_iterate` over `purged_snaps`,
from its start, for every mapping key: `O(M*P)`.  On snapshot-heavy
OSDs this pinned a core for days.

Collect the `purged_snaps` rows once up front, sort them numerically by
(pool, begin), and merge overlapping and adjacent rows of one pool
into disjoint ranges. Then each mapping key needs only one binary
search: `O(M log P)` instead of `O(M*P)`.

The numeric sort also fixes missed strays: with pools ordered as
decimal strings, the old walk could stop at a pool-20 row and never
reach pool 3.

The sort is needed because the on-disk key order is not numeric in
the pool: the pool id is a decimal string, so pool 20 sorts before
pool 3. The merge is needed because the writer can leave rows that
overlap or touch: `record_purged_snaps()` merges a new interval only
with rows already on disk, so intervals carried in one call do not
see each other. Once the ranges are disjoint and sorted, the last
row that starts at or before the snap is the only one that can
cover it.

Adds `unittest_scrubber_run`, a unit test for `Scrubber::run()`: it
builds a SnapMapper over a MemStore and fills it through the same
writer methods ceph-osd uses (`record_purged_snaps()`, `add_oid()`),
then checks every stray the scrub reports.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81592
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81798

72552.title: LRC: Store the layer plugin in the EC profile
72552.author: jamiepryde
72552.body:
### Problem
PR #58052 changed the default LRC layer plugin from jerasure to isa. For k/m/l-type LRC profiles, and explicit-layer LRC profiles that don't specify a plugin, the per-layer plugin is not stored in the profile (this was by design). It is re-derived when the plugin is initialized using the default on each OSD. This means that any pre-tentacle cluster that upgrades to tentacle or later will have its LRC pools silently switch from using jerasure to isa. Jerasure and isa produce the same first coding chunk using XOR, but subsequent coding chunks differ.

### Fix
Record the layer plugin explicitly in the LRC profile using a new layer-plugin key. This is resolved:
* on the OSD at runtime in build_pg_backend() during the upgrade window, before require_osd_release is committed. The tentacle OSD will continue using jerasure for a pre-tentacle LRC pool.
* in the mon when require-osd-release is committed in encode_pending(). 
* in the mon at profile creation (in both the normalize_profile() and the default EC profile paths).
The new key is a per-profile default. If a layer already has a plugin specified then that will continue to be used. If the key is absent, the default remains isa.

### Limitation
Clusters that have already upgraded to tentacle or later with pre-tentacle LRC profiles / pools cannot be automatically repaired. This fix only protects clusters that have not already upgraded.

### Testing
* New unit tests added to TestErasureCodeLrc to test setting layer-plugin.
* Mocked upgrade testing on a vstart cluster. Testing using the mon_debug_no_require_* flags to pin require_osd_release at squid, and fixed and unfixed versions of the OSD and mon. Daemons were swapped in place to simulate the upgrade. Checked that upgrading to unfixed tentacle hits the bug. Checked that upgrading to the fix stores jerasure as the layer-plugin for an existing LRC profile that does not have layer-plugin set.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81369

72554.title: cls/rgw: fix duplicate CURRENT null versions in versioning-suspended buckets
72554.author: k-keshava
72554.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81603

Problem

In a bucket with versioning suspended, concurrent PUT and DELETE (no version id) on the same key corrupt the bucket index. ListObjectVersions returns many VersionId=null entries with IsLatest=true, and "radosgw-admin bi list" shows leftover versioned list entries (<key>\0v<epoch>\0i, empty instance) that still carry FLAG_CURRENT. Running the same requests one at a time never triggers it.

On a vstart cluster with 8 concurrent clients x 200 PUT+DELETE iterations, main ends up with 6-14 list entries flagged CURRENT for one key, and v20.2.4 with 27 (350+ under heavier contention).

Root cause

Confirmed with debug_objclass=20 OSD logs, following one leaked entry from creation to orphaning.

1. Orphaned list entry. A null version's instance entry key (\x801000_<key>\0i) is reused by every null generation, and its versioned_epoch is the only way to find its list entry. When rgw_bucket_complete_op() removes that instance entry (a DEL, or a CANCEL after a racing delete marked it non-existent), only the instance entry is removed. prepare_op() then recreates it with versioned_epoch=0, so the next link_olh() computes the list key from epoch 0, misses the real one, and the old list entry stays with FLAG_CURRENT set.

   Observed sequence: PUT link_olh writes the list entry (CURRENT) -> a late complete_op DEL sets exists=false -> complete_op CANCEL removes the instance entry -> prepare_op recreates it with epoch 0 -> the next link_olh unlinks <key>\0v915\0i (which doesn't exist), orphaning the entry.

2. Version marker overwritten. When versions are listed, RGW sends dir_suggest_changes for the orphaned null entries. rgw_dir_suggest_changes() builds the key with encode_obj_index_key(), which for an empty instance is the plain <key>, so it overwrites the version marker. After that, read_key_entry() resolves null-version operations to the plain entry, and every later write leaks another list entry.

Changes

- cls/rgw: remove list entry together with its versioned instance entry. A new remove_key_entry() removes a versioned instance entry's list entry along with it. It is used by the CANCEL and DEL removal paths in rgw_bucket_complete_op(), and does nothing if the list entry is already gone. get_list_index_key() now takes a const reference.
- cls/rgw: dir_suggest_changes must not overwrite a version marker. Suggestions whose on-disk entry is a version marker are skipped.
- test/cls_rgw: regression tests.
  - index_null_version_racing_remove replays the sequence above at the cls level and checks that exactly one list entry stays CURRENT.
  - index_suggest_version_marker sends update and remove suggestions for a null version and checks that the marker survives.

Testing

Run on a vstart cluster (Ubuntu 24.04 arm64):

- New unit tests: fail without the fix (2 CURRENT entries; marker flags 8 -> 3), pass with it.
- ceph_test_cls_rgw (full suite, replicated + EC): 44/44 pass with the fix.
- ceph_test_cls_rgw_stats: passes with the fix.
- End-to-end reproducer (boto3; versioning suspended; 4-16 concurrent clients doing PUT+DELETE): without the fix, 6-14 CURRENT entries and the marker overwritten; with the fix, exactly 1 CURRENT entry and the marker intact, across 6 rounds.

With debug logging on, one 8x200 round hit the race 8 times, and the new code removed the list entry each time, so the clean results come from the fix actually running.

The same patch was also verified on v20.2.4 (tentacle). It applies there with only small test adjustments: the older TEST_F fixture, and an increasing olh_epoch, because there link_olh takes the epoch from RGW. Both tests fail on stock 20.2.4 and pass with the fix, the full suite passes, and the reproducer is clean (27 -> 1 CURRENT).

Notes for reviewers

- The fix restores the index invariant that a versioned instance entry and its list entry are removed together. I didn't change the RGW-side ordering that lets a la

72555.title: mon: preserve log acknowledgements and release rejected requests
72555.author: yulongshi0816
72555.body:
The unconditional no_reply() in preprocess_log() introduced by 56cb53db96380c917f4192c31cbdd0f0f3ef1fe9 releases a forwarded request before its log entries are committed. The later MLogAck is then dropped by the peon because the routed request no longer exists, leaving the client log queue untrimmed.

Restore the preprocessing flow so new log entries retain their routed request until _updated_log() sends the acknowledgement. Call no_reply() in prepare_log() when rejecting an MLog with a mismatched fsid, so the peon can release the routed request on the path that originally leaked.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81604
Related PR: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/61933

72556.title: common/io_exerciser: start Seq15 at its first stage
72556.author: aainscow
72556.body:
Seq15's `stage` member in `src/common/io_exerciser/IoSequence.h` has no initializer and the constructor does not set it, so a new Seq15 starts at whatever stage the reused heap memory holds. In a long `ceph_test_rados_io_sequence --parallel 4` run, one object's Seq15 issued `Create`, `Barrier`, `Swap`, `Truncate` and aborted:

```
src/common/io_exerciser/ObjectModel.cc: 153: FAILED ceph_assert(primary_created)
```

It started at `SWAP_TO_PRIMARY`, swapped to the secondary object it had never created and truncated it. Starting at `WRITE_SECONDARY`, `COPY_FROM_SECONDARY` or `READ_SECONDARY` also aborts, and the other stages skip part of the sequence.

Initialise `stage` to `WRITE_PRIMARY`. valgrind reports the uninitialised read in `Seq15::_next()` on a `--dryrun` of Seq15 without the fix, and no errors on a dry run of every sequence with it.

`Seq15IgnoresPriorMemoryContents`, added to `unittest_io_sequence` from #72383, builds a Seq15 in zeroed memory and one in memory that holds `SWAP_TO_PRIMARY`, and expects the same ops from both. Without the fix the second one runs `Create`, `Barrier`, `Swap`, `Truncate`; with it both run the full sequence.

Depends on #72383: this branch is stacked on it, and only the last two commits belong to this PR.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81606

72563.title: rgw: graceful, bounded and staggered realm reload on period commit
72563.author: RaminNietzsche
72563.body:
`radosgw-admin period update --commit` makes every gateway in the realm reload its configuration. The reload pauses the Beast frontend, and that pause is disruptive in three ways:

- By default, `AsioFrontend::pause()` closes all connections, so in-flight requests fail.
- With `rgw_graceful_stop=true` it waits for outstanding requests with no limit, so one slow transfer can stall the reload.
- All gateways reload at the same moment, so gateways behind one load balancer pause together.

This PR builds on the crash fixes from #68920 and #69713. Defaults are unchanged.

- **rgw/beast:** add `rgw_realm_reload_pause_timeout` (default 30s, 0 = no limit).
  - When `rgw_graceful_stop=true`, the pause waits at most this long, then closes the remaining connections like the non-graceful path does.
  - The logic lives in `rgw::asio::lock_or_close_on_timeout()` so that it can be unit tested.
- **rgw:** add `rgw_realm_reload_max_delay` (default 0).
  - `RGWRealmReloader::handle_notify()` schedules the reload after a random delay in `[0, max]`.
  - A reload blocked on a bad configuration is still woken up immediately.
- **test:** unit tests for the bounded pause, and a multisite test that reads a large object slowly across a period commit with `rgw_graceful_stop=true`.
- **doc:** document `rgw_graceful_stop` and the new options in the config reference and the multisite guide, plus a `PendingReleaseNotes` entry.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81524

## Testing

- `unittest_rgw_asio_frontend_connection`: 4 tests, `--gtest_repeat=50`, all passed.
- Multisite with `test_multi.py` and vstart, 2 zones with 2 gateways each:

| Run | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `test_period_update_commit` | defaults | passed |
| `test_period_update_commit` | `rgw_graceful_stop=true`, timeout 5s | passed |
| `test_period_update_commit` | as above, plus `rgw_realm_reload_max_delay=5` | passed; reloads spread between 1.1s and 4.9s |
| `test_period_commit_graceful_inflight` | as written: graceful, timeout 60s | passed; 64 MiB read completed across the reload |
| `test_period_commit_graceful_inflight` | `rgw_graceful_stop=false` | failed as expected: `IncompleteRead` after 11 MB |
| `test_period_commit_graceful_inflight` | graceful, timeout 2s | failed as expected; gateway log below |

```
00:55:12.019 frontend waiting up to 2s for outstanding requests to complete...
00:55:14.019 frontend outstanding requests did not complete within 2s, closed remaining connections
```

72566.title: test/osd: EC harness fixes and tests for writes queued behind a rollback
72566.author: aainscow
72566.body:
Tests for https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81611 (Fast EC: writes queued behind a rollback zero-fill the parts of pages they do not overwrite), and two fixes to the EC peering test fixture that the tests need.

### Commits

- `test/osd: wire the EC peering fixture's backend listeners to the fixture`: the shard and split-child `MockPGBackendListener`s had no OSD set, so `get_tid()` returned 0 for every op and two reads in flight on one PG hit `ceph_assert(!tid_to_read_map.contains(tid))` in `ECCommon::ReadPipeline::start_read_op()`.
- `test/osd: clear the PG's object contexts on an interval change`: `MockPeeringListener::on_change()` did not clear `object_contexts` as `PrimaryLogPG::on_change()` does, so a shard that became primary again reused the object contexts of its previous term.
- `test/osd: test EC writes queued behind a rollback`: `TestECRollbackPartialWrites` in `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering`, for every optimized EC config. Each test writes an object, snapshots it, writes again, rolls back without waiting, queues partial-page writes behind the rollback, then compares every byte and deep scrubs the object.

### Results on main (b8d62f134cb)

| test | result |
|---|---|
| `QueuedBehindRollback` (object not in the extent cache) | fails, 10/10 configs |
| `QueuedBehindRollbackAndOtherRMW` (same, behind another object's RMW) | fails, 10/10 configs |
| `QueuedBehindGrowingRollback` (clone larger than the head) | fails, 10/10 configs |
| `QueuedBehindCachedRollback` (object cached, same size) | passes, 10/10 configs |

In the failing tests the bytes that the writes do not cover in their pages read back as zeros (e.g. k=2 m=1, 4K chunks: 5009 bytes in 4096..39276), and with ISA the deep scrub reports the object inconsistent. The rest of `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering`, `unittest_backend_basics`, `unittest_ec_with_crush` and `unittest_peeringstate` pass with the fixture changes.

The fix is not in this PR yet, so make check fails until it is added.

72579.title: rgw/dedup: fix dedup races with copy and delete
72579.author: benhanokh
72579.body:
Dedup modifies manifest on target object while keeping target object ref_tag and mtime intact (since logically they are the same).
This can race with Delete passing obsolete manifest to GC and Server-Side-Copy overwriting copy-target manifest.
 
 The same change was used on both cases - when preparing the operation (which includes read object MD, manifest etc) cache shared-manifest existence (boolean state). If it exits the object is part of a dedup chain already and won't be modified again by dedup so can continue like before.
 If shared-manifest state is false (the vast majority of the objects) then when removing head (DELETE) or setting new manifest (SS-Copy) add an atomic check that shared-manifest is still false (which means dedup didn't touch this object).
On failure (very rare as this is a race condition) retry operation from the top.

Dedup code was verifying TGT object state based on ref_tag and ETAG, which is probably enough today, but to be on the safe side it now also verifies mtime was not not modified.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80901

72581.title: crimson: shard-aware client op routing
72581.author: mohit84
72581.body:
Problem: A Crimson OSD runs N reactors and every PG lives on one of them. A client connection is accepted on whichever reactor `connection_distribution` picks, so an op whose PG lives elsewhere costs a cross-core hop (`submit_to`) to the PG's reactor and another for the reply. With fewer client connections than reactors
(a few heavy clients), roughly (N-1)/N of ops pay this.

Solution: A shard-aware client sends each op on a connection that the OSD accepted on the
reactor owning the op's PG, so the op is dispatched and served locally.

72582.title: test/osd: EC fixture fixes and tests for omap recovery
72582.author: aainscow
72582.body:
Tests for https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81630 (Fast EC: omap update lost on a shard recovered while the PG is only peered), and three fixes to the EC peering test fixture that the tests need.

### Commits

- `test/osd: roll the peering fixture's PG log through the PG's backend`: `MockPeeringListener::get_log_handler()` handed `PeeringState` a log handler on the `MockPGBackend`, whose `ec_get_sinfo()` has k=0, so rolling forward an entry with an EC omap update divided by zero in `Trimmer::ec_omap()`. The PG's IO backend is now used, as in `PrimaryLogPG`.
- `test/osd: name recovery temp objects in MockPGBackendListener`: `get_temp_recovery_object()` returned an empty `hobject_t`, so every recovery that needs more than one push wrote its temp object as MIN.
- `test/osd: queue only the PeeringCtx transaction in prepare_write`: `MockPeeringListener::prepare_write()` also queued transactions that the caller queues itself, so the recovery push transaction in `recover_got()` was applied twice and the second pass removed the object the first had just renamed into place.
- `test/osd: add omap helpers to PGBackendTestFixture`: `write_omap()` sets and removes omap keys in one op; `get_shard_omap_keys()` reads one shard's ObjectStore omap.
- `test/osd: test EC omap removal across shard failure and recovery`: `TestECOmapRecovery` in `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering`, for every optimized EC config with omap enabled. Keys are removed while a parity shard or the primary is down, then the shard is recovered.
- `test/osd: test EC omap recovery of the primary while the PG is peered`: the reproducer. Keys are set and removed while the primary is down; the primary comes back to a PG that can only peer (min_size raised to k+m, one more shard down), is recovered there, and the PG then goes active.
- `test/osd: roll EC omap test writes forward as an OSD does`: the fixture advances `pg_committed_to` on write commit only when `enable_log_trimming` is set, so the tests' later writes did not roll earlier entries forward; the entries were only applied when the PG activated. `TestECOmapRecovery` now sets it. The results are unchanged.

### Results on main (b8d62f134cb)

| test | result |
|---|---|
| `RemoveKeysWhileShardDownThenRecover` | passes, 10/10 configs |
| `RemoveKeysWhilePrimaryDownThenRecover` | passes, 10/10 configs |
| `SetKeysWhilePrimaryDownThenRecoverWhilePeered` | fails, 8/8 configs with m >= 2 (skipped for k=2 m=1) |

In the failing test the primary's shard ends with the old omap (keys a..e) instead of c, d, e, x, y; the other primary-capable shards are correct. The same sequence with the recovery done while the PG is active passes. The rest of `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering`, `unittest_backend_basics`, `unittest_ec_with_crush` and `unittest_peeringstate` pass with the fixture changes.

The fix is not in this PR yet, so make check fails until it is added.

72586.title: mds: keep projected_version in sync when a dirfrag goes bad
72586.author: vshankar
72586.body:
When a dirfrag object is missing or its fnode header is corrupt, CDir::go_bad() marks the (non-fatally) damaged dirfrag complete and gives it a synthetic fnode with version 1 via reset_fnode(), leaving projected_version at 0. If that dirfrag is later part of a subtree being exported, Migrator::encode_export_dir() trips

  ceph_assert(dir->get_projected_version() == dir->get_version())

This is the same issue that was fixed for unlinked dirs in commit fcdee486697 ("mds: fix crash when exporting unlinked dir"), which introduced CDir::set_fresh_fnode(), but go_bad() was not converted. Use set_fresh_fnode() there too, which also handles the REJOINUNDEF state for a dirfrag opened during rejoin.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/62381

72589.title: rgw: cast time spans to ceph::timespan before adding
72589.author: MaxKellermann
72589.body:
Adding std::chrono::seconds to a ceph::coarse_real_time yields a time_point whose `rep` is common_type<uint64_t, seconds::rep>.  With libc++, seconds::rep is `long long`, so the result's `rep` is `unsigned long long` instead of `unsigned long`, the result is no longer a ceph::coarse_real_time, and ceph's operator<<(ostream&, time_point) doesn't match.  This breaks the build with clang/libc++.

Converting the duration to ceph::timespan before adding keeps the result type unchanged.

72600.title: cephadm: authenticate crash daemons as the inventory host
72600.author: kginonredhat
72600.body:
Hosts registered by FQDN get a crash daemon id of the short hostname (`crash.node1`), while the mgr creates the cephx key as `client.crash.<fqdn>`. 72611.title: mds: drop dirty_old_rstats of purged old inodes
72611.author: xiubli
72611.body:
With `mds_snap_rstat` enabled, the MDS can segfault while propagating the rstats of a stray directory:

```
 *** Caught signal (Segmentation fault) **
 in thread mds-log-trim
 2: (MDCache::project_rstat_inode_to_frag(...)+0x32e)
 3: (CDir::assimilate_dirty_rstat_inodes(...)+0x10e)
 4: (CInode::finish_scatter_gather_update(int, ...)+0x1c2e)
 5: (Locker::scatter_writebehind(ScatterLock*)+0x467)
 6: (Locker::scatter_nudge(ScatterLock*, MDSContext*, bool)+0x567)
 7: (LogSegment::try_to_expire(...)+0xb16)
 8: (MDLog::try_expire(...)+0x66)
 9: (MDLog::trim()+0x5b5)
```

The standby that takes over crashes the same way.  It is hit by `qa/tasks/cephfs/volumes/test_clone_stats.py`, which sets `mds_snap_rstat=true`.

### Root cause

1. The stray dirs live in the global snaprealm, so once any snapshot has been taken, `cow_old_inode()` cows an old inode for them.  As the rstat of that old inode is not fully accounted, its snapid is also recorded in `dirty_old_rstats`.
2. Committing the `~mdsN` dirfrag calls `CInode::purge_stale_snap_data()` on the stray dir.  No snapshot covers the old inode, so it is purged, but its `dirty_old_rstats` entry is left behind.
3. The next nest scatter of `~mdsN` runs `project_rstat_inode_to_frag()`, which does `cur->get_old_inodes()->at(p)` for each `dirty_old_rstats` entry.  `old_inodes` is now null, so the MDS crashes.  If only some of the old inodes had been purged, `at()` would throw `std::out_of_range` instead.

### Fix

Drop the `dirty_old_rstats` entries of the old inodes that `purge_stale_snap_data()` purges.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81672

72614.title: qa/cephfs: really drop the generic kernel spec from the job yaml
72614.author: ronen-fr
72614.body:
3-kernel.yaml exists so that a run scheduled with "-k <branch>" does not
install that kernel on every node: only the kclient facets (k-testing,
k-stock) are supposed to reinstate it, for the client roles alone. It has
never actually worked.

The script empties the kernel dict, but after all postmerge scripts have
run the scheduler calls

    update_key('sha1', parsed_yaml, self.base_config)

(teuthology/suite/run.py), and update_key() recurses into every nested dict
the two have in common (teuthology/misc.py). The emptied "kernel" mapping is
still a dict, so it gets the kernel sha1 put right back. A bare sha1 is all
Teuthology's kernel task needs to fetch and install a kernel, so the job ends
up doing exactly what this fragment is meant to prevent.

Remove the whole mapping once it has been emptied, leaving update_key()
nothing to recurse into. Jobs that do want a client kernel still carry
kernel.client from k-testing/k-stock, so their dict is not empty and is kept.
Only done for a custom kernel: with "-k distro" (the default) the re-injected
"sha1: distro" is what we want on all nodes, so that case is unchanged.

72615.title: build(deps): add krb5-devel/libkrb5-dev for make check (gssapi wheel build)
72615.author: senolcolak
72615.body:
## Fixes

Building Ceph with `make check` fails during `install-deps.sh`:
the bucket notification tests bring in the Python `gssapi` package
(`gssapi>=1.8.0`) via `src/test/rgw/bucket_notification/requirements.txt`,
which `install-deps.sh` pip-installs into the `install-deps-python3`
virtualenv (`preload_wheels_for_tox`).

The `gssapi` source distribution builds a non-pure-Python wheel and
needs `krb5-config`, which is provided only by the Kerberos development
packages. When they are missing, pip fails with:

```
/bin/sh: line 1: krb5-config: command not found
subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command 'krb5-config --libs gssapi' returned non-zero exit status 127.
```

This regression was exposed by commit
[803f698200edd784e3eaab86cb18aeee05b1a5ed](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/commit/803f698200edd784e3eaab86cb18aeee05b1a5ed),
which added `gssapi` to the bucket-notification test requirements.

Related: [tracker #80240](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80240) and
[#71519](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71519), which proposed the
Debian/Ubuntu dependency. This PR retains that fix under the
`pkg.ceph.check` profile and adds the corresponding RPM dependency.

## Changes

- **ceph.spec.in**: add `BuildRequires: krb5-devel` to the `make check`
  dependencies for Fedora/RHEL/openEuler (this is picked up by
  `dnf builddep` in `install-deps.sh` when `FOR_MAKE_CHECK=1`).
- **debian/control**: add `libkrb5-dev <pkg.ceph.check>` to `Build-Depends`
  so Debian/Ubuntu `make check` builds get the same dependency.

`krb5-devel`/`libkrb5-dev` are only pulled in for `make check` builds,
matching the existing pattern used for other test-only dependencies.

## How tested

Reproduced the failure on a CentOS 9 (el9) host: `./install-deps.sh`
failed while building the `gssapi` wheel because `krb5-config` was
missing. Installing `dnf install krb5-devel` resolves it; this PR makes
the dependency declared so `install-deps.sh` installs it automatically.

72616.author: jiaweien
72616.body:
With the rgw s3vector backend, LanceDB stores the vector data in a regular S3 bucket with the same name as the vector bucket (see the "Backing Buckets" section of doc/radosgw/s3vectors.rst). When that bucket is missing - either it was never created before `CreateVectorBucket`, or it was deleted after the vector bucket was created - every vector operation that requires the backend fails with a bare 404 "NoSuchKey", identical to the response for a vector bucket that does not exist. `ListIndexes` additionally returns a misleading empty list while `GetVectorBucket` still reports the bucket as healthy.

This change maps such failures, at the operation layer, to a dedicated 404 "VectorBucketBackendNotFound" error with an actionable message, by verifying the existence of the backing bucket when an operation fails with `-ENOENT`. The plain "NoSuchKey" behavior for a vector bucket or an index that does not exist, and the empty index listing of a vector bucket without a backend, are kept unchanged.

**Before:**
```json
{"Code": "NoSuchKey", "Message": ""}
```

**After:**
```json
{"Code": "VectorBucketBackendNotFound", "Message": "backing S3 bucket 'my-vectors' does not exist; recreate it via the S3 API"}
```

(verified on a live 21.3.0 deployment; the outputs above are actual responses)

Notes:
- `ListIndexes` intentionally keeps its existing semantics (200 + empty index list for a vector bucket without a backend), so that a vector bucket without a backend can still be deleted.
- PR #72143 changed the semantics of duplicate `CreateVectorBucket` requests; this change is orthogonal: it addresses the error reporting of operations failing because the backing bucket is missing.
- Improvement to an unreleased feature; no backports apply since s3vectors has not been part of any release.

72617.title: mgr: restore mgr_util logger after time series doctests
72617.author: vshankar
72617.body:
The doctests for get_time_series_rates() and _filter_time_series() replace logger.debug on the module-level logger with a three argument lambda to print the "Duplicate timestamp" messages, but never restore it. Since doctests share the module's logger object, any test running later in the same pytest(-xdist) worker that ends up calling mgr_util.logger.debug() with a different number of arguments fails with:

  TypeError: <lambda>() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'x' and 'y'

This shows up in make check as an ordering-dependent failure in volumes/tests/test_async_job.py (via lock_timeout_log()), depending on whether the mgr_util doctests got scheduled on the same xdist worker.

Delete the instance attribute at the end of each doctest so that the Logger.debug method is used again.

72618.title: common/ceph_atomic: constrain dummy_atomic operators with std::integral
72618.author: tchaikov
72618.body:
`dummy_atomic`'s arithmetic operators were templated on a dummy TT parameter only so that enable_if could hide them when T is not integral. Use a requires-clause instead. It does the same job without the extra template parameter, and the return type is now just T.

The `!std::is_enum_v` check was redundant, as `std::integral<T>` is already false for enums. Drop it.

72620.title: cmake: select the linker with CMAKE_LINKER_TYPE
72620.author: Doracly
72620.body:
## Summary

`-DCMAKE_LINKER_TYPE=BFD|LLD|MOLD` selects the linker. It replaces `WITH_MOLD`,
which stays as a deprecated alias, and makes lld usable. Of the three, lld links
Ceph fastest and with the least CPU and memory (numbers below).

The linker is passed as `-fuse-ld`, as CMake honours `CMAKE_LINKER_TYPE` itself
only from 3.29 on.

The last two commits group the build speed-ups in the developer guide under one
section and document the option there, ahead of ccache: it needs only a package
and costs neither disk space nor memory. The grouping commit is identical to the
one in #71901, so the two PRs merge cleanly in either order.

## Fixes to the mold support from #69711

- mold drops the base-version symvers in `librados_c.cc`, so a mold-linked
  librados exported `rados_connect` and friends as `LIBRADOS_PRIVATE` and lost
  the four compat definitions; lld rejects them outright. librados now always
  links with ld.bfd where it uses symvers.
- That, not `--exclude-libs`, is what hid `rados_*` under mold, so the
  workaround that disabled `--exclude-libs` for mold is dropped.
- The `rados_*`/`_rados_*` globs added to `librados.map` made every build,
  including ld.bfd ones, export the 250 internal `_rados_*` functions behind the
  C API. The second commit removes them, restoring the previous export list.

## `--copy-dt-needed-entries` in the libcephfs and fs tests

Ten test binaries pass `-Wl,--copy-dt-needed-entries`, a workaround for
ld.bfd (tracker #70498). lld and mold reject the option, so these failed to
link with them. A configure check now passes it only where the linker accepts
it, instead of excluding Windows and macOS.

## Testing

Clang 21 + lld (with crimson) and GCC 15 + mold, Debug, on current main:

- `all` builds; every binary and library loads with all symbols resolved
  (`ldd -r`), apart from plugins that take symbols from their host
- librados exports match ld.bfd (`rados_*` versions unchanged, no `_rados_*`)
- vstart cluster: `HEALTH_OK`, rados put/get, rbd create, Python `rados`,
  `rbd`, `cephfs` and `rgw` import, `ceph-dencoder list_types`
- all `unittest_*`: 252/252 passed with both
- configure: default, `BFD`, `LLD`, `MOLD`, `WITH_MOLD=ON`, unusable linker

With mold, `ceph-dencoder` additionally needs #71814.
Not tested: CMake < 3.29, the aarch64 lld fallback for lancedb, and Windows
for the `--copy-dt-needed-entries` check (to be covered by `jenkins test windows`).

## Link performance

Clang Debug (`-O0`), idle 24-thread machine, outputs on tmpfs, the default 13
parallel links:

| linker      | 62 vstart binaries (2.5 GiB) | 336 test binaries (15.4 GiB) | CPU (tests) | peak heap (tests) |
|-------------|------------------------------|------------------------------|-------------|-------------------|
| ld.bfd 2.46 | 10.7 s                       | 50 s                         | 768 s       | 13.5 GiB          |
| lld 21.1.8  | 1.8 s                        | 11 s                         | 236 s       | 1.7 GiB           |
| mold 2.40.4 | 2.1 s                        | 24 s                         | 565 s       | 5.4 GiB           |

mold is faster only one link at a time (the vstart set in sequence: mold 5.4 s,
lld 7.0 s, ld.bfd 46 s) and is CPU-bound from four parallel links on.
lld 17 to 21 perform the same. With `-Og` objects all three link faster
(ld.bfd about 2x).

72621.title: mgr/dashboard: rgw: expose LIST and DELETE rate limits in dashboard backend API
72621.author: pujaoshahu
72621.body: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f286b44-9785-4c2d-8c2a-28a0c4dced9c Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81695 Signed-off-by: pujaoshahu Summary: The backend change lets the dashboard API save RGW's dedicated LIST and DELETE rate limits. 72642.title: squid: cephfs_mirror: fix incremental sync after directory rename
72642.author: lumir-sliva
72642.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81279

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/70757
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78910

this backport was staged manually

Both commits needed a hand resolution, the logic is unchanged:

- The fix. Main's SnapDiffSync::get_entry() was reworked by the datasync thread series (it queues files and creates remote directories itself); squid's still returns every entry to do_synchronize(). The same block goes in front of init_directory() here: stat the path in the previous snapshot, traverse in full if it is absent there, purge the remote and traverse in full if it changed type or inode. Squid already turns pic into sync_check=false, so files below such a directory are copied whole, as on main.
- The test. Squid has no setup_mount_b() and its check_peer_status_idle() does not retry, so the secondary mount is set up inline and sync_and_verify() waits 30s after each snapshot, like the other squid tests.

Besides the silent loss in #78910, the same snapdiff of a moved directory can fail outright on squid: if a subdirectory inside it was renamed or removed between the two snapshots, the client stats the old entry with a HEAD-relative path (#<dir-ino>/<old-name>), gets ENOENT, and the dir_root fails on every retry with "readdir_snapdiff error: (2) No such file or directory". This was hit on a 19.2.5 cluster. The full traversal avoids the snapdiff for such directories, so it fixes that too.

Tested on a vstart cluster built from v19.2.5, with and without the fix commit (src/tools/cephfs_mirror is the same in v19.2.5 and squid), using a standalone reproducer with the qa test's three scenarios plus a moved directory with renamed subdirectories:

| scenario | v19.2.5 | v19.2.5 + fix |
|---|---|---|
| same-parent rename (`mv dirB dirB-renamed`) | `dirB-renamed/sub/deeper/unchanged` missing on the remote | synced |
| cross-parent move (`mv d1/X d2/Y`) | `d2/Y/sub/deeper/unchanged` missing on the remote | synced |
| same-name replacement (`rm -rf replace/B; mv replace/A replace/B`) | not isolated (same run, earlier misses carry over) | synced, stale `old-only` removed |
| moved dir with renamed subdirectories, cold client cache | sync fails: `readdir_snapdiff error: (2) No such file or directory` | "is absent from the previous snapshot; using full traversal", synced |

The ported qa test also passes locally with vstart_runner.py on the same build (`Ran 1 test in 239s, OK`) and fails without the fix at the first rename step (`sync_and_verify('snap1', 2)` -> `verify_snapshot`: source and remote snapshot differ).

Squid is EOL soon, so it'd be great to squeeze this into the last squid release if there's still room. Squid users with mirrored directories that get renamed lose data on the backup without any error until then.

72643.title: mon,osd,osdc: EC stretch cluster (stretch pools with num_zones)
72643.author: aainscow
72643.body:
This PR lets a pool, replicated or erasure coded, be stretched over `num_zones` zones (CRUSH buckets, `datacenter` by default). Each zone holds a full copy of the data: `replica` copies of a replicated pool, or a whole set of k+m shards of an erasure coded pool. So the pool size is `num_zones` times the copies per zone, and `min_size` applies to each zone. In this release a pool has one or two zones, and an erasure coded pool over two zones must be FastEC (`allow_ec_optimizations`).

Stretch mode is now driven by the pools rather than by cluster-wide settings: `ceph mon enable_stretch_mode` and `disable_stretch_mode` change every pool as `ceph osd pool set <pool> num_zones` does, creating a pool over two zones enables stretch mode, and deleting the last stretched pool disables it. Individual stretch pools (`ceph osd pool stretch set`) are kept for clusters with more than two zones and behave as in Umbrella (one zone, with `min_size` counted over all their copies, including after an upgrade, except that from the upgrade commit a data center reached through two device classes counts once and a missing shard of an erasure coded pool is not counted as a data center), but cannot be combined with stretch mode.

The design is in `doc/dev/osd_internals/erasure_coding/ec_stretch_cluster.rst`, which says for each part whether it is in this release or a later one. The user documentation is in `doc/rados`.

### What changes
- **Pool fields:** `pg_pool_t` gains `num_zones` and `replica` (struct version 34). Version 34 is written only after the upgrade is committed, and only for peers with the new feature bit `OSD_STRETCH_ZONES`. A pool decoded from an older version has one zone, `replica` equal to its size and `min_size` as written: only the commit converts pools.
- **CRUSH rules:** `CrushWrapper::add_simple_stretch_rule()` chooses the zones, then the OSD failure domains in each zone, so that each zone's OSDs form a contiguous block of the acting set. Erasure code plugins build such rules from the profile, which gains `crush-zone-failure-domain`, `crush-osd-failure-domain` and `crush-num-osd-failure-domains`. LRC refuses more than one zone. There is a new command, `ceph osd crush rule create-stretch-replicated`, and `ceph osd crush rule create-erasure` takes `--num_zones`.
- **Per-zone min_size:** peering, the manager's ok-to-stop and ok-to-upgrade checks and the monitor check `min_size` for each zone of a stretch pool. The monitor no longer changes `min_size` when stretch mode enters or leaves degraded mode.
- **Pool creation:** `ceph osd pool create` takes `--num_zones`, `--replica`, `--min_size`, `--k`, `--m`, `--root`, `--zone_failure_domain`, `--osd_failure_domain` and `--class`. It builds and checks a pool's parameters in one place (`PoolCreateParams`), from the `osd_pool_default_*` options, then the erasure code profile, then the command line. An error caused by a default names its option, and pool creation through librados checks the defaults the same way. `--k` and `--m` generate a profile for the pool. An erasure code profile or CRUSH rule is removed with the last pool that uses it, except the `default` profile and the default replicated rule.
- **Pool creation defaults:** `ceph osd pool default set` and `get` set and show the defaults that pool creation uses, which are kept in the global section of the configuration database. Nothing is written unless pool creation would succeed with the new defaults. A new health check, `POOL_DEFAULT_CONFIG_OVERRIDE`, warns when a monitor's configuration overrides one of these defaults.
- **Changing a pool:** `ceph osd pool set <pool> num_zones` moves a pool between one and two zones, and `ceph osd pool set <pool> replica` changes the copies per zone of a replicated pool. Each generates or takes the new rule and updates `min_size` and the stretch peering values. A change of size drops the pool's `pg_temp` and `primary_temp`. When zones are added it also drops `pg_upmap` entries; when they are r

72645.title: RGW Posix - Escape '.' in object names
72645.author: dang
72645.body:
'.' is usually not a problem for object names, but a few specific cases can cause problems:  The single names "." and ".." can cause path problems, and we use ".<namespace>" internally to reprecent namespaces.

To avoid these issues, always escape '.' in addition to '/' for PosixDriver.

To accomplish this, add a new "path_encode()" equivalent to "url_encode()" that should safely escape everything dangerous in POSIX paths.  If anything is missed, it can be added in the future, and be automatically picked up.

72646.title: mgr/cephadm: complete filtered orch upgrades without cluster-wide gate
72646.author: kginonredhat
72646.body:
## Summary

Fixes a hang in **staggered / filtered** `ceph orch upgrade` steps (`--daemon-types`, `--services`, `--hosts`, `--limit`) where `ceph orch upgrade status` stayed `in_progress: true` indefinitely even after the filtered daemons were on the target image.

Root cause (seen in Teuthology job **614344** on `wip-rkachach-testing-2026-10-07-1110`):

1. `_do_upgrade()` still upgraded **monitoring stack** daemons (e.g. grafana) when the CLI filter was **`--daemon-types mgr`** only.
2. `_mark_upgrade_complete()` always required **all** mon/mgr/OSD/mds daemons cluster-wide before clearing upgrade state, so scoped steps never finished (`Cannot mark complete` loop).

Signed-off-by: Kobi Ginon <kginon@redhat.com>

## Failure context (Pulpito 614344)

| Item | Link |
|------|------|
| Job | https://pulpito.ceph.com/rkachach-2026-10-07_12:44:40-orch:cephadm-wip-rkachach-testing-2026-10-07-1110-distro-default-trial/614344/ |
| Teuthology log | https://qa-proxy.ceph.com/teuthology/rkachach-2026-10-07_12:44:40-orch:cephadm-wip-rkachach-testing-2026-10-07-1110-distro-default-trial/614344/teuthology.log |
| Suite fragment | `orch:cephadm/upgrade/3-upgrade/staggered` (+ agent/off, mon_election/connectivity, etc.) |
| Ceph SHA1 | `61145e16bd8357715a749b3c31b314d6f383f0b9` |
| Symptom | **dead** — `failure_reason: hit max job timeout` (~6h); stuck on first `upgrade start --daemon-types mgr` wait loop |
| Status while stuck | `progress: "2/2 daemons upgraded"`, `message: "Currently upgrading grafana daemons"`, `in_progress: true` |
| `ceph.cephadm.log` | ~24k× `Cannot mark complete` (mons/OSDs not upgraded); one `Upgrade: Updating grafana.a` at upgrade start |

## Code changes

- Add `_upgrade_filters_active()` and `_daemon_type_in_upgrade_scope()`.
- Skip `_do_upgrade` iterations (and monitoring/nvmeof redeploy helpers) for daemon types **outside** the active filter.
- For filtered upgrades, **`_mark_upgrade_complete()`** no longer blocks on cluster-wide mon/OSD/mds; **`auth_service_cipher`** is deferred until an upgrade **without** filters (full cluster upgrade).
- Use **filtered** daemons for per-type completion checks when filters are active.

## Tests

- `test_daemon_type_in_upgrade_scope_daemon_types_filter`
- `test_mark_upgrade_complete_scoped_skips_cluster_daemon_check`
- `test_mark_upgrade_complete_unscoped_requires_cluster_up_to_date`

```bash
cd src/pybind/mgr
python -m pytest cephadm/tests/test_upgrade.py::test_daemon_type_in_upgrade_scope_daemon_types_filter \
  cephadm/tests/test_upgrade.py::test_mark_upgrade_complete_scoped_skips_cluster_daemon_check \
  cephadm/tests/test_upgrade.py::test_mark_upgrade_complete_unscoped_requires_cluster_up_to_date -q
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests above pass in CI (`make check` / mgr tox as appropriate)
- [ ] Re-run `orch:cephadm/upgrade/3-upgrade/staggered` (or full matrix that included job 614344)
- [ ] Manual smoke: deploy cephadm cluster with monitoring stack → `ceph orch upgrade start … --daemon-types mgr` → `in_progress` clears when both mgrs match target; mon/OSD versions unchanged

72648.title: script: add release-eta.py, the release schedule estimator
72648.author: dvanders
72648.body:
Estimate when each active Ceph release gets its next point release and reaches end of life, from where the release actually is in the release process: tags, `<name>-release` branches, ceph.io release-notes PRs, GitHub milestones and releases.yml, plus historical lags for each stage. It moves here from ceph.io (https://github.com/ceph/ceph.io/pull/1232), which renders its output as /en/users/releases/. The data it reads is mostly this repository's, so the logic belongs next to it; ceph.io's daily workflow runs it from a ceph/ceph checkout and keeps only the generated JSON, so nothing commits to ceph/ceph.

```
src/script/release-eta.py --json out.json
```
