72650.title: tentacle: revert #72012 "osd: Set projected_size to current_size on cache invalidate."
72650.author: aainscow
72650.body:
Reverts https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72012 (tentacle backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/70377, backport tracker https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78467).

That change introduced a regression. `ECExtentCache::Object::invalidate()` now sets `projected_size` to `current_size`, so replaying a queued rollback re-adds the rolled-back data as a growth hole in `do_not_read`. Writes queued behind the rollback then skip reading that data and zero-fill the parts of pages they do not overwrite: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81611

Reverting reopens https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78465 (`ceph_assert(reads_sent)` in `do_read_op`), which needs a different fix.

72651.title: osd: serve an EC direct read only from this shard's own data
72651.author: aainscow
72651.body:
Each shard of an EC split read gets the same ro extent and works out its own data within it.
`ECBackend::extent_to_shard_extent()` got this wrong for a single-chunk extent of another shard: it gave
this shard's chunk in the same or the next stripe, so the OSD replied success with data from another
offset of the object, or with a short or empty buffer when that position is past the end of the shard's
object.

Clients without the fix for https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80836 (#72016) send such reads: an op whose
reads are each within one chunk, in chunks of different data shards, goes whole to the shard of the
first read. These are clients built from main since #66459 and the v21.0.1, v21.1.0, v21.1.1,
v21.1.2 and v21.3.0 tags.

- test/osd: `TestBackendBasics.DirectReadOfOtherShardsChunk` reads half of each chunk of a two-stripe
  object from every data shard; it fails before the next commit.
- osd: `extent_to_shard_extent()` returns only this shard's data within the extent, with zero length
  when there is none, through the new `stripe_info_t::ro_range_to_shard_range()`.
  `ECUtil.ro_range_to_shard_range` checks it against `ro_range_to_shard_extent_set()`.
- osd: `PrimaryLogPG::do_op` replies -EINVAL to an EC direct read op with a READ/SPARSE_READ extent that
  holds none of the shard's data. Such an op is a client bug: failing it shows the bug, where having
  the client resend it to the primary would hide it. Clients without the 80836 fix get -EINVAL for these
  ops rather than wrong data. Reads from fixed clients and from the split path always include the
  shard's own data, so they are not affected. `PGBackend::check_direct_read()` makes the check. The
  backend test harness's new `direct_read()` applies it as `do_op` does, and
  `TestBackendBasics.DirectReadRefusedForOtherShardsData` checks that reads of other shards' chunks,
  a zero-length read and the op of such a client get -EINVAL.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81736

Tested: full build including tests (clang, Debug, -Werror). `unittest_backend_basics`: 1048 passed;
`DirectReadOfOtherShardsChunk` fails in all 80 optimized EC configurations without the fix, and
`DirectReadRefusedForOtherShardsData` fails in all 80 if the guard replies -EAGAIN.
`unittest_ecutil`, `unittest_ecbackend`, `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering`, `unittest_ec_omap_journal`,
`unittest_ec_transaction`, `unittest_ec_with_crush`, `unittest_osd_types`, `unittest_peeringstate`,
`unittest_pglog`, `unittest_scrubber_be`, `unittest_split_ops_ut` pass. Not yet run on a cluster.

72652.title: [DNM] rgw/s3vectors: test lancedb-c#69 (C API on runtime worker threads)
72652.author: aaltshuler
72652.body:
**Do not merge.** This is the validation PR @yuvalif asked for in https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb-c/pull/69#issuecomment-5571046583: RGW built against lancedb-c#69, with the `lancedb_run_on_stack()` calls removed, so the change can be tested with a real client before #69 merges.

With lancedb-c#69, every C API call runs its async work on the lancedb-c runtime's worker threads (8 MiB stacks by default) and the caller only blocks until it completes, so RGW no longer needs to grow the coroutine stack around LanceDB calls. #69 removes `lancedb_run_on_stack()` and the `stacker` dependency.

## Changes

- `src/rgw/lancedb-c` submodule: `a4ac1c0` → `11e8072` (#69 head; it also brings in the explain-plan FFI already on lancedb-c `main`). `.gitmodules` points at the `aaltshuler/lancedb-c` fork, because `11e8072` is not on an upstream branch yet. Both revert to upstream once #69 merges.
- `src/rgw/rgw_s3vector.cc`: `create_index`, `remove_indexes`, `create_vector_bucket` and `put_vectors` call their `*_impl` functions directly.
- `src/rgw/Cargo.lock`: removes `stacker` and the three packages only it used (`psm`, `ar_archive_writer`, `object`). Generated with `cargo update --workspace`, no other changes.

## Testing

Not built locally; I'm relying on `make check` for the build and the existing unit tests. Neither `unittest_rgw_s3vector` nor `unittest_rgw_lancedb_store` calls these four operations, so the real check is the `rgw/s3vectors` teuthology suite. Could you schedule it on this branch?

One thing to watch under load: `lancedb-rgw-store` calls into SAL synchronously inside its async `ObjectStore` methods. With #69 those calls run on the runtime's worker threads (one per CPU by default), so concurrent object-store I/O from LanceDB is bounded by the worker count. RGW does not call `lancedb_runtime_configure()` here, so it gets the defaults.

72653.title: tools/bluestore: force discard when explicitly trimming free space
72653.author: YiteGu
72653.body:
The trim command in ceph-bluestore-tool calls try_discard() with async=false when iterating over free extents in the BlueStore and BlueFS allocators. This selects synchronous discard, but does not bypass the bdev_enable_discard configuration setting.

Since bdev_enable_discard defaults to false, explicitly invoking trim on a discard-capable device can iterate over all free extents without issuing any discard requests. The command nevertheless reports "trim done". This defeats the intended use case of performing an offline trim while leaving discard disabled during normal OSD operation.

Pass force=true to try_discard() in both BlueStore::trim_free_space() and BlueFS::trim_free_space(). This allows explicit trim requests for the main block device and dedicated DB/WAL devices to bypass the online discard configuration setting while retaining synchronous execution and the device discard capability checks.

The change does not modify the process configuration, persistent configuration, or the behavior of normal online discard operations. Existing handling of underlying discard errors remains unchanged.

72656.author: tchaikov

The doctests of `get_time_series_rates()` and `_filter_time_series()` set logger.debug to a three-argument lambda to print duplicate timestamps, and never restore it. pytest runs doctests and unit tests in the same xdist workers, so a later test that logs through `mgr_util` with a single argument fails in the same process. The async job tests from bd5831609f0 and 027af56aec3 do so via `lock_timeout_log()`, and fail with

72657.title: cmake: make SIMD_COMPILE_FLAGS a list
72657.author: sunyuechi
72657.body:
SIMD_COMPILE_FLAGS is a space-separated string with a leading space.
Since d6728294f26 ("cmake: use target_compile_options() for crc32 ASM
flags") it goes through target_compile_options(), which passes it as a
single argument, so on riscv64 gcc treats " -march=rv64gcv_zbc_zvbc" as
an input file and crc32c.cc fails to build.

Build it with list(APPEND), and switch gf-complete_objs from the
COMPILE_FLAGS property to target_compile_options() as well.

A CI failure on this: https://github.com/openRuyi-Project/ceph-ci/actions/runs/38427960758/job/115402270531

72658.title: .github: post the .githubmap reminder from a workflow_run
72658.author: tchaikov
72658.body:
The `.githubmap` reminder added in 5aeebc53971 fails on every pull request from a fork. For those, pull_request_review workflows get a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so createComment gets a 403 "Resource not accessible by integration". See https://github.com/ceph/ceph/actions/runs/38387487717 on #72618.

The checks and the comment now live in a new `workflow_run` workflow, `reviewer-githubmap-comment.yml`, which runs with a write token. `reviewer-githubmap.yml` just runs on the review and puts the PR number in its run name. The new workflow takes the reviewer from workflow_run.actor, and only uses that PR number if the PR's head matches the run's head commit.

The second commit stops repeat reminders. Each reminder carries a hidden per-reviewer marker, and runs for the same PR and reviewer are serialized.

I tested the script locally against the payload of the failed run above. `workflow_run` workflows only run from the default branch, so the full path can only be tested once this is merged.

72659.title: crimson/os/seastore: return from operator<< for all enum values
72659.author: tchaikov
72659.body:
GCC warns about operator<<() for write_policy_t and backend_type_t, because neither switch has a default:
```
  seastore_types.cc:1236:1: warning: control reaches end of non-void function [-Wreturn-type]
  seastore_types.cc:1297:1: warning: control reaches end of non-void function [-Wreturn-type]
```
`write_policy_t` only exists in memory, so a value outside its two enumerators would be a bug. End that printer with `std::unreachable()`.

backend_type_t is decoded from device_spec_t on disk, so a corrupted or newer superblock can hold a value we don't know. Print it as invalid, like the placement_hint_t printer does, instead of running into undefined behavior while logging it.

72660.title: rgw: include <fmt/chrono.h> for formatting std::tm
72660.author: tchaikov
72660.body:
`rgw_rest_client.cc`, `rgw_bucket_logging.cc` and `test_rgw_lc.cc` call `fmt::gmtime()` or `format a std::tm` with a spec like "{:%Y-%m-%d}", which needs `<fmt/chrono.h>`. They used to get it through common/ceph_time.h, but a76d2ca8d5c moved the fmt formatters to `ceph_time_fmt.h`, so the `rgw_common` library now fails to build:
```
  rgw_rest_client.cc:114:52: error: 'gmtime' is not a member of 'fmt'
```
Include the header where it is used.

72662.title: rgw/rgw_cksum: use std::unreachable() in combine_crc_cksum()

72665.title: os/bluestore: don't relocate misreferenced extents onto false-free blocks
72665.author: ming1
72665.body:
fsck repair relocates misreferenced extents into space from an allocator built from the freelist, before it checks the freelist against the blocks in use. With a bitmap freelist that also has false-free blocks, the relocation can pick a block another object still uses and overwrite its data; the false-free fix then allocates the same block again and the freelist toggles it back to free.

Before relocating, take every block fsck found in use out of the allocator, so the relocation only gets truly free space. The unit test injects both corruptions, repairs, and checks the victim object and a clean fsck.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81430

72666.title: osd: revert #70377 "Set projected_size to current_size on cache invalidate."
72666.author: aainscow
72666.body:
Reverts #70377 (a970eae8efa, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78465).

With that change, `ECExtentCache::Object::invalidate()` replays from `current_size`, so a rollback replayed behind another op re-adds the rolled-back data as a growth hole in `do_not_read`. Writes queued behind the rollback then skip reading that data and zero-fill the parts of their pages they do not overwrite (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81611).

The tentacle backport is reverted by #72650. Reverting on main too keeps the two branches the same, so the replacement fix backports cleanly.

The first commit disables the three tests from #70371 that were written against the reverted change (`CloneInvalidateStaleSize`, `TruncateGrowWithSuspendedReads`, `RollbackInvalidateRealistic`): without it the extent cache test fails and the two backend tests hit `ceph_assert(reads_sent)`, which aborts the rest of `unittest_backend_basics`. A follow-up PR re-enables them with the replacement fix.

The replacement fix, with a description of the whole problem, is tracked in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81754.

72668.title: crimson/os/seastore/omap: check only live log keys in the trim walk
72668.author: shraddhaag
72668.body:
## Problem Primary OSD asks for a replica's `pg_query_t::LOG` since X. While building the dup list from the replica's pglog entries older than X, the OSD aborts. It asserts as the oldest pglog entry version is less than what is expected by the OSD's pglog. And so it asserts with `ceph_assert(i->version > other.tail)`. Why is there a mismatch between what the OSD expects the pglog to be and what it really is? When a client write comes along with a trim to a replica, the OSD trims the pglog in the memory heap and requests the same from seastore. Due to a bug in seastore's `remove_kvs`, it does not mark those entries as removed on disk. A divergence is created between the in memory pglog and the one on disk. The problem only becomes noticeable when the OSD is restarted and the pglog is loaded from disk and doesn't match what the OSD expects. Initially it only results in a `log bound mismatch` log but ultimately results in an assert when the primary requests for `pg_query_t::LOG` since pglog version X.
Full RCA for https://pulpito.ceph.com/xuxuehan-2026-04-27_04:29:46-crimson-rados:thrash-wip-new-128-distro-debug-trial/179259/ There is a peering request for PG 3.a from primary OSD.0 to OSD.1 asking for `pg_query_t::LOG` since `50'0`: ``` DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,188 [shard 0:main] ms - [0x7c36b01e0840 osd.1(cluster) v2:10.20.193.125:6805/2658048002@51993 >> osd.0 v2:10.20.193.125:6802/1684756780] <== #17,14 === pg_query2(3.a 3.a query(log 50'0 ec=19/19 lis/c=49/45 les/c/f=50/46/0 sis=53 epoch_sent 53) e53/53) v1 (131) ``` In the replica OSD.1, `PeeringState::fulfill_log` is triggered to build the reply: ``` DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,365 [shard 0:main] osd - pg_epoch 53 pg[3.a( v 50'80 (46'71,50'80] local-lis/les=49/50 n=23 ec=19/19 lis/c=49/45 les/c/f=50/46/0 sis=53) [0,2,1] r=2 lpr=53 pi=[45,53)/1 (log bound mismatch, actual=[34'38,50'80]) crt=50'80 lcod 0'0 unknown NOTIFY PeeringState::fulfill_log log request from 0 DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,365 [shard 0:main] osd - pg_epoch 53 pg[3.a( v 50'80 (46'71,50'80] local-lis/les=49/50 n=23 ec=19/19 lis/c=49/45 les/c/f=50/46/0 sis=53) [0,2,1] r=2 lpr=53 pi=[45,53)/1 (log bound mismatch, actual=[34'38,50'80]) crt=50'80 lcod 0'0 unknown NOTIFY PeeringState::fulfill_log sending info+missing+log since 50'0 ``` Notice the `pg[3.a( v 50'80 (46'71,50'80]` and `(log bound mismatch, actual=[34'38,50'80])`. This means OSD.1 expects the pglog to start from beyond the tail `46'71`, but we see that the actual pglog is `[34'38,50'80]`, ie it starts way before the expected `46'71`. `PeeringState::fulfill_log` invokes `copy_after`, which is responsible for building the reply with log entries since `50'0` and dups (pg's complete dup list + pg log entries that are less than `50'0` also get added as dups). ``` DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,365 [shard 0:main] osd - copy_after v 50'0 dups.size()=0 other.dups.size()=71 ``` In the reply, the only pglog entry greater than `50'0` is `50'80`, which gets added. Then `_handle_dups` is invoked to build the dup list for reply. First, all the dups in PG 3.a get copied over. We see dups being copied from `22'1` to `46'71`: ``` DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,365 [shard 0:main] osd - _handle_dups earliest_dup_version 0 DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,365 [shard 0:main] osd - copy_up_to/copy_after copy dup version 22'1 .... DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,366 [shard 0:main] osd - copy_up_to/copy_after copy dup version 46'71 ``` Now, from the PG 3.a's pglog (which the OSD expects to start from beyond `46'71` but in reality starts from `34'38`), pglog entries before `50'0` need to be added as dups. It starts iterating from the oldest entry, `34'38`, finds it to be smaller than expected `46'71` and asserts: ``` ERROR 2026-04-27 05:58:17,366 [shard 0:main] osd - /ceph/rpmbuild/BUILD

72669.title: rgw/multisite: never distribute an uncommitted staging period
72669.author: lumir-sliva
72669.body:
A failed `period update --commit` on the master zone still notified the realm. The period at that point carries the staging id `<realm_id>:staging`, so the period pusher sent it to every other zone and they made it their current period. The real period that follows has a lower epoch and gets dropped, every later master change is refused, and in my tests both zones ended up master of their own copy (split brain).

The notify became unconditional in ab303922097 (#57640), when it moved out of `rgw::commit_period()`. Squid isn't affected.

The fix has three layers, each of which stops the leak on its own, so a zone that still leaks can't poison a zone with the fix:
- `commit_period()` in radosgw-admin notifies only after a successful commit
- `RGWPeriodPusher::handle_notify()` refuses to push a staging id
- `RGWOp_Period_Post` rejects a pushed staging id with -EINVAL

Tested on two tentacle 20.2.4 clusters (4 gateways per zone) with a genuine refusal: metadata sync stopped on zone B, master moved A -> B -> A, then promoting B without `--yes-i-really-mean-it` refused with "2 period(s) behind". Each layer was switched on alone:
- no layer: 4 staging pushes reach A 0.07 s after the refusal, HTTP 200
- full fix: nothing sent
- only the pusher check (old radosgw-admin): 4x "not pushing uncommitted staging period", 0 pushes
- only the receiver check (old sender): 32 pushes in 120 s, all HTTP 400, A keeps its period.

The receiver check protects the peer's state but not period delivery. An old pusher that leaked a staging period has recorded its realm epoch, so it drops the real period from the next commit as "not newer" and keeps retrying the staging one (backoff capped at 30 s) until its gateway restarts or a later period comes along. In a mixed-version realm the zone that runs `period update --commit` needs the new radosgw-admin or the new gateways; if a commit fails on a zone that hasn't been upgraded yet, restart that zone's gateways before retrying.

A zone that already took the staging period as current doesn't recover by itself after the upgrade: the real period with the same realm epoch is refused as a fork in the period history. In my tests `radosgw-admin realm pull --url <master>` on that zone, then `metadata sync init` and a gateway restart on both zones got it back.

Built on current main (504b1a2b334, `radosgw` and `radosgw-admin`); the lab runs were on a v20.2.4 backport of the same commit.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81760

Backport: tentacle.

72670.title: rgw/multisite: fix metadata sync of past periods
72670.author: lumir-sliva
72670.body:
Two bugs in how a secondary catches up on past periods after a master change. Both leave metadata missing on the zone while `sync status` reports it caught up.

**More than 100 entries behind on a shard** (first commit). `RGWMetaSyncShardCR::incremental_sync()` leaves a past period when `period_marker <= mdlog_marker`. But `RGWCloneMetaLogCoroutine` clones the remote shard up to its tip and moves `mdlog_marker` there, while each pass applies at most 100 entries. So on the second pass the period ends and everything after the first batch is never applied. Compare against `max_marker`, the position actually read, instead. This dates back to 574ff5f5df6 (2017).

The second commit adds `test_multi_period_incremental_sync_backlog`: the third zone is down while the master moves, 150 buckets are created whose mdlog entries all hash to the same shard, and after the master moves back the third zone must have all of them. It works with the default shard count. Without the fix it fails (3 of 3; 50 of 150 buckets missing), with it it passes (3 of 3). It takes about 8 minutes, most of it the two master changes and the checkpoints.

**More than one gateway running the sync thread** (third commit). `RGWMetaSyncCR` advances to the next period only once every shard of the past period completed in the same process. `RGWMetaSyncShardCR` returns -EBUSY for a shard this gateway doesn't hold the bid for (#45958), before the "finished syncing current period" check, and `RGWBackoffControlCR` retries that forever. So a gateway only gets out if it wins the bid on every shard, and with more than one sync gateway the secondary stays on the old period for good.

The fix:
- a gateway that loses the bid on a past-period shard, or wins it but can't take the lease because another gateway holds it while syncing that shard in a later period, reads the shard marker from rados and treats the shard as done if the owner already reached the period marker or a later realm epoch;
- the owner writes that marker when it finishes a past period, while it still holds the lease. That part is needed because a shard can finish a period without applying anything, in which case the marker tracker never writes (compare https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/55770). If the lease ran out while the last entries drained, the owner retries the period instead, and it never moves a marker that's already on a later realm epoch back;
- a gateway that takes the lease with a stale marker checks the stored one first and finishes the shard without replaying the period.

This end-of-period write is why the first commit comes first: it is based on the position actually read.

Every gateway now advances through past periods on its own, and each writes the unversioned sync info, so one that finishes a period later can store an earlier, still valid period over a later one until it catches up. It's in the commit message; happy to switch that write to a version-checked one if you'd rather. The fix only fully applies once every gateway running the sync thread in the zone has it.

Tested with `test_multi_period_incremental_sync` (3 zones, 2 gateways per zone), which reproduces the multi-gateway stall once https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80439 (#71707), https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81760 and https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81758 are fixed:
- on 504b1a2b334 with those fixes: without this PR it fails (every gateway of zones 2 and 3 stays on realm epoch 2); with only the lost-bid part, 1 of 3; with this PR, 5 of 5
- on current main (04ba07e56c8, same fixes, `rgw_rest_conn_connect_to_resolved_ips=false` to avoid https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81756): 5 of 5

An earlier version of the third commit also passed 3 of 3 failover/failback runs on two tentacle 20.2.4 clusters with 4 sync gateways per zone.

Teuthology runs one gateway per zone, so the multisite suite can't hit the second bug; the existing test does with `gateways_per_zone = 2` in the test config.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81759

72671.title: rgw/multisite: keep the period id when pulling a period from the master
72671.author: lumir-sliva
72671.body:
`RGWPeriodPuller::pull()` fetches a period the zone doesn't have yet from the metadata master and stores it. Since the configstore refactor in 976889ff3ac it first gives the pulled period a new random id and resets its epoch to 1, which looks like a copy of the "create a new period" step of a period commit. Every gateway that pulls a period stores it under its own made-up id.

The pull path runs when a zone missed a period push, for example a zone that was down while the master moved. Its metadata sync then walks the period history with that made-up id, finds no mdlog for it on the master, and stays on that realm epoch for good.

The fix stores the pulled period as it came, as `store_info()` did before the refactor. Not in squid or tentacle, so no backport.

Tested with `test_multi_period_incremental_sync`, where the third zone is down while the master moves and then pulls the latest period:
- without the fix (1 gateway per zone): fails, the third zone walks realm epoch 3 under a random id instead of the real one; with 2 gateways per zone the two gateways of that zone log two different ids for the same period
- with the fix (together with the metadata sync fixes for more than one gateway per zone in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72670): the third zone walks the real ids for epochs 2, 3 and 4, 5 of 5 runs pass

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81758

72672.title: cephadm: add systemd timer for pushing RGW bucket usage to pushgateway
72672.author: ujjawal-ibm
72672.body:
Depends-on: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/66671
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81767

## Problem:
We need a way to periodically export per-bucket/per-user RGW usage metrics to Prometheus. Currently there is no mechanism in cephadm to push these stats, so operators have no visibility into bucket-level storage consumption through their monitoring stack.

## Solution:
This PR adds support for an optional systemd timer-based cron job that pushes RGW bucket usage metrics to a Prometheus pushgateway.

### New RGWSpec fields:
- `metrics_push_enabled` -> enables the metrics push timer for the RGW service
- `metrics_push_interval` -> how often the job runs (default: 3600s, minimum: 60s)
- `metrics_push_timeout` -> max time the job can run before being killed (default: 300s, minimum: 30s)

### How it works:
1. The MGR orchestrator discovers a running pushgateway daemon and passes its URL to cephadm during RGW deployment.
2. cephadm generates a bash script (from a Jinja2 template) that executes into the RGW container, resolves the zone ID, and runs `rgw-export-bucket-usage` to push metrics.
3. A (systemd timer + oneshot service) pair is installed to run the script at the configured interval.
4. (timer, service, script) is automatically cleaned up when the RGW daemon is removed.

### Example usage:
```yaml
service_type: rgw
service_id: myrealm.myzone
spec:
  rgw_realm: myrealm
  rgw_zone: myzone
  metrics_push_enabled: true
  metrics_push_interval: 3600
  metrics_push_timeout: 300
```

## Testing:
**1.Deployed RGW with `metrics_push_enabled: true`, created 3 S3 buckets with objects, and verified the full pipeline.**

**2.Timer is active and firing on schedule.**

**3.Oneshot service runs successfully (exit code 0)**
```
$ systemctl status ceph-6318a164-c7af-11f1-988a-525400d3b5c0-metrics-push@rgw.testrealm.testzone.ceph-node-3.mntabo.service
     Active: inactive (dead) since Wed 2026-10-14 10:19:42 UTC; 1min 52s ago
TriggeredBy: ● ceph-6318a164-c7af-11f1-988a-525400d3b5c0-metrics-push@rgw.testrealm.testzone.ceph-node-3.mntabo.timer
```

**4.Status file**
```
$ cat /var/lib/ceph/6318a164-c7af-11f1-988a-525400d3b5c0/rgw.testrealm.testzone.ceph-node-3.mntabo/metrics-push.status
{"status": "ok", "ts": 1791973182}
```


**3. Pushgateway receives per-bucket metrics with correct labels**
```
$ curl -s http://localhost:9091/metrics | grep '^ceph_rgw_bucket'
ceph_rgw_bucket_usage_bytes{bucket="test-bucket-1",instance="",job="rgw-bucket-usage",owner="testuser",tenant="",zone="91d001c9-1dce-4ffa-b8c7-d8b3b47f0f24"} 62464

72673.title: osd: Preserve op ordering when requeuing into waiting_for_coro_op
72673.author: MattyWilliams22
72673.body:
## Problem

With allow_ec_optimizations enabled, ops containing CEPH_OSD_OP_CALL run in a
coroutine that yields during async backend reads. While it is in flight
(coro_op_in_flight == true), PrimaryLogPG::do_op() parks every incoming op on
waiting_for_coro_op with push_back().

That breaks ordering in the following sequence:

1. An earlier op (e.g. tid 994) is parked in obc->waiters, waiting for an
   object rw-lock.
2. A coroutine starts, and newer ops (e.g. tid 997) are queued on
   waiting_for_coro_op.
3. The rw-lock is released, and release_object_locks() calls requeue_ops().
   Op 994 is dequeued by the shard thread while coro_op_in_flight is still
   true, so do_op() push_back()s it behind 997.
4. When the coroutine completes, on_coroutine_complete() requeues
   waiting_for_coro_op, and 997 runs before 994.

The OSD then aborts on the "bad op order" assertion at PrimaryLogPG.cc:4461.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81661

## Fix

requeue_op(), requeue_ops() and requeue_object_waiters() now take an
OpWaitingList argument identifying the waiting list the op came from. The enum
lists the waiting lists in pipeline order (MAP, PEERED, FLUSH, ACTIVE, READABLE,
CORO, SCRUB, CACHE_NOT_FULL, PRIMARY_REPAIR, UNREADABLE_OBJECT,
DEGRADED_OBJECT, BLOCKED_OBJECT, OBJECT_LOCK), followed by IN_PROGRESS for ops
that were not on any waiting list.

requeue_op() checks the gates an op can hit on the way back in (waiting_for_map,
waiting_for_readable, waiting_for_coro_op). If the op's previous list is
earlier in the pipeline than the gate, the op has not yet reached that gate and
goes to the back (push_back). Otherwise it is older than anything already
parked there and goes to the front (push_front). If no gate applies, the op is
enqueued on the scheduler as before.

Other changes:

- waiting_for_coro_op and coro_op_in_flight move from PrimaryLogPG to PG, so
  PG::requeue_op() can see them. The coroutine-specific state (active_coro_op,
  coro_resumer, active_coro_ctx) stays in PrimaryLogPG.
- PG::requeue_ops() is now a plain loop that delegates to requeue_op(). The
  special-case splice into waiting_for_readable is removed, because
  requeue_op() now handles that gate.
- Call sites that requeue from waiting_for_readable now swap
  the list into a local list first. This keeps requeue_op() from treating the
  source list as a gate for its own ops.
- In on_change(), the interrupted active_coro_op is placed at the front of the
  coro list before requeueing, so it stays ahead of ops that queued behind it.
- All requeue call sites now pass an explicit OpWaitingList. There is no
  default, so a new caller has to say where its ops came from.

72674.title: ceph-crash: fix the auth name fallback and add tests for it
72674.author: tchaikov
72674.body:
Since 3a0f9ee5, ceph-crash gives up on the first auth name unless it fails with EACCES. But a name without a keyring fails with EPERM, so a host without a keyring for `client.crash.<host>` never posts its crashes. rados/singleton/all/test-crash fails this way on every run, see https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/76470.

With this change, ceph-crash tries the next name after any error, and only stops early if the command itself failed or the cluster rejected the dump. The startup ping uses the same names instead of client.admin. `--connect-timeout 5` makes a name the monitors don't know fail within 5 seconds instead of waiting for the 30s `timeout(1)`, and the name that worked last is tried first.

`post_crash()` and `scrape_path()` are now covered by unit tests, with `subprocess.Popen` mocked.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/76470

72683.title: osd/ECExtentCache: hold reads behind a cache invalidation, pin growth holes
72683.author: aainscow
72683.body:
Stacked on #72666 (the revert of #70377); only the last two commits are new to this PR. The tests are in #72684.

Fixes two defects in the Fast EC extent cache. The full description is in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81754.

**1. Reads replayed after a cache invalidation overtake the invalidating write.** An op that invalidates the cache (a clone or rollback onto the object, a remove and recreate, a shrinking truncate) waits at the head of the queue. Then `ECExtentCache::Object::invalidate()` replays the ops queued behind it on the same object and sends their reads at once. The invalidating op's sub-writes are only sent once all the cache ops of its transaction are ready, after those reads. Unless the invalidating op reads something itself, the queued writes read the object as it was before it:
- below the old size, they get the old data instead of the clone's data, or instead of the zeros a truncate or recreate leaves, and write it back silently;
- past the old size, the reads are dropped, and a write with no other reads hits `ceph_assert(reads_sent)`.

The reverted #70377 turned the assert into zero-fill (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81611). Now the reads of the replayed ops wait for `write_done()` of the invalidating op, which runs after its sub-writes are sent and sets `current_size`.

**2. A growth hole is erased by an older op's cache line** (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81315, from #72331, unchanged). The growing op now pins every line its hole spans. This matches the `ceph_assert(reads_sent)` crash reports on https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78465 (tentacle 20.2.1/20.2.2).

Both commits cherry-pick cleanly onto tentacle after #72650.

Supersedes #72331 (fix) and, with #72684, #72332 and #72566 (tests).

Results with the tests from #72684, on main with #70377 reverted (10 optimized EC configurations per peering test):

| Test | main + #72666 | + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.Rollback` | abort, `ceph_assert(reads_sent)` | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.CachedRollback` | old data, 10/10 fail | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.TruncateGrow` | old data, 10/10 fail | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.CachedRecreate` | old data, 10/10 fail | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.Recreate` | abort | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.TruncateGrowShortShard` | abort | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.UnalignedTruncate` (control) | pass 10/10 | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECRollbackPartialWrites.*` (4 tests; 3 zero-fill with #70377) | pass 10/10 | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECFailoverWithPeering.ExtentCacheGrowthHoleErasedByLineDeath` | abort | pass 10/10 |
| `ECExtentCache.HoleErasedByOlderOpLineDeath`, `HoleErasedBeforeReadDoneSendReads` | abort | pass |
| `ECExtentCache.CloneInvalidateStaleSize` | abort | pass |
| `TestBackendBasics.TruncateGrowWithSuspendedReads`, `RollbackInvalidateRealistic` | abort | pass 96/96 |

With this PR and #72684 merged into main, all of `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering` (338), `unittest_backend_basics` (888), `unittest_extent_cache` (12), `unittest_ecbackend`, `unittest_ec_with_crush`, `unittest_ec_transaction`, `unittest_ecutil`, `unittest_ec_omap_journal` and the `_l` variants pass. The new and rollback tests passed 600/600 over 5 repeats. Locally, the ctest unit tests pass (218/219: `run-cli-tests` fails only on `radosgw-admin/help.t`, as RGW was not built), as do `smoke.sh`, `safe-to-destroy.sh`, `crush_weights.sh` and `run-rbd-unit-tests-*`.

72684.author: aainscow
72684.body:
Stacked on #72683, which is stacked on #72666; only the last six commits are new to this PR. Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81754.

These are the tests for the Fast EC extent cache defects fixed in #72683. They combine the tests from #72566 and #72332, which this PR supersedes, with new tests for the remaining cases.

Commits:
- From #72566, unchanged:
  - Two EC peering fixture fixes: wire the backend listeners to the fixture so that read tids are unique, and clear the PG's object contexts on an interval change, as `PrimaryLogPG::on_change()` does.
  - `TestECRollbackPartialWrites`: partial-page writes queued behind a rollback, with every byte checked and the object scrubbed.
- From #72332, unchanged: `ECExtentCache.HoleErasedByOlderOpLineDeath` and `HoleErasedBeforeReadDoneSendReads` (`unittest_extent_cache`), and `TestECFailoverWithPeering.ExtentCacheGrowthHoleErasedByLineDeath`.

72685.title: [DNM] crimson: replication throughput work (testing/eval branch)
72685.author: Matan-B
72685.body:
edit: This PR would be splitted into separate PRs

---

This branch collects ongoing work around Crimson replicated write throughput.
It is not meant to be merged as-is.

Once the work is ready, it will be split into separate PRs by area.
Until then, this branch is used to run all fixes together and measure
their combined impact.

**The layers depend on each other.** While one bottleneck is limiting
throughput, improvements above or below it **usually won't show up in the
results**. Because of that, the work is done one layer at a time.

The numbers below were measured with the stats from #72580. Those
commits are intentionally kept out of this branch so the two don't
conflict.

Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80545

#### Approach:

1. Take the backend out of the way: run on CyanStore (cyanstore fixes included here)
2. Use stats to identify where a write spends its time (client stages,
   local commit, repop round trip, waiting for replicas) and which
   reactor is busy.
3. Use perf to understand where the CPU time is going.
4. Fix the biggest issue/bottleneck in replicated write path, rerun and repeat.

Fixes so far:
* cyanstore write path overhead
* sharding the OSD<>OSD msgr
* mclock immediate throttle
* batch acks
 
Results (3 OSDs, 4 reactors each, size 3, 4k randwrite, single runs):

So far, the CyanStore work increased throughput from about **19K IOPS to
nearly 30K** IOPS with replication enabled, while maintaining 1.71 ms
primary write latency.

More results, including SeaStore measurements, will be shared once the
branch is ready.

72686.title: osdc: send a single direct op holding primary-only ops to the primary
72686.author: aainscow
72686.body:
SplitOp sends an op whose reads all fall in one chunk whole to the shard holding that chunk, as an EC direct
read. When the op also holds ops only the primary may run (CALL, STAT, GETXATTR(S), CMPXATTR, CHECKSUM, or a
version request), its reads must be in raw shard 0's chunk, and the op goes to the OSD of shard 0 without a
check that this OSD is the primary. It may not be: when primary affinity rejects the OSDs of all the data
shards, a parity shard becomes primary while shard 0 is up and acting, and `ceph osd primary-temp` can name
any OSD. The OSD then runs the CALL on a shard that is not the primary.

- test/osdc: `TestSingleDirectOpTarget` gives an Objecter an OSDMap where primary affinity makes the parity
  shard primary. `CallGoesToPrimary` fails before the next commit: an op of a read and a CALL goes to the
  shard 0 OSD. `ReadGoesToItsShard` and `CallGoesDirectToPrimaryShardZero` check the direct reads that stay.
- osdc: `prepare_single_op()` sends an op holding primary-only ops direct only when the read's shard is the
  primary's shard; otherwise the op goes to the primary as usual. `validate()` also returns whether the op
  holds such ops.

Introduced by #66459. #72016 changes the same validation but keeps the rule; both add tests to
`test_splitop.cc`, so whichever merges second needs a rebase.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81773

Tested: full build including tests (clang, Debug, -Werror). `unittest_split_ops_ut`: 22 passed;
`CallGoesToPrimary` fails without the fix. Not run on a cluster.

this backport was staged manually

The first commit picks cleanly. The second conflicts in src/rgw/rgw_period.cc:
on tentacle RGWPeriod::update_sync_status() and read_sync_status() still live
in src/rgw/driver/rados/rgw_period.cc, so I applied the same change there
(read the status through rgw_read_local_meta_sync_status(), treat -ENOENT as an

the Conflicts: block of the commit.

On tentacle this is a regression since v20.2.2, which got 203aa43fa09 (backport of

the local config that `zone modify --master` just changed, considers itself the

segfault instead of asserting): on two 20.2.4 clusters with 4 gateways per zone
that was 16 restarts per gateway in 120 s and 502 for clients. Squid isn't
affected (it never got that change), details on the tracker.

from this PR and test_multi_period_incremental_sync:

72694.title: doc: Simplify the Assisted-by tag to match the Linux kernel
72694.author: aainscow
72694.body:
Depends on #66788

This PR is stacked on #66788 (the AI coding assistants guidance currently before the Ceph Steering Committee). Only the last commit is new.

The guidance is based on the Linux kernel's `Documentation/process/coding-assistants.rst`. Linux has since dropped the agent and model name from its attribution tag in [816d9992d9ed](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/816d9992d9ed) ("coding-assistants: simplify attribution", merged for 7.3), so the tag records only that an LLM was used. This changes the Ceph guidance to match:

```
Assisted-by: LLM [TOOL1] [TOOL2]
```

replacing `AGENT_NAME-AGENT_VERSION[:MODEL_NAME] [TOOL1] [TOOL2]`. The optional analysis-tool list and the rule against listing basic development tools are unchanged.

The model name was discussed on #66788 (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/66788#discussion_r3647807333), and the wording approved by https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79745 keeps it. As the guidance requires, this change needs its own Ceph Steering Committee motion before merge.

72695.title: test/ceph-crash: test the auth name fallback in post_crash()
72695.author: aainscow
72695.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This fix has NOT BEEN REVIEWED by a human. It is being done with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. This is why the commits have no Signed-off-by.







This adds a unit test for https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72674, which fixes https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/76470: since 3a0f9ee5099, `post_crash()` moves on to the next auth name only when `ceph` exits with `EACCES`, so a host whose `ceph.keyring` has no key for `client.crash.<host>` (EPERM, exit status 1) never tries `client.crash` or `client.admin`, and `rados/singleton/all/test-crash` fails on main. The PR includes #72674's two commits until it merges; only the last commit is new. It replaces my own fix for the same bug, which #72674 supersedes.

`src/test/test_ceph_crash.py`, run by make check, loads `ceph-crash.in` with a fake `ceph` command and checks that `post_crash()`:
- tries the next auth name after a connection error (exit status 1) or `EACCES`;
- stops once a command ran (exit status 0, even with an error message);
- reports a failure when every name fails;

and that `scrape_path()` posts the crash with the fallback.

Testing:
- Three of the five tests fail on main and all five pass with #72674.
- teuthology `rados/singleton` `all/test-crash` passed with the earlier version of the fix (same fallback), https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_14:23:06-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/.

72696.title: common/admin_socket: only wait for the hook being unregistered
72696.author: aainscow
72696.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This fix has NOT BEEN REVIEWED by a human. It is being done with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. This is why the commits have no Signed-off-by.







`AdminSocket::unregister_commands()` waits until no admin socket command is running, whatever hook the running command belongs to. If that command blocks on a lock held by the thread doing the unregister, both wait forever.

`OSD::init()` hits this (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/59079). It holds `osd_lock` while BlueStore mounts, and the mount destroys an allocator whose `SocketHook` unregisters its commands. If an admin socket `config set` arrives during the mount, `handle_conf_change()` waits for `osd_lock`, and the OSD never boots. In teuthology this shows up as `wait_for_all_osds_up` timeouts, mostly in `rados/singleton/all/recovery-preemption`, where the OSD restarts after `kill -9` with a large store to mount.

This PR replaces the global `in_hook` flag with a multiset of running hooks. `unregister_commands()` waits only while the hook it is removing is running, which is the case the wait exists for.

Testing:
- New `AdminSocketRunningHook` tests in `unittest_admin_socket`: unregistering another hook while one runs (hangs without the fix, then fails after 30 s), and unregistering the running hook still waits for it.
- The whole `unittest_admin_socket` suite passes with the fix.
- teuthology `rados/singleton` `all/recovery-preemption` on a ceph-ci batch with all of these RADOS QA fixes (`wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014`): 10/10 passed, 7 of them with the facets every recent QA failure had (`mon_election/connectivity`, `msgr-failures/few`, `msgr/async-v1only`): https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_13:56:28-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_14:46:26-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_16:18:45-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/.

> - `rados/valgrind-leaks` `2-inject-leak/none` passed: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_13:55:32-rados:valgrind-leaks-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/.







This builds on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71606, which suppresses the OpenSSL records the monitors report under valgrind (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79831). It includes that PR's commit until it merges; only the last commit is new.

Since the rocksdb 9.11 update (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/70807), `Env::Default()` is never destroyed, so the queues of its thread pools stay reachable when `ceph-mon` exits. The mons in `rados/verify` and `rados/valgrind-leaks` run with `--show-reachable=yes` and report two records:

```
operator new[] < deque::_M_push_back_aux<BGItem> < rocksdb::ThreadPoolImpl::Impl::Submit
  < DBImpl::CompactRange < RocksDBStore::compact_thread_entry
```

Teuthology reports only the first error, an OpenSSL record that https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71606 suppresses, so these stay hidden until that PR merges. This PR adds a suppression next to the other rocksdb ones.

72699.title: qa/tasks/mgr: keep the class setup config across tests
72699.author: aainscow
72699.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. It has not been reviewed by a human yet, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - On main, `test_list_enabled_module` failed in 91 of the 92 `rados/dashboard` jobs of the 46 main QA batches from 2026-07-24 to 2026-10-16.
> - teuthology with this PR: both `rados/dashboard` jobs passed all 290 tests (1 skipped), including `test_list_enabled_module`: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_15:03:51-rados:dashboard-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/. Both passed again in https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_06:56:10-rados-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v5-261015-distro-default-trial/.







`CephTestCase.tearDown()` resets the config to the epoch saved when the cluster came up. That also removes what a test class set in `setUpClass()`: the per-mgr module ports from `setup_mgrs()` (`MODULE_PORTS`) and `_assign_ports()`, and settings such as the dashboard password policy in `UserTest`. The running mgrs keep the old values, so nothing shows until they respawn and lose them.

In `rados/dashboard`, `test_list_enabled_module` enables iostat, all mgrs respawn, and each starts the dashboard on the default port 8443:
- the test keeps polling the active mgr on its old port and fails;
- the two mgrs that share a host collide on 8443 ("Port 8443 not free"), which raises MGR_MODULE_ERROR.

Both dashboard jobs fail this way in almost every main batch, filed as https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/70669, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75358 and https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/62972. Since the run stops at the first failure, about half of the dashboard API test modules had not run in teuthology for a long time. With the ports kept, one of them fails the same way: `UserTest.setUpClass()` enables the password policy, the first test's reset removes it, and after a later mgr respawn `test_validate_password_fail_name` finds the username check off.

This PR saves the config version when a class's first test starts, after `setUpClass()`, and resets only that far back after each test, so every test still starts from the state `setUpClass()` left. The class resets to the saved cluster epoch at the end, as before.

Testing:
- teuthology `rados/dashboard` with the first version of this change, which kept only the ports: `test_list_enabled_module` passed, no "Port 8443 not free", and all 285 tests ran, with one failure, `test_validate_password_fail_name`, explained above. The mgr log shows the password policy removed by the first test's `config reset` and lost at the next respawn.
- teuthology `rados/dashboard` with this version, both jobs: all 290 tests passed (1 skipped), including `test_list_enabled_module` and `test_validate_password_fail_name`: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_15:03:51-rados:dashboard-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/.

72700.author: aainscow
72700.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - The new `qa/standalone/mon-stretch/mon-stretch-command-replies.sh`, run with `CEPH_CLI_TEST_DUP_COMMAND=1` as teuthology sets it, on main of 2026-10-28 (with https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72711): without the fix, the stretch mode test and both disallowed-leader tests fail in 3 of 3 runs; with the fix, all four tests pass in 3 of 3.
> - On main, `mon/mon-stretch-mode-5-mons-8-osds.sh` failed in 15 of the 46 `all/stretch-mode-5-mons-8-osds` jobs of the main QA batches from 2026-07-24 to 2026-10-16 (one job per batch), including all 6 in October. In the first QA batch with https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72711, the same job got past `enable_stretch_mode` and failed on `disable_stretch_mode` (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82182).
> - teuthology with this PR on main of 2026-10-21: all 6 jobs passed, including `all/stretch-mode-5-mons-8-osds` with both election strategies (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-21_13:40:46-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-mon-commit-waiters-v3-261021-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-21_13:40:50-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-mon-commit-waiters-v3-261021-distro-default-trial/) and `rados/standalone` `workloads/mon-stretch`, which runs the new tests (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-21_13:41:08-rados:standalone-wip-aainscow-mon-commit-waiters-v3-261021-distro-default-trial/). All runs: https://pulpito.ceph.com/?branch=wip-aainscow-mon-commit-waiters-v3-261021.








Every monmap command that changes the elector's disallowed leaders (`enable_stretch_mode`, `disable_stretch_mode`, `add/rm disallowed_leader`, `set_new_tiebreaker`) loses its reply and runs a second time (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81930). The second run fails or reports the command's own change. The stretch mode job failed with `Error EINVAL: stretch mode is already engaged` in every main QA batch in October (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81136), and now fails with `Error EINVAL: stretch mode is already disabled` (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82182).

When a committed monmap changed the disallowed leaders, `notify_new_monmap()` started an election in the middle of `Monitor::refresh_from_paxos()`. The election restarts every service, which completes the commit's waiters with -EAGAIN; since a2230c9b0d2 (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71248) those waiters run only from `post_refresh()`, after the election. The command was then dispatched again, or resent by the peon that forwarded it, and ran against the updated monmap.

That election is not needed: every caller of `notify_new_monmap()` bootstraps afterwards, and `bootstrap()` applies the disallowed leaders again and holds the election. So `notify_new_monmap()` no longer calls an election, and its `can_change_external_state` parameter goes away. The notification stays in the refresh rather than moving to `MonmapMonitor::tick()`, because the bootstrap's election starts before the next tick and would run with the elector's old election strategy and ranks.

https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72711 (merged) makes a repeated `enable_stretch_mode` succeed, but the command still runs twice: its reply says "stretch mode is already engaged", and `disable_stretch_mode` still fails. The teuthology jobs' deliberate duplicate commands (`CEPH_CLI_TEST_DUP_COMMAND`) do not need it: when the CLI's second attempt fails, it prints a warning and still exits 0.

The backports of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71248 (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71968, https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71969) bring the regression with them unless this goes in alongside them.

72701.title: client: resend MDS commands after a remote session reset
72701.author: aainscow
72701.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. It has not been reviewed by a human yet, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - The new `unittest_client_command_reset` fails on main (the command is not resent after the session reset) and passes with the fix.
> - On main, the cephtool workunit failed in 15 of the 91 `rados/singleton-bluestore` `all/cephtool` jobs with `msgr-failures/many` in the 46 main QA batches from 2026-07-24 to 2026-10-16. With this PR and https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72702, 6 of 6 passed: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_14:23:11-rados:singleton-bluestore-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_16:18:51-rados:singleton-bluestore-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/. The hang hits about 1 job in 6, so the unit test is the stronger evidence.







`ceph tell mds.<id> ...` can wait forever. `rados/singleton-bluestore/all/cephtool` hangs until the 3 h timeout this way when it runs with injected socket failures (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/72888).

When the MDS answers the client's reconnect with RESETSESSION, the messenger discards the unacked messages, including an outstanding MCommand, and calls `ms_handle_remote_reset()`. The client aborts only one-shot commands there. The CLI's commands are not one-shot, and a client without a mount has no MDSMap, so `cancel_commands()` never runs either: `ceph_mds_command()` waits on its condition with no timeout.

This PR resends the remaining commands on that connection from `ms_handle_remote_reset()`, as MonClient, MgrClient and Objecter already do for their commands after a reset. One-shot commands are still aborted with -EPIPE.

Testing:
- New `unittest_client_command_reset` runs a `Client` against a fake MDS connection, discards what was sent as RESETSESSION does, and calls `ms_handle_remote_reset()`. Without the fix the outstanding command is not resent; with it, it is resent with the same tid and its reply completes the caller. A second test checks that one-shot commands are still aborted. The first test fails on main and both pass with the fix.
- `Client::mds_command()` needs monitors and an FSMap, so the test registers commands directly; `command_lock` and `command_table` become protected for that.
- teuthology `rados/singleton-bluestore` `all/cephtool` with `msgr-failures/many`, the facet of every recent QA failure, on a ceph-ci batch with all of these RADOS QA fixes (`wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014`), including https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72702: 6/6 passed, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_14:23:11-rados:singleton-bluestore-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_16:18:51-rados:singleton-bluestore-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/.

72704.title: osd: free the stack of a coroutine that completes without yielding
72704.author: aainscow
72704.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. It has not been reviewed by a human yet, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - The new `unittest_osd_coroutines`: `CompleteWithoutYieldFreesStack` fails when `start_coroutine()` keeps no reference (as on main), and valgrind then reports the 128 KB stack definitely lost in `create_control_block`, the same stack as the teuthology jobs. With the fix it passes with no valgrind errors.
> - teuthology: the two `rados/verify` valgrind `rados_api_tests` jobs that showed this leak on every OSD (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_13:56:33-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/) were re-run with the same seed and the fix. No OSD or monitor log of either job has a valgrind error: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_19:18:46-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v3-261014-distro-default-trial/. One job passed; the other failed only on an unrelated test race (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72744).







`PrimaryLogPG::do_op()` runs a CALL op on a pool with EC optimizations in a coroutine. `coro_resumer` owns the coroutine, and the coroutine body ends with `on_coroutine_complete()`, which resets `coro_resumer`. Since https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71327, `CoroHandles` keeps only a `weak_ptr`, so `coro_resumer` is the only strong reference. When the op completes without yielding, the reset destroys the coroutine while it is still running on its own stack. Boost then never unwinds the fiber, and its 128KB stack leaks once per such op. (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81777)

A coroutine that yields is safe: the `objects_read_sync()` completion resumes it through a locked `weak_ptr`, which keeps it alive until it returns.

`rados/verify` valgrind jobs show the leak as `Leak_DefinitelyLost`/`Leak_PossiblyLost` in `create_control_block<...push_coroutine...>` from the `do_op` lambda. Teuthology reports only the first valgrind error, and on main that is usually the monitor `CRYPTO_malloc` leak (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79831), so this one has been hidden. For example, jobs 629993 and 604377 have it on every OSD. With the monitor leak suppressed, it is the remaining failure.

This PR moves the coroutine start into `start_coroutine()` in `osd/Coroutines.h`. It holds a local reference while the coroutine runs, so a completed coroutine is destroyed after it returns, outside its own stack.

The in-body reset was introduced by 52f862cebbc (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/67079). https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71327 (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79515) fixed the use-after-free in `on_change()` but kept this reset.

Testing:
- New `unittest_osd_coroutines` counts the stacks a coroutine started by `start_coroutine()` allocates, and checks they are freed when it completes without yielding, completes after a yield, or is destroyed while suspended. Without the fix, `CompleteWithoutYieldFreesStack` fails, and valgrind reports `131,072 bytes in 1 blocks are definitely lost` in `create_control_block`, the same stack as the teuthology jobs. With the fix, the test passes and valgrind reports no errors.
- teuthology `rados/verify` `validater/valgrind` `tasks/rados_api_tests`, the same two jobs (same seed) that reported this leak in https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_13:56:33-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/, re-run with this fix: no valgrind errors in any OSD or monitor log of either job (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_19:18:46-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v3-261014-distro-default-trial/). One job passed; the other failed only on `LibRadosPoolIsInSelfmanagedSnapsMode.FreshInstance` (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/64056), where a fresh client read the osdmap from a monitor one epoch behind the pool deletion.

72706.title: os/bluestore: fix NaN and underflow in allocator fragmentation metrics
72706.author: trukhinyuri
72706.body:
Return a zero fragmentation score when allocation leaves exactly one free block, and keep the Btree2 range-tree fragmentation estimate in bounds when free space resides only in the extent cache.

This PR contains two commits:

- `81ed0d0071`: handle the single-block case in `Allocator::get_fragmentation_score()`. With one free allocation block, `ideal` equals `terrible`, so the original formula returns `NaN`. Add a regression that allocates all but one block through the real allocator API.
- `e3436e5a61`: guard the range count before subtraction in `Btree2Allocator::_get_fragmentation()`. Add a `hybrid_btree2` regression that allocates the whole device, releases two nonadjacent blocks through the extent cache, checks the metric bounds, and allocates those blocks again. Before the guard, this sequence returns a fragmentation value of `-1`.

The cache guard bounds the existing range-tree estimate. A cache-aware fragmentation calculation is outside this change.

The empty-allocator crash tracked in [#70908](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/70908) was already fixed by [#70528](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/70528).

## Validation

Built and ran the real `unittest_alloc` target on Linux arm64 against base `d8552606423c86efe4df2d39c0b7e4b20ba69c73` and the proposed changes:

- Single-block regression: fails on all six allocator variants before the guard; passes on all six with it.
- Cache-only regression: fails for `hybrid_btree2` before the guard; passes with it. The five other allocator variants are skipped for this cache-specific test.
- Full allocator suite with both changes: **262 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failures (276 cases)**.

```sh
cmake --build build --target unittest_alloc -j1
build/bin/unittest_alloc
```

Problem:
Enabling stretch mode updates the monmap and can trigger an election
before the client gets a reply. When the command is replayed after the
election, stretch mode is already enabled and we return EINVAL even
though the original command succeeded.

Solution:
Return success if stretch mode is already enabled without changing the
existing configuration. If enablement is still pending, wait for the
commit and retry instead of returning success on uncommitted state.

Add regression coverage in both the standalone stretch test and the
five-monitor workunit used by
rados/singleton/all/stretch-mode-5-mons-8-osds. Repeat the enable command
and verify that it succeeds without changing the monmap.

Also remove obsolete CRUSH rule min_size/max_size fields and enable the
pool application in the standalone test to avoid unrelated health warnings.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81136
Signed-off-by: Kamoltat (Junior) Sirivadhna <ksirivad@redhat.com>

72712.title: rgw: avoid no-op dynamic reshard reduction and scale versioned limit_check
72712.author: trukhinyuri
72712.body:
In `RGWBucketReshard::calculate_preferred_shards`, `calculated_num_shards == current_num_shards` was checked before rounding up to `nearest_prime(calculated_num_shards)` and before clamping to `min_layout_shards`. In addition, the reduction condition only checked `current_num_shards > min_dynamic_shards` rather than `current_num_shards > std::max(min_dynamic_shards, min_layout_shards)`. When a bucket was already at `min_layout_shards` (or when `nearest_prime` rounded `calculated_num_shards` back to `current_num_shards`), `calculate_preferred_shards` set `need_resharding = true` with `*suggested_num_shards == current_num_shards`. Because `RGWReshard::process_entry` only dropped reduction requests when `suggested_shard_count > current_shard_count` instead of `>=`, RGW could execute a no-op reshard to the same shard count.

Also scale `safe_max_objs_per_shard` by one third for versioned buckets in `RGWBucketAdminOp::limit_check` (`radosgw-admin bucket limit check`) to match `RGWRados::calculate_preferred_shards`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/55546
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/69464

72713.title: mon: retry pings to dead peers after reconnect
72713.author: kamoltat
72713.body:
Problem:
A full messenger session reset can drop the last queued monitor ping.
Once the peer is marked dead, dead_ping only updates its connection
score without sending another ping.

This leaves the peers waiting on each other and can keep MON_NETSPLIT
active even after all monitors reconnect and rejoin quorum. This happened
during the monitor restarts in rados/singleton/all/mon-stretch-pool.

Solution:
Send another ping on each dead_ping interval so the peers can resume
pinging after reconnecting. Keep the peer marked dead until we hear from
it, and stop probing if its rank is no longer valid in the monmap.

Add unit tests for repeated dead-peer probes, keeping the peer marked
dead without a response, and stopping probes for invalid peer ranks.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79814
Signed-off-by: Kamoltat (Junior) Sirivadhna <ksirivad@redhat.com>

72714.title: DNM: rgw/datum: add independent data facilities
72714.author: chardan
72714.body:
Datum gives Ceph a shared vocabulary for describing and manipulating data independently of where it is stored.

Its purpose is to reduce duplicated infrastructure across Ceph components while keeping storage behavior and application policy in their appropriate domains. The library targets recurring machinery, especially in RGW: key construction and range selection, record projection, fragmented-buffer handling, serialization, pagination, and diagnostic formatting.

A bucket listing or metadata scan can use the same vocabulary from selecting keys through processing records to retaining a continuation and reporting results, replacing separate helpers for each stage. Borrowed views avoid unnecessary copies; explicit ownership identifies what must survive the current operation; compile-time checks and work, storage, and output budgets make contracts easier to enforce.

Datum supplies these mechanics while allowing consumers to retain control of transactions, I/O, authorization, and storage semantics. The benefit is less bespoke glue and more consistent behavior across consumers.

Ceph integration is opt-in through `WITH_DATUM`. This PR introduces the library without migrating existing consumers.

Documentation: [Datum tutorial and design (PR preview)](https://ceph--72714.org.readthedocs.build/en/72714/dev/radosgw/datum/). Eighteen provisional lessons include runnable examples, expected output, figures, an index, and source downloads; the native RGW integration preview is identified separately.

Validation: two Catch2 suites pass 116 test cases and 273,702 assertions, including optional RapidCheck property tests. Codec-disabled tests and 18 architecture examples also pass. Benchmarks and historical performance studies are preserved outside the branch and build system.

Note: This is C++26. The reason for that choice is that the library benefits heavily from reflection and-- importantly-- I wanted to be sure choices were made with C++26 support strongly in mind. I would really prefer that we can get it into Ceph as C++26, but can back-migrate this to C++23 if needed. 

Assisted-by: Codex:GPT-6

Signed-off-by: Jesse F. Williamson <jfw@ibm.com>

72715.title: tools/cephfs_mirror: close directories by kind in finish_crawl
72715.author: lumir-sliva
72715.body:
SnapDiffSync::finish_crawl() closes every directory left on the sync stack with ceph_close_snapdiff(). Directories that are traversed in full instead of diffed (new, moved-in or replaced directories, purged or itype-changed subtrees) are opened with opendirat() and have no snapdiff handle, so closing their uninitialized ceph_snapdiff_info segfaults the daemon.

finish_crawl() runs whenever the crawl stops early, so any of these crashes cephfs-mirror while such a directory is on the stack:
- a sync error, e.g. a remote mkdir failing with EDQUOT. The daemon restarts and retries the same snapshot, so a persistent error turns into a crash loop
- stopping or restarting cephfs-mirror (SIGTERM)
- `ceph fs snapshot mirror remove` of the directory
- the mirror client getting blocklisted (same branch, not tested)

The fix closes the leftover entries with fini_directory(), which already picks ceph_closedir() or ceph_close_snapdiff() per entry when a directory is finished normally.

The qa test replaces a synced directory under the same name, so the next sync walks it in full, and makes its remote mkdir fail with a file quota. Without the fix the daemon dies at the failed mkdir and the test times out waiting for the sync failure; with it the sync fails, the daemon stays up, and the snapshot syncs once the quota is lifted. The SIGTERM and mirror-remove routes aren't covered by the test, there's a vstart reproducer for all three on the tracker.

squid and tentacle have the same loop in finish_sync(), so the backports need a small hand adjustment there.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81573

72716.title: tools/cephfs_mirror: resume a failed sync only from its base snapshot
72716.author: lumir-sliva
72716.body:
Depends on #72715, its two commits are in here because the new tests need that fix. Only the last two commits are new.

cephfs-mirror stores the snapshot it's about to sync in ceph.mirror.dirty_snap_id on the remote dir_root. When that id equals the snapshot being synced, an earlier attempt didn't finish, and the daemon resumes it with a snapdiff from the newest remote snapshot (prev). That only works if the earlier attempt diffed from the same prev. If the base gets deleted between attempts and the deletion is mirrored, prev moves back to an older snapshot while the remote tree still reflects the deleted one. Entries that only existed in the deleted snapshot are in neither side of the new diff, so they stay on the remote, in the remote snapshot and in every later one, and the sync is reported as successful.

The value is now written as "<current>:<base>" (base 0 for a remote scan), and an interrupted attempt is only resumed with a snapdiff when its base is still prev. Anything else falls back to a remote scan, same as any other mismatch. Side effect: a remote scan that fails is redone as a remote scan instead of being continued as a diff from prev.

Mixed versions:
- older daemons parse the value with atoll() and read the leading id, so they behave exactly as before
- a bare id from an older daemon still matches prev, so idle directories keep syncing incrementally after an upgrade
- a directory whose sync was interrupted by the upgrade has no recorded base and syncs its current snapshot once with a remote scan
- the MDS already allow-lists the xattr without validating the value, so no MDS change is needed

I checked both directions on vstart by swapping the daemon binary between failed attempts, steps and results are on the tracker.

Two qa tests make every attempt at a snapshot fail before it reaches the entries it removes, delete the base, then let the sync finish: once with the daemon mirroring the deletion itself, once with the base already gone on both sides. Both fail on main (the removed entries stay on the remote) and pass with the fix.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81572

72717.title: mgr/prometheus: iterate over a copy of the rbd_stats pool ids
72717.author: anthonyeleven
72717.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81782

`get_rbd_stats` deletes stale entries from `self.rbd_stats['pools']` while iterating over its keys. When a tracked pool is dropped from `rbd_stats_pools`, is deleted, or loses its rbd application, the next loop step raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`, and that metrics collection fails.

This iterates over a list of the keys instead, as the code a few lines below already does for `pool_ids`.

72718.title: mon,osd: send the HIGH_DEBUG_LEVEL metric only while a level is high
72718.author: lumir-sliva
72718.body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #68442. The OSD, crimson OSD and monitor attach a `HIGH_DEBUG_LEVEL` health metric to every report they send to the mgr, with a count of 0 when nothing is elevated and even when the guard is disabled (the default). This PR only attaches it when at least one subsystem is at or above `high_debug_level_threshold`.

## Problem
A mgr that predates the metric doesn't have a collector for it, so `DaemonHealthMetricCollector::create()` returns nothing and `DaemonServer::send_report()` logs

    mgr.x sent me an unknown health metric: 3

for every report from every daemon that sends it. During a rolling upgrade (mons first, then mgrs) that is one error line per upgraded daemon every few seconds until the mgr itself is upgraded, for a feature nobody turned on. It also matters for the tentacle/umbrella backports of #68442, where a point-release upgrade would hit this on every cluster.

## Fix
Wrap the `emplace_back` in `if (count > 0)` in `OSD::get_health_metrics()`, `Monitor::get_health_metrics()` and the crimson `OSD::get_health_metrics()`.

An absent metric reads the same as a zero one for the new mgr:
- `DaemonServer` replaces a daemon's `daemon_health_metrics` wholesale on each report (`DaemonServer.cc:872`), and `send_report()` rebuilds the checks from scratch each time.
- `HighDebugLevel::_update()` already ignores entries with a count of 0.

So the warning still raises while a level is high and clears once it drops, the threshold is removed or the level is reverted. With the guard on and a level actually elevated, an old mgr still logs it, which is expected.

One visible side effect: `ceph_daemon_health_metrics{type="HIGH_DEBUG_LEVEL"}` from mgr/prometheus is now absent at idle instead of 0. Nothing in `monitoring/` or the tests reads it, and since #68442 hasn't shipped in a release yet, nobody can depend on the 0 series.

## Test
3-OSD vstart (MON=1, MGR=1, OSD=3), `debug_mgr 10`, counting `handle_report daemon_health_metrics` lines in the mgr log:

    before, idle, threshold 0:     37/38 lines carry HIGH_DEBUG_LEVEL(0|(0,0))
    after,  idle, threshold 0:      0/28
    after,  threshold 10:          12/13, HEALTH_WARN HIGH_DEBUG_LEVEL
    after,  config rm threshold:    0/8,  HEALTH_OK within 10s

`qa/workunits/mon/debug_level_guard.sh` passes (warning raised, auto-revert, warning cleared, warn-only, disabled) and `unittest_debug_level_guard` 9/9. The crimson hunk wasn't built locally, it's the same one-line change as the classic OSD.

No new test: the change is in what goes over the wire, and `ceph health` looks the same before and after. There is no seam to unit test `get_health_metrics()` without a running daemon.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75467

72719.title: mgr: add an osd_map_pools getter for rbd_support
72719.author: anthonyeleven
72719.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81783

The mirror snapshot and trash purge schedule handlers in rbd_support each call `get_rbd_pools` once a minute, even when no schedules exist. `get_rbd_pools` fetches `osd_map` only to read pool ids, names and applications.

Dumping `osd_map` holds the GIL while it converts every OSD and every `pg_upmap_items` entry to Python objects. It also computes a read balance score for each replicated pool, and each score copies the OSDMap and maps every PG of the pool. On a Reef cluster with 10,130 `pg_upmap_items` entries, Python module commands stalled for about 6 seconds every 66 seconds.

This adds an `osd_map_pools` getter that dumps the pools section of `osd_map` in the same format, without the read balance scores, and uses it in `get_rbd_pools` and `TaskHandler.resolve_pool_name`. Other modules that only need pools, such as the prometheus module's `get_rbd_stats`, could use it too.

The new key is not added to the mgr API cache, since dumping only the pools is cheap.

72720.title: mgr/MgrClient: send keepalives on the mgr session
72720.author: anthonyeleven
72720.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81784

The mgr sends nothing back on a daemon's lossy mgr session, and `AsyncConnection`'s idle check counts only received traffic. So every OSD and MDS faults its mgr session once it has been open for `ms_connection_idle_timeout`, even though it reports every `mgr_stats_period` seconds. It then reconnects, authenticates again and declares all of its perf counters again. Daemons that connected together after a mgr failover stay in step, so they all reconnect to the mgr at the same moment.

MonClient avoids this by sending keepalives. After a report, `MgrClient` now sends one if half of the daemon's own `ms_connection_idle_timeout` has passed since the last, so the ack arrives well before the timeout. With the default 900 s timeout that is one keepalive every 450 s, not one per report. The mgr's messenger answers the keepalive itself, so nothing new reaches the mgr's dispatch path.

An earlier revision sent the keepalive from the mgr, so that daemons of any release would be fixed once the mgrs were upgraded. It is back in `MgrClient` because the daemon's idle timer is what closes the session, and only the daemon knows that timer's setting.

72723.title: qa: test lock requests interrupted after the MDS grants them
72723.author: vshankar
72723.body:
(This PR doesn't include the user-space driver fix yet -- raised it to link it in the kernel driver fix as a reproducer link)

A blocked fcntl/flock request can be interrupted after the MDS has granted the lock but before the client has seen the grant. The MDS keeps the lock, since an interrupt request only cancels a waiting lock. If the client discards the grant, the lock is orphaned on the MDS: the process that asked for it is gone and nothing unlocks it until the client releases its caps on the inode.

The test runs the lock holder and the waiter on the same mount so the holder's unlock and the waiter's interrupt queue up in order on one MDS session while the MDS is stopped. On resume, the unlock grants the lock to the waiter before the interrupt is processed. Another client then checks that the lock is free.

This reproducer is based on @deshpandevaishnavi20 reproducer report.

Reproduces: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81698
Assisted-by: Gemini
