72977.title: osdc, osd, mon: fix split and replica reads for pools in a pool migration
72977.author: aainscow
72977.body:
Stacked on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/69112 (pool migration, at 566b09e1de6): only the last ten commits are new.

Reads that do not go to the primary of a pool in a migration can return wrong or stale data:

- `SplitOp::create()` plans a split or direct read on the pool the op is addressed to (`base_oloc`), but
  `_calc_target()` then routes an op on a migrating pool to the other pool of the migration. An op on the
  target, which takes the pool's name, goes back to the source for PGs that have not migrated. An op on the
  source's id goes to the target for PGs that have migrated, and for every PG once the migration has
  finished. When the two pools have different layouts, the read returns wrong data or aborts the client.
  The fix: plan the read for the pool `_calc_target()` routes it to, with that pool's layout.
- A source OSD redirects a direct read of a migrated object, and the Objecter resent it to the same shard;
  a second redirect failed `ceph_assert(found)`. The fix: such a read takes the `-EAGAIN` path of a direct
  read whose PG changes, and is redriven to the primary.
- An OSD of a source PG treats an object as migrated once it applies the object's delete, and the primary
  starts redirecting clients at once. A client can then write the object in the target while a replica
  whose delete has not arrived serves the old copy to balanced and localized reads, and to split reads
  that do not ask for the version. The fix: the primary redirects only once the delete has committed on
  every shard, and holds ops on the object until then; a replica or shard bounces a read of a migrated
  object to the primary with `-EAGAIN`. Because of this, reads routed to the source can be split too.

And `prepare_new_pool()` applies `--enable_ec_optimizations` after choosing the stripe unit and deciding on
split reads, so a pool created or migrated with it gets the 4K stripe unit of an unoptimized pool and no
`split_reads` flag. The fix: apply it before those decisions, as `osd_pool_default_flag_ec_optimizations` is.

The first version of this PR sent every read of a migrating pool to the primary. This version keeps split
and direct reads during a migration.

Tests: unit tests for the SplitOp planning and the redirect, a standalone test that reads each object from a
delayed replica as soon as it is written in the target (`qa/standalone/osd/osd-pool-migration-replica-read.sh`),
and a thrash-erasure-code workload in which `ceph_test_rados` reads with `balance_reads` while its pool
migrates between EC k=2 m=1 and k=4 m=2 (`ceph_test_rados --migration-erasure-code-profile`, rados task
`migration_erasure_code_profile`; it runs with the pool-migration facet enabled).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81981

Tested: full build including tests (gcc, Debug) and the unit-test suite (211 of 211 pass); clang 19 finds
nothing new in the changed code. The 6 new or changed tests in `unittest_split_ops_ut` fail without the SplitOp and
Objecter fixes. `osd-pool-migration-replica-read.sh` fails on #69112 (5 of 8 objects read stale) and passes with
the fix, and the mon-only `TEST_enable_ec_optimizations` passes. On a cluster, with one source OSD's messages from
other OSDs delayed by `ms_inject_delay_*` (up to 8 s) and a client writing each object as soon as the primary
logged its delete: no stale reads in about 777,000 localized, balanced and versionless EC split reads. An EC k=2 m=1 pool migrating to k=4 m=2, read by 8 clients by name and by the source's id: 292,800 reads all
correct, 194,400 of them split or direct, in unmigrated, migrating and migrated PGs (the run stopped at 87%
migrated; a unit test covers reads by the source's id after completion).

72978.title: crimson/os/seastore/omap: consistent naming across LogManager and in memory pglog

72981.title: mgr: limit in-flight commands per module with EAGAIN
72981.author: NitzanMordhai
72981.body:
Picks up #60194 (closed as stale), reworked per the review there and the tracker discussion.

  Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/62712

  ## Problem
  A module's queued commands keep their client message throttle slot (`mgr_client_messages`) until they reply. If a module is stuck (e.g. volumes blocked on an MDS), its backlog fills the throttle and the mgr stops reading
  commands from all clients, including other modules and native mgr commands (`pg dump`, `osd perf`).
 
  ## Change
  - New per-module option `mgr/<module>/max_command_queue_length`, default 0 (off).
  - `DaemonServer` counts commands queued or running per module and replies `-EAGAIN` instead of queueing once the limit is reached.
  - The limit is read in C++ on each command, so `ceph config set` takes effect even while the module's thread is stuck.
  - New perf counters in `mgr_module_<name>`: `cmd_in_flight` and `cmd_eagain` (exported by ceph-exporter).

  ## Review points from #60194
  | Comment | Now |
  |---|---| 
  | One global counter/limit shared by all modules (@tchaikov) | Counter lives on each `ActivePyModule`, limit is per module option |
  | No MgrMap/mon command, use a module option (@batrick) | Option registered in `mgr_module.py`, no mon change |
  | Thread safety (@batrick) | Atomic counter; admission already serialized by `DaemonServer::lock` |
  | Count in `Finisher` / use finisher queue length (@batrick, @kotreshhr) | The module finisher also runs `notify`/`config_notify`, so its length would reject commands on a healthy but busy module. Commands only are counted |
  | Add counts to perf dump (@batrick) | `cmd_in_flight`, `cmd_eagain` |
  | Python setter via `_config_notify` | Removed: it runs on the module's own thread, so it can't apply a new limit while the module is stuck |
  | Counter can leak on error paths | Decremented by a guard captured in the queued context; verified on success, module error, handler exception and failed-module (`EIO`) paths |
  | Per module for other users, e.g. audit logging (@dparmar18) | Any module can opt in, or declare its own default in `MODULE_OPTIONS` |
  | Sensible default? (@vshankar) | 0 here, see below |

  ## Testing 
  vstart, `mgr_client_messages=16`, 20 concurrent commands to a stuck module (rc 124 = killed after 10s):

  | | limit 0 (today) | limit 4 |
  |---|---|---|
  | selftest blocked by a 30s `eval` sleep: `balancer status` / `pg dump` / `osd perf` | hang (124) | 0.4s |
  | volumes with MDS frozen (`kill -STOP`), `fs subvolume create`: same probes | hang (124) | 0.5s |
  | stuck module `cmd_in_flight` | 16 (whole throttle) | 4, rest get `EAGAIN` |
 
  New qa test: `tasks.mgr.test_module_selftest.TestModuleSelftest.test_command_queue_limit`.

72988.title: qa/tasks/mgr/dashboard: write non-zero data in test_copy
72988.author: djgalloway
72988.body:
`tasks.mgr.dashboard.test_rbd.RbdTest.test_copy` fails intermittently in the dashboard API tests ([tracker #68544](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68544), open since 2024-10; most recently on [ceph-pr-pipeline 5952](https://jenkins.ceph.com/job/ceph-pr-pipeline/5952/)) with:

```
  File "/ceph/qa/tasks/mgr/dashboard/test_rbd.py", line 791, in test_copy
    self._validate_image(img_copy, ... disk_usage=img['disk_usage'])
AssertionError: 0 != 67108864
```

**Cause:** the test fills the source image with `rbd bench --io-type write --io-total 5M`, and rbd bench's default `--pattern-byte rand` fills its single write buffer with one byte, `memset(bp.c_str(), rand() & 0xff, io_size)` (`src/tools/rbd/action/Bench.cc`, seeded from `time()`). So in about 1 run of 256 every byte written is `0x00`. The source still accounts the written objects (64 MiB), but librbd's copy skips all-zero extents (`if (m_bl->is_zero()) ... return;` in `src/librbd/internal.cc`), so the copy is correctly sparse and reports `disk_usage` 0.

This is not a timing race, so waiting for the copy's usage to converge (#68904, auto-closed unreviewed) would only turn the failure into a `TestTimeoutError` 30 s later.

**Fix:** `--pattern-byte 1`, so the data is never all zeros. The other `rbd bench` calls in `test_rbd.py` (`test_disk_usage`, the rollback test) only check the image they wrote to, which accounts zero-filled writes too, so they're unaffected.

**Backports:** `--pattern-byte` (13a59272967) is on tentacle and umbrella, so this applies there as-is. squid doesn't have it and has the same 1-in-256 behaviour, so a squid backport would need another way to write non-zero data.

72993.title: rgw/rados: fix DeleteObjectTagging resetting object mtime to epoch
72993.author: mheler
72993.body:
set_obj_attrs() increments the object mtime by 1 ns so multisite can detect the change. However, it takes the starting mtime from the RadosObject. DeleteObjectTagging does not read the object first, so that mtime is zero. As a result, the update sets the mtime to 1970 on both the head object and its bucket index entry.

This regressed in f5f6194c07b40c50913e956e06aaa3709d4d53aa , Main and Tentacle stopped exhibiting the issue for DeleteObjectTagging after 94016c7786f29f3061a181c132abd4069337f5c9 which began reading the object first. The D4N and NFS setattr/xattr paths are still affected on all branches.

set_attrs() already reads the head object, so increment its actual mtime by 1 ns there. This preserves the multisite change notification without resetting the mtime to 1970.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81980

72995.title: mgr/PyOSDMap: efficient implementation in OSDMap.get_pools / get_pool…
72995.author: Harshit-AI3018
72995.body:
Previously, `OSDMap.get_pools()`, `get_pools_by_name()`, `get_ec_profile()`, and `get_require_osd_release()` called `self._dump()`. This triggered a full OSDMap dump through `PyFormatter` that serialized all OSD records, PG temps, xinfo, and CRUSH state before discarding everything except pool/profile data.

On large clusters with hundreds or thousands of OSDs, this caused high latency, memory churn, and GIL contention during periodic ticks of `pg_autoscaler`, `balancer`, and `dashboard`.

This PR introduces targeted C-level accessors in `BasePyOSDMap`:
- `_dump_pools()`: Serializes only pool records using `OSDMap::dump_pool()`, avoiding full cluster state serialization while keeping 100% schema compatibility.
- `_get_ec_profile()`: Fetches a single erasure code profile dictionary directly by name.
- `_get_require_osd_release()`: Directly retrieves the release string.

In addition, `OSDMap.get_pools()` and `get_pools_by_name()` now lazily cache the resulting pool dictionaries per `OSDMap` instance. Because an `OSDMap` instance represents an immutable epoch snapshot, repeated accesses within the same epoch are $O(1)$ operations that avoid crossing the C++/Python boundary.

Fallback to `_dump()` is preserved to maintain compatibility with test harnesses and mocks.

73007.title: blk/kernel: collect the wakeup read in _aio_stop() on FreeBSD
73007.author: wjwithagen
73007.body:
Depends on #71449; only the last commit (blk/kernel: collect the wakeup read in _aio_stop()) is new, the first two belong to #71449.

_aio_stop() submits a 4096 byte read to wake the aio thread and then joins it.  The thread leaves its loop as soon as it sees aio_stop, so it can exit before it has collected that read.

FreeBSD keeps a finished aio job until aio_return() is called for it and finds it by the address of its aiocb.  The leftover job stays in the kernel after wakeup_ctx, and with it the aio_t, has been freed. he next aio_t allocated at that address gets the result of the leftover job (4096) instead of its own, and its own result is handed to the request after that.  This shows up as the abort in _aio_thread(): "unexpected aio return value: does not match length".

Wait for the wakeup read to finish (bounded to 10 seconds) and aio_return() it before the aio_t is released.  Only the HAVE_POSIXAIO path changes; libaio is not affected.

Follow-up to #71449.

Signed-off-by: Willem Jan Withagen <wjw@digiware.nl>

73008.title: mgr/dashboard: order CRUSH map viewer like `ceph osd tree`
73008.author: vobruba-martin
73008.body:
The CRUSH map viewer sorted bucket children with Array.prototype.sort() as strings. With 10 or more OSDs per host this shows osd.10 before osd.2 and buckets are ordered by the string form of their negative ids, so the tree looks random.

The `nodes` list returned by the backend is already in the same order as `ceph osd tree`: buckets by name before devices, devices by device class and then numerically by id. The `children` lists in it are reversed, so order the children by their position in `nodes` instead of re-sorting them on the client.

The roots from crush.find_roots() are already ordered by id like the CLI. Keep that order (the viewer used to reverse it) and only skip the shadow roots, which are not part of `nodes`.

Also stop mutating the API response.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68752

73018.title: os/bluestore: weight buffer cache shard limits by occupancy
73018.author: ming1
73018.body:
Buffer cache shards get equal limits, but PGs map to shards by
`pg seed % N` and load them unevenly (1.3x to 1.6x the average on the
busiest shard). Loaded shards trim on every insert, light shards never
fill, and the data cache stops at ~70% of what PriorityCache committed,
so a hot set that fits the budget still reads from disk.

Give each shard 1/8 of its even share as a floor and split the rest by
what it holds; the limits still sum to the committed size, and an
evenly loaded OSD keeps today's split.

4-OSD vstart, `osd_memory_target` 2 GiB, 4K random reads of a 3 GiB hot
set: 5,643 -> 106,712 IOPS, hit rate 76% -> 100%, disk reads 77-253 MiB
per OSD -> 0; 4M sequential reads 19 MiB/s -> 6 GiB/s; writes unchanged.

Reported by Dan van der Ster in #72884 (reads through the page cache).
With this fix BlueStore's cache serves the same hot set at 106,712 IOPS
against 96,196 through the page cache, with a 4 us hit instead of 18 us.

Onode shards keep the even split (their count includes pinned onodes).

73021.title: msg/async/rdma: demote to_dead beacon error log to debug
73021.author: taaahaaa
73021.body:
When tearing down RDMA QueuePairs, `Infiniband::QueuePair::to_dead()` transitions the QP to `IBV_QPS_ERR` and posts a dummy beacon send work request (`BEACON_WRID`) to drain remaining work completions.

On verbs providers like Mellanox mlx5, calling `ibv_post_send()` on a QP that has already transitioned to `IBV_QPS_ERR` fails with `EAGAIN` (errno 11, "Resource temporarily unavailable").

`RDMADispatcher::schedule_qp_destroy()` already handles a non-zero return from `to_dead()` by destroying the QP directly. Logging this expected condition with `lderr(cct)` (-1) pollutes stderr with false error messages on every ephemeral client disconnection (e.g. `ceph -s` or any rados client command).

Demote the log level from `lderr(cct)` to debug `ldout(cct, 20)`, matching the surrounding teardown log statements in `to_dead()`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82025
Fixes: e907e18154c7 ("msg/async/rdma: use special Beacon to detect SQ WRs drained")

73024.title: rgw: support Keystone write-only S3 credentials
73024.author: xek
73024.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in support for OpenStack Keystone scoped S3 signing-key exchange in RGW (`rgw_keystone_s3_auth_mode = signing_key`).

In `signing_key` mode, the gateway exchanges SigV4 request proofs for date- and service-scoped derived keys via `POST /v3/s3tokens/signing_key`, avoiding permanent root secret retrieval and network exposure. SigV2 requests undergo per-request identity validation via `POST /v3/s3tokens/validate`. Derived keys are held in a bounded process-local LRU cache bounded by identity expiration and local TTL; there is no fallback to raw secret retrieval.

## References

- Keystone spec: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/keystone-specs/+/1011634
- Related Keystone server-side change (WIP): https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/keystone/+/1012017

## Testing

- Native suite on this change: 91/91 tests and 2/2 ctest pass, including the new signing-key exchange and credential-validation tests.
- Functionally validated against a live Keystone + RGW deployment: baseline (5) and advanced (8) credential scenarios pass.

Opening as draft for early review.

Assisted-by: gemini-3.8-flash

73029.title: mgr/cephadm: fix host maintenance when the CRUSH host bucket is not named after the host
73029.author: vobruba-martin
73029.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82029

## Problem

When a host is placed into maintenance, cephadm sets the `noout` flag on the host's CRUSH bucket. The bucket name was derived from the hostname known to cephadm (the short hostname) instead of being looked up in the CRUSH map. If the bucket is named differently (renamed bucket, custom `crush_location`, bucket named after the FQDN, host added under a different name), the monitor rejects `osd set-group` with EINVAL and maintenance fails with `Unable to set the osds on <host> to noout (rc=-22)`.

Worse, `noout` was set only after `cephadm host-maintenance enter` had already stopped all daemons on the host. The error was raised before the host was marked as being in maintenance, so the host was left with all daemons stopped while `ceph orch host maintenance exit` refused with `Host <host> is not in maintenance mode`.

## Changes

1. **mgr/cephadm: set noout before stopping daemons for maintenance**

   `noout` is now set right after the ok-to-stop checks, before the NVMe-oF gateways are disabled and the daemons are stopped, which is also the usual order when taking OSDs down. If anything afterwards fails, `noout` is unset again. A failure to set `noout` now leaves the host untouched.

2. **mgr/cephadm: look up CRUSH buckets when setting noout for maintenance**

   New helper `_get_noout_targets()` takes the host's OSD ids from the cephadm daemon cache and looks up the host buckets holding them in `osd_map_tree`. A bucket is used only if it contains nothing but OSDs of this host, so OSDs of other hosts are never flagged. OSDs not covered by such a bucket (shared bucket, OSD not in CRUSH) are flagged individually as `osd.N`. The same targets are used for `osd unset-group` on exit.

   For clusters where the bucket is named after the short hostname, the target is the same as before, so hosts that entered maintenance with the old code exit cleanly.

73033.title: qa: Fix race in test_mgr_snapshot_mirror_status_cache
73033.author: kotreshhr
73033.body:
Avoid flaky metrics cache hit assert in mirror status test.

Retry consecutive status calls until they match. The metrics cache
keys entries by time window (int(monotonic() / ttl)), not by "N seconds
since the last fill", so two quick calls can still miss if they cross a window edge.

Example with ttl=3s: a call at monotonic 8.9 uses token 2 and caches the
result; a call 0.2s later at 9.1 uses token 3, misses, and reloads omap.
The mirror tick may have refreshed metrics_updated_at in between, so
assertEqual(res1, res2) fails even though the gap is well under the TTL.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82032

73037.title: src/common/options: add descriptions to mgr messenger throttle options
73037.author: anthonyeleven
73037.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82055

Add a `desc` and a `long_desc` to the eight messenger throttle options in `src/common/options/mgr.yaml.in` that had neither: `mgr_client_bytes`, `mgr_client_messages`, `mgr_osd_bytes`, `mgr_osd_messages`, `mgr_mds_bytes`, `mgr_mds_messages`, `mgr_mon_bytes` and `mgr_mon_messages`. Without them, `ceph config help` and the generated option docs said nothing.

What the text says, and where it comes from:
- `DaemonServer` gives each peer type one byte throttle and one message throttle through `set_policy_throttlers`, so every connection of that type shares them. Client covers the ceph CLI and daemons that connect as clients, such as RGW.
- A connection takes 1 message and the message's size before reading it off the network, in `ProtocolV2::throttle_message` and `throttle_bytes`, and gives both back when the `Message` is destroyed or its op is unregistered.
- When `get_or_fail` fails, the connection stops reading and retries every `ms_client_throttle_retry_time_interval`, so the senders back up.
- The active Manager's `throttle-mgr_<type>_<bytes|messages>` perf counters show it: `val` at or near `max`, and `get_or_fail_fail` rising.
- A limit of 0 means no limit, and a single message larger than the byte limit is still read.
- The throttles are built in the `DaemonServer` constructor and nothing tracks these keys, so a change takes effect when a Manager next becomes active, after a restart or failover.
- Each byte and message pair links to the other, and the byte options link to `mgr_dispatch_throttle_bytes`, whose `long_desc` says to size it against them.

73042.author: kotreshhr

73044.title: osd/OSDMap: don't copy the map to compute a read balance score
73044.author: anthonyeleven
73044.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82062

`OSDMap::calc_read_balance_score` made a `deepish_copy_from` of the whole OSDMap and scored the copy, and `get_pgs_by_osd`, which the score calls for every pool, made another copy to map the pool's PGs. Nothing changes either copy: every call made on them is const, and `deepish_copy_from` doesn't copy the CRUSH map anyway. This uses the map itself in both and drops the OSDMap argument from `calc_rbs_fair` and `calc_rbs_size_optimal`, which only read it.

`OSDMap::dump` scores every replicated pool, so each dump copied the map twice per replicated pool, including every `pg_upmap_items` entry. The mgr dumps `osd_map` under the GIL whenever a Python module asks for it, and the mons do the same for `osd dump` and `osd pool ls detail`.

Measured with `osdmaptool --dump json` on one host, using the map of a Reef cluster with 1,018 OSDs, 134 replicated pools and 10,108 `pg_upmap_items` entries:

| Build | Dump time |
|---|---|
| main | 2.52 s |
| main with this change | 2.05 s |

The output is byte-identical. Each copy took about 1.7 ms, twice per replicated pool. Most of the remaining time is spent mapping every PG of every replicated pool for the scores. #73045 leaves the scores out of the mgr's `osd_map` getter. The prometheus module reads `osd_map` twice per collection, and on that cluster the mgr stops dispatching messages for about 7 s each time.

73045.title: mgr: leave read balance scores out of the osd_map getter
73045.author: anthonyeleven
73045.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82063

`OSDMap::dump` computes a read balance score for every replicated pool, and each score maps every PG of the pool. The mgr's `osd_map` getter dumps the map under the GIL whenever a Python module asks for it, so every module stalls while the scores are computed.

On a Reef 18.2.8 cluster with 1,018 OSDs, 134 replicated pools and 10,108 `pg_upmap_items` entries, `osdmaptool --dump json` of the same map takes 2.55 s with Reef and 0.09 s with Quincy, which has no read balance score. The prometheus module reads `osd_map` twice per collection there, and the mgr stops dispatching messages for about 7 s each time. rbd_support reads it twice a minute.

No module needs the scores from `osd_map`:
- The balancer, the only module that uses them, gets them from `get_osdmap().dump()`, which still includes them.
- `ceph osd dump` and `ceph osd pool ls detail` are served by the mons and are unchanged.
- The dashboard passes every pool field through `/api/pool`, including `read_balance`. Neither its UI nor its OpenAPI spec uses it, so the field just stops appearing there.

This adds a `with_read_balance` argument to `OSDMap::dump` and `dump_pool`, true by default, and has the getter pass false. #73044 makes the scores cheaper for the callers that still want them.

#72754 complements this. It has pg_autoscaler and the balancer read the `osd_map` getter instead of building their own dump with `OSDMap.dump()`, and this PR takes the scores out of that getter. With both, the balancer's `upmap` mode plans from the getter's dump, which doesn't need the scores. The `read` and `upmap-read` modes still plan from `osdmap.dump()`, which has them.

The new `DumpWithReadBalance` test in `TestOSDMap.cc` dumps the map with the default, with `with_read_balance` true and with it false. It checks that only the replicated pool has a `read_balance` section, and only in the first two.

73046.title: mon/OSDMonitor: defer purged snaps scrub stamps to the next real map change
73046.author: anthonyeleven
73046.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82064

Each OSD scrubs its purged snaps every `osd_scrub_min_interval`, plus up to `osd_scrub_interval_randomize_ratio` of that, and reports when it last did in every beacon. `prepare_beacon` proposed a new OSDMap epoch every time the stamp moved, so a cluster made one epoch per OSD per scrub interval, about every 30 hours with the defaults.

Nothing reads the stamp: `osd_xinfo_t::last_purged_snaps_scrub` is only encoded, decoded and printed by `osd dump`. The epochs still cost what any epoch costs. Every OSD and client receives and applies the incremental, the mons store it and later trim it, and the mgr rebuilds `osd_map` for its Python modules, which takes seconds under the GIL on large clusters. On main each epoch also empties MgrMapCache.

Why we want this: on a Reef 18.2.8 cluster with 1,018 OSDs, days with no data movement and no OSD up or down changes have 790 to 920 epochs. Comparing 133 consecutive epochs field by field, everything that wasn't backfill was a single OSD's `last_purged_snaps_scrub` changing. 1,018 OSDs every 1.25 days on average is about 815 epochs a day, and on that cluster each one makes the mgr's Python modules stall for 2.5 s or more.

This records the stamp in the pending incremental without proposing, so it goes out with the next real map change. The OSD resends it in every beacon in case that incremental is lost, for example across a mon election.

Current rgw_write() implementation does not preserve extended attributes across writes for object,
therefore, if object is modifying all of its extended attributes are lost.

73049.author: dcasier

Removes the keys of deferred records that _deferred_replay() drops
entirely; they were left in the DB and could be replayed over object
data at a later mount. Details in the commit message.

This is a fallback for #69961, which fixes the root cause. If #69961 is
merged, this change is unnecessary and should be dropped.

Field report: Tentacle 20.2.4, EC 5+4 RBD pool with overwrites, HDD-only
OSDs without block.db. During an upgrade, systemd stop timeouts left OSD
containers running, which were then killed. After later restarts, 17
objects showed read_error, each on a single shard. On the one checked,
the 4 KiB block on disk held data foreign to the object (the crc32c of
the on-disk and expected blocks match the _verify_csum log), consistent

73050.title: mgr: set program_name to the python path, not the macro name
73050.author: sunyuechi
73050.body:
WCHAR() stringizes its argument without expanding it, so program_name has always been the literal "MGR_PYTHON_EXECUTABLE". Python then cannot find its executable: sys.executable is empty and sys.prefix is derived from the current directory.

Since Python 3.14 multiprocessing defaults to forkserver on Linux and spawns its helpers with sys.executable, so creating the ThreadPool in the cephadm module fails with BrokenPipeError and the module does not load.

Pass the byte string to PyConfig_SetBytesString() instead.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82073

73051.title: debian, rpm: let ceph-mgr-cephadm depend on routes
73051.author: sunyuechi

73053.author: vxtls
73053.body:
RGW currently reports `aws:PrincipalType` as `User` for every request. A public bucket policy that explicitly denies anonymous reads under a restricted prefix therefore fails to match those requests.

Update the bucket policy documentation.

73066.title: mds: do not ship null dentries with an exported dirfrag
73066.author: xiubli
73066.body:
A dirfrag keeps a null dentry for every name unlinked from it, and an export ships all of them. When a deleted tree spread by `ceph.dir.pin.distributed` empties, every MDS hands its subtrees back to the parent's MDS through `export_empty_import()`, and that MDS's cache jumps by millions of dentries (rank 0 went from 1.9M to 9.4M dentries in about a minute at the end of IO500 mdtest-easy-delete with 7 active MDS). An export pin moved after a delete ships them too, and the importer hands the empty dirfrag straight back with all of them.

This change:
- keeps an emptied dirfrag in `export_empty_import()` while it is dirty; the rmdir that usually follows drops the null dentries without a commit;
- drops the clean, unreferenced null dentries of each dirfrag in `encode_export_dir()`, as `trim_dentry()` would;
- drops them in batches before the export when a dirfrag has more than `mds_null_dentry_drop_batch` (new option, default 10000), letting go of `mds_lock` between batches.

Moving the export pin of a directory with 1000000 committed null dentries between 2 active MDS, while a create/unlink loop runs on each; ops and latency in the 120 s after the move, 2 runs each:

|                    | main        | this change |
|--------------------|-------------|-------------|
| ops                | 567k / 558k | 818k / 847k |
| p50 (us)           | 103 / 102   | 111 / 108   |
| p99 (us)           | 1176 / 1166 | 1175 / 1110 |
| p99.9 (ms)         | 51 / 52     | 10.5 / 9.2  |
| p99.99 (ms)        | 372 / 359   | 224 / 239   |
| max (s)            | 13.3 / 10.4 | 5.1 / 2.6   |
| longest export (s) | 11.3 / 10.4 | 2.7 / 1.0   |
| dentries exported  | 2.0M / 2.0M | 5 / 1       |

Reproducer and more numbers in the tracker.

Tested with vstart_runner: test_exports, test_strays, test_fragment, test_multimds_misc, test_snapshots, test_failover, test_forward_scrub, test_scrub_checks, test_journal_repair, test_dump_tree, test_misc; no new failures compared to main.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82078

73067.title: debian: build with ninja
73067.author: tchaikov
73067.body:
Since #66066 (0665ed1391a), every RGW executable and library statically links `librgw_lancedb.a` through `rgw_common`. All of these links wait for the cargo build and then start together. With Ubuntu's default LTO and `make -jN`, nothing limits how many run at once, so the jammy and noble package builds run out of memory. In ceph-dev-pipeline build 10219, 31 LTO links were running on a host with 255 GiB of RAM when the OOM killer killed `ld`. See https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82052.

This PR builds the Debian packages with `cmake+ninja`, so the job pools in `LimitJobs`, which are sized by the host's memory, limit the links too. With LTO enabled, each link is budgeted 6000 MiB instead of 4500 MiB. The RGW targets and `ceph-osd` are already in the heavy link pool, which has half as many jobs, so they get about 12000 MiB each. On a host with 255 GiB of RAM, that allows 43 regular and 21 heavy links at once.

Ninja has no jobserver, though, and without one `-flto=auto` runs an LTRANS job per CPU thread in every link. The first noble build with Ninja (build 10226) still ran out of memory: 21 heavy links were running 1485 LTRANS jobs between them, about 12.4 GiB per link. So the last commit passes `-flto=N` to the linker, where N is the number of CPU threads divided by the size of the heavy link pool. On a 192-thread builder, N is 9.

Peak PSS of each link's whole process tree, from two full local builds (`-g -O2 -flto=auto -ffat-lto-objects`, 32 threads, 3 heavy link jobs, so N = 10):

| target | link pool | `-flto=auto` | LTRANS jobs | `-flto=10` | LTRANS jobs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `crimson-osd` | heavy | 8.8 GiB | 29 | 5.5 GiB | 0 (peak in WPA) |
| `radosgw` | heavy | 8.0 GiB | 32 | 5.6 GiB | 9 |
| `denc-mod-rgw.so` | heavy | 7.4 GiB | 29 | 5.5 GiB | 9 |
| `radosgw-admin` | heavy | 7.2 GiB | 26 | 5.2 GiB | 8 |
| `librgw.so` | heavy | 7.2 GiB | 28 | 5.8 GiB | 9 |
| `ceph-osd` | heavy | 4.4 GiB | 27 | 2.3 GiB | 9 |
| **whole build** | | **2697 s** | | **2708 s** | |

With the cap, the heaviest link fits in the 6000 MiB budget, and 21 heavy links would need about 126 GiB. Each LTRANS job costs about 120 MiB, so without the cap a link grows with the size of the host. All 76 targets that link `librgw_lancedb.a` are in the heavy pool, so the RGW links don't need a pool of their own.

RGW should still link `rgw_lancedb` only into the targets that serve s3vectors. This PR doesn't change that. It only keeps the package build within the host's memory when many links become ready at once.

We could disable LTO instead, but I'd rather keep the performance it gives us.

The OOMs in #40097 happened before Ninja had these job pools, which were added in 897fd990bfc.

73069.title: crimson/osd/scrub: fix scrub stats accounting
73069.author: ronen-fr
73069.body:
Fixes in how the Crimson scrubber updates PG stats at the end of a scrub:

- **Shallow/deep stats update:** the scrub-maintained stats were copied only if
  `deep && !skip_for_shallow`. A shallow scrub therefore never recorded its errors,
  and a deep scrub never updated `num_deep_scrub_errors` or the omap stats.
  Now, as in Classic, `num_scrub_errors` is recomputed as shallow + deep errors
  (stat mismatches included), so a shallow scrub keeps the deep errors found
  earlier. `last_deep_scrub` and `last_clean_scrub_stamp` are now set too.
  The update moved into `update_stats_from_scrub()`, which has unit tests.
- **`num_objects_omap`:** this was counted from the scanned omap keys, which only
  a deep scrub reads, so with the above fix every shallow scrub of a PG with omap
  objects would report a stat mismatch. It is now counted using `oi.is_omap()`.
- **Segfault in a debug log:** a debug log in `compare_candidate_to_authoritative()`
  dereferenced `end()` when the candidate had no object info.

73072.title: crimson/os/seastore: prevent duplicate journal batch flushes
73072.author: myoungwon
73072.body:
When the journal I/O depth reaches FULL, RecordSubmitter waits for an outstanding I/O to complete before flushing the pending batch.

When an outstanding I/O completes, decrement_io_with_flush() is called to release an I/O slot and flush the pending batch if RecordSubmitter was FULL.
In decrement_io_with_flush(), flush_current_batch() is called before wait_unfull_flush_promise is resolved and reset. Note that flushing the batch may trigger another I/O completion callback, re-entering decrement_io_with_flush() before the promise is reset.

Since wait_unfull_flush_promise is still present, the reentrant call attempts to flush the current batch again, even though the first flush has already submitted its records and replaced the current batch with an empty one.

This can result in encode_records() being called with an empty record group, causing the metadata length assertion to fail:

ceph_assert(bl.length() == record_group.size.get_raw_mdlength());

To prevent this, move wait_unfull_flush_promise to a local variable and reset the optional before calling flush_current_batch().


Signed-off-by: Myoungwon Oh <ohmyoungwon@gmail.com>

73076.title: mgr/cephadm: fix misleading --force note on host maintenance enter
73076.author: anthonyeleven
73076.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/64267

When `ceph orch host maintenance enter` fails its ok-to-stop checks, the error always ends with `Note: Warnings can be bypassed with the --force flag`. With `--force` the warnings have already been let through, so what is left is an alert that `--force` cannot get past, for example an OSD ok-to-stop failure because PGs would become offline. Repeating the same note sends the user back to the flag they just gave.

This keeps the note when `--force` was not given. When it was, the note now says that `--force` does not bypass the check, that adding `--yes-i-really-mean-it` does, and that doing so is dangerous. Behavior is unchanged.

The host management docs already describe `--force` as bypassing warnings but not alerts, so no doc change is needed.

73079.title: rgw/sts: select JWKS keys by token kid before signature verification
73079.author: next0262
73079.body:
Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82089 (Enhancement)

`WebTokenEngine::validate_signature()` tries the provider's JWKS keys in order until one verifies the JWT. It reads each JWK's `kid` for logging but does not use the token's `kid` to select the verification key.

Use the token's `kid` to select matching keys before verification. This follows the key-selection model described in [OIDC Core §10.1.1](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#RotateSigKeys), where old and new signing keys can coexist during rotation. All eligible signing keys sharing the matching identifier are tried. If none verifies the token, validation fails. The existing all-key fallback is retained when the token has no `kid` or the JWKS has no eligible signing key with a matching identifier.

The helper selects candidates in one traversal of the parsed JWKS. The existing verification loop uses those objects directly, without serializing and reparsing individual keys. The OIDC documentation describes matching-key validation and the fallback behavior.

Testing: sixteen key-selection unit tests passed locally on Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 / GCC 13.3 using a separate CMake harness with existing Ceph common, Boost and GoogleTest libraries. Also compiled `rgw_rest_sts.cc` to an object file. Full RGW linking and STS integration tests have not been run locally. RGW teuthology QA is pending review.


A local RS256/RSA-2048 microbenchmark with eight signing keys and the matching key last reduced verification attempts from eight to one: bare n/e took 536 → 172 µs, and x5c took 4.11 → 1.03 ms. These are medians of seven batches of 200 validations in an ARM64 VM, including JWT/JWKS parsing but excluding network, thumbprint checks and logging; they are not end-to-end STS timings. [Method, build details, source and full results](https://github.com/next0262/ceph/tree/212b17082cf8bc396b09f6b4e6989b7f1f8c8f4b/benchmarks/rgw-sts-kid).

73080.title: squid: tools/ceph-bluestore-tool: remove duplicate "--yes-i-really-really-mean-it" registration

Commit 48b1db81e6 ("tools/ceph-bluestore-tool: fix
`--yes-i-really-really-mean-it` option") renamed the legacy

This breaks every ceph-volume invocation that passes the flag — in
particular `ceph-volume lvm zap` fails during OSD provisioning, so any
test that provisions OSDs with the `ceph:squid` CI image dies in setup.
All 25 failures of this upgrade run are this single error:

https://pulpito.ceph.com/yuriw-2026-10-23_17:06:15-upgrade-umbrella-release-distro-default-trial/

main, tentacle and umbrella-release have a single registration and are

73081.title: mon/OSDMonitor: unstick osdmap trim after PG merge
73081.author: anthonyeleven
73081.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82094

#48212 made `LastEpochClean::Lec::report` truncate `epoch_by_pg` to the pool's new `pg_num`, but the cached `floor` is kept. The floor is recomputed only when the reporting PG's previous value equals it, so when the PG that held the floor was merged away nothing moves it again, and osdmap trimming stops until the leader mon restarts. This takes the floor from the remaining PGs when the list shrinks. It also brings `next_missing` back inside the list, so that PGs added by a later split are waited for instead of being counted as already reported.

Why we want this: on a Reef 18.2.8 cluster with 30 CephFS file systems, after seven pools were shrunk the mons kept about 52,600 osdmaps for almost nine days. During that time a layout change through a kernel mount that had been idle for months made the mon send that client about 47,500 maps, roughly 30 GB. While the mon built and queued them it stopped answering its other sessions for about 20 seconds. The MDS daemons whose sessions were on that mon passed `mds_beacon_grace`, and 7 file systems failed over. The stuck trim is why the backlog was that large.

Testing:
- New `unittest_mon_last_epoch_clean`: both tests pass with the change, and both fail without it, 10 instead of 60 for the merged floor and 21 instead of 0 for the split that follows a merge.

73083.body:
While a split of a dirfrag is pending, every hit_dir() on it calls should_split_fast().  When the dirfrag holds more than the fast limit (mds_bal_split_size * mds_bal_fragment_fast_factor) of linked and null dentries together but no more than that in its fragstat, it counts the linked dentries one by one, under mds_lock.

A big directory that is being emptied gets there: when its dirfrags shrink below mds_bal_merge_size they merge into one that still holds some thousand files and every null dentry left by the unlinks.  In an IO500 mdtest-hard-delete with 16 tasks the merged dirfrag had 12831 files, so a split was queued, and 1.93 million null dentries.  Each lookup and unlink in the directory then held mds_lock for about 270 ms to scan them; the finisher thread got the lock only between two of them, so journal completions waited up to 62 seconds and the client requests behind them piled up: the slowest tasks finished 100 to 150 seconds after the others.

Return false straight away while the dirfrag is already being split or merged: can_fragment() refuses another fragment operation until that one is done.  That is also the worst case, since the freeze waits for every auth pin on the dirfrag to drop, and each request dropping one went through the scan.  Another run caught the merged dirfrag in that state with 2627 nested auth pins, each completion taking 260 ms.

Otherwise, a dentry whose projected linkage differs from its current one is xlocked, and so auth pinned, by the request changing it, and that pin counts in dir_auth_pins.  The effective size is therefore within dir_auth_pins of the linked dentries; only scan when the fast limit lies in that range.  Should a projected linkage ever come without a pin, the fast split is only delayed until the normal one.

IO500 mdtest-hard-delete, 1 MDS, kernel client, 16 tasks on 4 mounts, the same build without and with this change, one row per run.  "tasks" is the time of the fastest and the slowest task, "no journal" the longest time without a journal completion in 7 s perf samples:
```
  +---------+-------+--------+------------+------------+
  | build   | IOPS  | time   | tasks      | no journal |
  +---------+-------+--------+------------+------------+
  | before  | 3.82k | 488 s  | 350-478 s  |    43 s    |
  | before  | 3.50k | 535 s  | 360-527 s  |    57 s    |
  | before  | 4.83k | 394 s  | 366-384 s  |     0 s    |
  | before  | 4.78k | 400 s  | 360-391 s  |     0 s    |
  +---------+-------+--------+------------+------------+
  | after   | 4.67k | 399 s  | 370-390 s  |     0 s    |
  | after   | 4.72k | 398 s  | 354-387 s  |     0 s    |
  | after   | 4.65k | 409 s  | 372-402 s  |     0 s    |
  +---------+-------+--------+------------+------------+
```
More data from IO500 tests:

Setup: IO500 SC26 on 1 MDS (32 GiB cache), 3 OSDs, kernel clients, 16 tasks on 4 mounts, 3 interleaved runs per build. Latency comes from the paired mdbench runs (libcephfs) at 2/4/8/12 clients. Each value is the median of 3 runs, and latency is pooled over all clients.

73084.title: mds: optionally give no writeable range until the client asks for one
73084.author: xiubli
73084.body:
An open with `CEPH_FILE_MODE_WR` gives the client a writeable range right away: `Server::handle_client_open()` calls `check_inode_max_size()`, which takes the filelock wrlock (possibly revoking other clients' file caps) and journals an inode update with the new `client_ranges`. When the client releases Fw on close, the range drops to 0, which is another journaled update. Many applications open read-write and never write; mdtest did that in its read phase until hpc/ior#557.

This PR adds `mds_defer_open_client_range` (default **off**). With it, an open for write still issues the caps but no range, and a client gets a range only when its cap message asks for a max_size above the range it has. Only the client asking gets a new range: `check_inode_max_size()` no longer hands ranges to every Fw holder on the inode. `_do_cap_update()` no longer grows max_size ahead of the writes for a client without a range. Otherwise, the journaled update would just move from the open to the close. The kernel client and libcephfs already wait for the MDS before writing past max_size and resend the request after a reconnect or a cap import, so no client change is needed.

The first commit is a separate fix found while measuring this: since 52918175f01, `issue_new_caps()` flushes the journal when the opener wants caps whose lock is busy, and that includes the rdlocks the open request holds itself. So every write-mode open of an existing file by name, as the kernel client sends it, forced a journal flush.

### Measurements

Setup:
- One bare-metal host, 3 NVMe OSDs, 1 MDS with a 32 GiB cache, pinned to 4 cores.
- Kernel client: the Fedora 7.2.9 in-tree module.
- tuned `latency-performance`.
- Fresh cluster per run; 3 runs per arm, interleaved; numbers are medians.

| arm | build | option |
|---|---|---|
| base | main + the fix for [82083](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82083) | n/a |
| off | this PR + the fix for 82083 | `mds_defer_open_client_range=false` |
| on | this PR + the fix for 82083 | `mds_defer_open_client_range=true` |

All arms carry the fix for tracker 82083 (`should_split_fast()` scanning every null dentry under mds_lock), which is a separate PR. Without it, hard-delete can stall for tens of seconds while `should_split_fast()` rescans about 1.9M null dentries of a merged dirfrag, and those stalls hide the effect of this change.

#### IO500 (16 processes, standard mode; score, median [min–max] of 3)

| phase | base | off | on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ior-easy-write | 1.275 | 1.278 | 1.273 |
| mdtest-easy-write | 6.720 | 6.790 | 6.833 |
| ior-hard-write | 0.186 | 0.188 | 0.187 |
| mdtest-hard-write | 5.816 | 5.758 | 5.707 |

73090.title: mds: compute ephemeral split floor before requeuing pins
73090.author: vshankar
73090.body:
When max_mds changes, MDCache::handle_mdsmap() requeues every ephemerally pinned directory before recomputing the minimum split depth (export_ephemeral_dist_frag_bits) for the new max_mds. queue_export_pin() therefore checks a rank's dirfrags against the old depth and only queues the directory if one of them now hashes to another rank. On ranks where none does, the dirfrags are never split to the new depth, leaving part of a distributed pinned directory coarsely fragmented after max_mds is increased and limiting how evenly it is spread across the ranks.

Compute the split depth before requeuing.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82102

73092.title: bluestore-tool: remove duplicate "--yes-i-really-really-mean-it" registration
73092.author: kginonredhat
73092.body:
The backport of c266ef0f61f7 ("tools/ceph-bluestore-tool: fix \"--yes-i-really-really-mean-it\" option\") accidentally left the option registered **twice** in `main()`, which makes boost::program_options reject the flag whenever it is used:

```
$ ceph-bluestore-tool zap-device --dev /dev/vg_nvme/lv_4 --yes-i-really-really-mean-it
option '--yes-i-really-really-mean-it' is ambiguous and matches different versions of '--yes-i-really-really-mean-it'
```

This breaks `ceph-volume lvm zap` on freshly built squid containers and every cephadm OSD deployment bootstrapping from the squid image (e.g. 7 jobs in rkachach-2026-10-22_16:59:52-orch:cephadm-wip-rkachach-testing-2026-10-22-1457-distro-default-trial, 17 jobs in yuriw-2026-10-21_19:55:50-orch-wip-yuri15-testing-20261021.152238-umbrella-distro-default-trial).

Only squid is affected (main/tentacle register the option once; reef doesn't have it), so this is a direct branch-specific fix.

**Closing in favor of #72991 (same fix by the original author, already being tested).** See also trackers #81992 / #82088.

73093.title: container: revert to nfsganesha-9 repo
73093.author: kginonredhat
73093.body:
Commit 4c4b34fa0de ("container: bump nfs-ganesha version to 15", tracker #80549) made the container build install ganesha 15.x from the CentOS storage SIG `nfsganesha-15` repository. With ganesha **15.8 and 15.9** from that repo (the versions served since mid-October 2026), `ganesha.nfsd` dies during startup whenever an **RGW export** is configured: the daemon exits right after `Load client info completed from backend` and systemd restarts it in a loop. Note that ganesha 15.x exits with status 0 on fatal errors, so the unit log shows a misleading `Deactivated successfully`, and the actual error is lost with the buffered log.

As a result `ceph nfs export create rgw` renders the nfs daemon unusable and mounts fail with `mount.nfs: Connection reset by peer`. The orch:cephadm `nfs-ingress-rgw-user` / `nfs-ingress-rgw-bucket` tests fail on every main-based branch since the SIG repo started serving 15.8/15.9:

* rkachach-2026-10-22_16:59:52-orch:cephadm-wip-rkachach-testing-2026-10-22-1457-distro-default-trial (ganesha **15.9**, 3 jobs)
* rkachach-2026-10-24_20:04:03-orch:cephadm-wip-rkachach-testing-2026-10-24-1642-distro-default-trial (ganesha 15.9, 2 jobs)
* rkachach-2026-10-20_13:33:31-orch:cephadm-wip-rkachach-testing-2-2026-10-20-1240-distro-default-trial (ganesha **15.8**, 1 job)

while the same tests pass on branches whose containers still use ganesha **9.16** from the `nfsganesha-9` repository:

* yuriw-2026-10-21_19:55:50-orch-wip-yuri15-testing-20261021.152238-umbrella-distro-default-trial (all 4 nfs-ingress-rgw-* pass)
* yuriw-2026-10-20_19:35:34-orch-wip-yuri13-testing-20261020.164521-umbrella-distro-default-trial (all 4 pass)

I verified that `libfsalrgw.so` and `librgw.so.2` are present in the affected images and that the module loads cleanly against the bundled ceph libraries, so the failure happens inside the ganesha 15.x RGW FSAL itself (running `ganesha.nfsd -F -L STDOUT` inside a built container reproduces the fatal exit and shows the actual error).

This reverts the container to the `nfsganesha-9` repository until the ganesha 15.x RGW FSAL issue is understood and fixed (either upstream in nfs-ganesha or in the SIG build), at which point the bump can be re-introduced.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80549

**Testing:** verified the failing/passing runs above against the ganesha version reported by `ceph orch ps` for the nfs daemons (15.8/15.9 failing vs 9.16 passing); diff of the container image contents confirmed libfsalrgw.so/librgw.so.2 presence and a successful dlopen.

73094.title: mgr/cephadm: process user-scheduled daemon actions first
73094.author: kginonredhat
73094.body:
`_check_daemons()` iterates the known daemons in cache order and acts on them one at a time. If one daemon misbehaves -- e.g. its reconfig keeps failing because the unit does not come up -- it can occupy the (single threaded) serve loop for a long time on every cycle, and the reconfiguration storm that typically follows an mgr failover adds even more dependency-driven work. User-scheduled actions (e.g. `ceph orch daemon redeploy`) can end up starved for minutes as a consequence.

Example: in job 667884 of run rkachach-2026-10-22_16:59:52-orch:cephadm-wip-rkachach-testing-2026-10-22-1457-distro-default-trial, the second standby mgr was scheduled to be redeployed (`Scheduled to redeploy mgr.y` at 17:34:17, persisted in the host inventory), but the serve loop of the active mgr kept getting stuck on:

* a broken iscsi gateway whose `systemctl restart` timed out on every cycle (each attempt blocking the loop ~25-90s), and
* the post-failover reconfigurations of the monitoring stack (prometheus/grafana/... redeploys and reconfigs, which make `_apply_all_services()` keep returning early with `continue`).

The redeploy never executed before the test failed on `ceph versions | jq -e '.mgr | length == 1'`.

Process daemons with pending user-scheduled actions first, so that explicit user requests are not delayed by reconciliation work. Python's stable sort keeps the relative order within each group unchanged.

**Testing:** added `test_daemon_action_priority` unit test (follows the existing `test_daemon_check` pattern: two managed rgw services, a monmap change so both daemons want a reconfig, plus a scheduled redeploy for the second daemon; verifies via a mocked `_daemon_action` that the scheduled daemon is processed first and both are processed). Full suite runs in CI via tox.

73095.title: qa/tasks/cephfs/test_nfs: wait more robustly for ganesha redeploy
73095.author: kginonredhat
73095.body:
`apply_ganesha_spec()` waits for the ganesha daemon to be redeployed after `ceph orch apply -i` by polling `pgrep ganesha.nfsd` on the cluster host and waiting for the PID to change, with a 60 second window (15 tries x 4s).

That is both fragile and too tight:

* the redeploy can legitimately take longer than 60s when the cephadm serve loop is busy (e.g. a broken daemon whose reconfig keeps failing, or the reconfiguration storm following an mgr failover) -- see job 667870 of run rkachach-2026-10-22_16:59:52-orch:cephadm-wip-rkachach-testing-2026-10-22-1457-distro-default-trial, where the wait timed out with `MaxWhileTries: reached maximum tries (15) after waiting for 60 seconds` during `test_async_io_fio` setup;
* matching on the host-side PID of the daemon process is indirect: `ceph orch ps` already reports the `started` timestamp of every daemon, which changes exactly when the daemon is redeployed.

Poll the `started` timestamps reported by `ceph orch ps -f json` instead, and extend the window to 3 minutes.

**Testing:** syntax-checked; exercised by the `qa/suites/cephadm/nfs` suite in CI.

73096.title: mds: fix session handling when a subtree import is reverted
73096.author: LiShengG
73096.body:
If the exporter fails while the importer is journaling EImportStart, the
import is reverted in IMPORT_LOGGINGSTART while C_MDS_ImportDirLoggedStart
is still pending. That callback owns the sessions force-opened by
prepare_force_open_sessions(), but since #51766 it no longer cleans them up:

- without bystanders, `import_logged_start()` hits
  `ceph_assert(it != import_state.end())`;
- with bystanders, `importing_count` and the projected sessionmap version
  leak; the client can no longer be evicted, and the next session journal
  fails `ceph_assert(projected.front() == v)` in `Session::pop_pv()`.

Related problems in the same rollback path:

- `close_forced_opened_sessions()` decides by the state_seq of the import
  that force-opened the session. With imports sharing a session it closes
  one a finished import is using (dropping its caps), asserts
  `!session->is_importing()` while another import still holds it, and never
  closes it after OPEN -> STALE, so the client is later evicted and
  blocklisted.
- `terminate_sessions()` on a stopping rank can close a session the pending
  callback still references, and `finish_force_open_sessions()` then asserts.
- `PIN_IMPORTINGCAPS` is only dropped in IMPORT_ACKING, so it leaks on a
  LOGGINGSTART revert.

Testing: each case in the tracker was reproduced on vstart against main
 and no longer reproduces with this series. Also ran export pin churn 
across 3 ranks under client IO followed by `max_mds` 3 -> 1,
with no asserts, leaked sessions or blocklisted clients. 

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82107

73103.title: cephadm: add fcm-dedup daemon type for per-OSD dedup deployment
73103.author: David-Skel
73103.body:
Deploy the FCM dedup process as a first-class cephadm daemon, one per "in" OSD on the host that runs it, using the Ceph base container image. Each daemon runs /usr/bin/fcm-dedup privileged with /dev mounted for NVMe IO passthrough, and gets its own client.fcm-dedup.<osd_id> keyring.

The fcm-dedup mgr module (downstream) decides when to deploy by applying a single FcmDedupSpec. This change only registers the service and daemon type and expands that spec into per-OSD daemons. It contains no dedup logic.

- cephadm/services/fcm_dedup.py: new FcmDedupService. `filter_host_candidates()` returns one daemon per "in" OSD, named by OSD id and placed on the host that runs the OSD. `prepare_create()` provisions the `client.fcm-dedup.<osd_id>` keyring and config.

- cephadm/services/cephadmservice.py: add 'fcm-dedup' to `get_auth_entity()`.

- cephadm/module.py: add `apply_fcm_dedup()` and a default placement entry (all hosts).

- cephadm/utils.py: add 'fcm-dedup' to `CEPH_IMAGE_TYPES` and `name_to_config_section()`.

- cephadmlib/daemons/fcm_dedup.py: new FcmDedup daemon form. Runs /usr/bin/fcm-dedup --id <osd_id> --fsid <fsid> with --privileged, /dev passthrough, ceph.conf and keyring mounts.

- `cephadmlib/daemons/__init__.py`: export FcmDedup daemon form.

73105.title: test/osd: make rb_osdsize_opt_score deterministic
73105.author: kginonredhat
73105.body:
`OSDMapTest.rb_osdsize_opt_score` is flaky: the fixture's `balance_capacity()` calls `calc_pg_upmaps()` **without a seed**, so the PG shuffle inside is seeded from `/dev/random` (see `OSDMap::get_random_engine`: *"When p_seed == nullptr it generates random engine with a seed from /dev/random"* — and `osd_calc_pg_upmaps_aggressively` defaults to true, so the shuffle runs). The resulting placement — and with it the read balance scores — differs from run to run.

For some placements the **rounded** `acting_adj_score` coincides with the **rounded** `fair_score` even at read ratios ≤ 85, failing the `ASSERT_NE(rbi.acting_adj_score, fair_score)`:

```
/ceph/src/test/osd/TestOSDMap.cc:3509: Failure
Expected: (rbi.acting_adj_score) != (fair_score), actual: 1.15 vs 1.15
```

This was hit by an unrelated QA-only PR (touching only `qa/tasks/cephfs/test_nfs.py`) in [jenkins run 6543](https://jenkins.ceph.com/job/ceph-pr-pipeline/6543/); the neighboring pipeline runs of the same code passed, confirming the run-to-run variance comes from the random seeding.

`calc_pg_upmaps()` already takes an optional `p_seed` parameter that exists precisely *"to create regression test without random effect on the results"*. Use it: give `balance_capacity()` an optional fixed seed (default 0 keeps the current behavior for its other users) and pass a fixed seed from `rb_osdsize_opt_score` so its placement is stable.

73106.title: mon: drop messages from unranked peers in quorum
73106.author: kamoltat
73106.body:
**Problem:**
A monitor outside the monmap can authenticate and keep exchanging messages with quorum members. Drop its messages and close the connection while we are in quorum, without changing discovery during bootstrap.


**From tracker 81588**
A ceph-mon was running on a host that is listed in mon_host and has a [mon.c] section in ceph.conf, but that is NOT a member of the monmap. It held the cluster's valid mon. keyring, so both quorum mons authenticated it, and it exchanged ~19,000 messages per second with each of them indefinitely. Both quorum mons grew without bound in the buffer_anon mempool, at roughly 35-39 MB/s (~130 GiB/hour), until the kernel OOM-killed them (observed at ~243 GiB RSS). With a 2-mon monmap, this repeatedly took the whole cluster offline. Stopping the stray daemon stopped the growth immediately.

The stray mon came from a misconfiguration. Even so, a single unranked peer should not be able to cause unbounded memory growth on the quorum mons which took down the cluster every hour and a half.



**Solution:**
Add a guard against a mon that doesn't exist in monmap

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81588

Assisted-by: Copilot
Signed-off-by: Kamoltat (Junior) Sirivadhna <ksirivad@redhat.com>

73118.title: mds: keep the first-data-pool backtrace of a file renamed before an MDS failover
73118.author: anthonyeleven
73118.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82134

A file created in a data pool other than the first data pool is journaled with DIRTYPARENT and DIRTYPOOL. Its backtrace in the first data pool is stored when that segment expires. A later backtrace update, such as a rename, an unlink to stray or a stray reintegration, journals the inode with DIRTYPARENT only. It also moves the inode onto the current segment's `dirty_parent_inodes` list, so the first segment can expire without storing anything. If the MDS fails over before the later segment expires, replay calls `mark_dirty_parent(logseg, false)`, and the backtrace in the first data pool is never written. A cold `open_ino()` through a hard link then returns EIO and records backtrace damage.

This makes `EMetaBlob::add_primary_dentry()` journal DIRTYPOOL whenever it journals DIRTYPARENT for an inode that still has STATE_DIRTYPOOL set. The new test in `test_backtrace.py` renames a file in a later segment, fails the MDS over after the create's segment is trimmed, and checks the backtrace in the first data pool.

### Testing

On an 18.2.8 lab cluster, using the reproducer in the tracker (`mds_log_events_per_segment=10`, `mds_log_max_segments=2`):

- **Without the fix:** five files renamed in a later segment lost their first-pool backtraces. Control files created alone, or created and renamed in the same segment, kept theirs. A cold read through a hard link to one of the five returned EIO, with `damage_type: backtrace`.
- **With this change applied to 18.2.8** (the function is the same there): all seven files have their first-pool backtrace. The renamed files' backtraces point at the second pool with the new name as the first ancestor. The cold read through the hard link succeeds, and `damage ls` is empty.

The new qa test hasn't run yet.

Scrub's not checking the first-pool backtrace is tracked separately in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82135.

73120.title: mgr/DaemonServer: move mark_finish_mon_command into ReplyOnFinish::finish()
73120.author: stzuraski898
73120.body:
### Summary
ReplyOnFinish::ReplyOnFinish() called op->mark_finish_mon_command() in its constructor body. The constructor runs as soon as the Context is allocated, before monc dispatches the command and before any mon reply arrives. The op-tracker therefore reported "mon command finished" for ops that were still waiting on the mon, for example during a mon election.

### Fix
Remove the call from the constructor and make it the first step of ReplyOnFinish::finish(). MonClient invokes finish() when the mon reply arrives, so the finish flag is now set only after the command has completed. The if (op) guard is kept. Nothing else in finish() changes: it still claims from_mon into cmdctx->odata and calls cmdctx->reply(r, outs).

The change is 4 insertions and 5 deletions in src/mgr/DaemonServer.cc.

### Impact / likelihood
This is an observability bug, not a functional one. The command path and the reply to the client are unchanged. Only the timing of the op-tracker's "finished mon command" event moves, from before dispatch to reply receipt. It matters when the mon is slow or unavailable, because the old code recorded a finish time for a command that had not run. This affects the reported timing and op-tracker output, such as dump_ops_in_flight and slow-op diagnostics, for these commands.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82136

73124.title: osd: defer the optimized EC roll-forward kick by pct_update_delay
73124.author: vitaly-goot
73124.body:
When the RMW pipeline of an optimized EC PG goes idle after a write whose version is past `can_rollback_to`, `finish_rmw` sends every shard that still holds rollback state a dummy, transaction-empty op carrying `pg_committed_to`, so that the shard can discard that state. Each kick costs those shards a transaction with a full PG info write (`last_update` does not move, so the fast info key cannot be used) and a message pair, and the next write's acknowledgement queues behind the kick's commit. Under eleven clients at queue depth 128 on 512 PGs, a PG has about three writes in flight, most of them still queued ahead of `do_op`, so the pipeline is idle after about every third write and the kicks were about a quarter of all shard transactions.

`ReplicatedBackend` sends its committed point the same way after the pool's `pct_update_delay` (`maybe_kick_pct_update`). This PR gives the optimized EC pipeline the same pool option:

| `pct_update_delay` | replicated pool (unchanged) | optimized EC pool |
|---|---|---|
| not set | committed point not sent on its own (replicas learn of it with the next write) | kick sent at once (as today) |
| `0` | the mon removes the option: same as not set | same as not set: kick sent at once |
| `N > 0` | sent N s after the last write, if nothing is in flight | kick sent N s after the last write, if the pipeline is still idle and still past `can_rollback_to` |

(`pool set <pool> pct_update_delay 0` unsets an integer pool option, `OSDMonitor::prepare_command_pool_set`; the "<= 0 sends immediately" in the `osd_types.h` comment therefore only applies to a negative value.)

With a positive delay, `finish_rmw` hands the kick to `ECBackend`, which arms the PG timer (`RMWPipeline::defer_rollforward`, modelled on `pct_callback_t`); each write that finishes starts the delay again, and `kick_rollforward` then sends the dummy op only if the pipeline is still idle and `committed_to` is still past `can_rollback_to`. A PG under steady load sends none, since every write carries `pg_committed_to` itself. An interval change cancels the timer, and the pipeline's reset of `committed_to` makes a kick that already left the timer a no-op. Without the option, or with `0`, the kick is sent at once, as before: unlike a replica, an EC shard needs the committed point to free its rollback state, so the EC kick cannot go unsent the way the replicated update does without the option.

### Costs of the delay

Both are bounded by the delay after the last write of an otherwise idle PG, and neither applies under steady load:

- A shard keeps the rollback clones of the overwritten ranges (`PGBackend::rollback_extents`, the `ghobject_t(hoid, gen, shard)` clones) that much longer before the roll-forward removes them.
- A balanced read of a just-written object that reaches a non-primary shard is bounced to the primary (`PeeringState::can_serve_read`, `-EAGAIN`) that much longer.

The extent cache is not affected: the dummy op never enters it (`finish_rmw` calls `cache_ready` directly), and its LRU is bounded by size, not by the kick.

### Measured

On a v20.2.4-based prototype of this change with a 200 ms delay, at saturation (aligned 4 KiB random writes, eleven clients at queue depth 128, an 8+3 pool with optimizations, 3 and 96 GiB per volume, two alternated runs per cell): 1.05x write IOPS, 0.93x p99 write latency and 0.95x bytes written to the devices, against the immediate kick. The pool option counts whole seconds, so 1 s is the shortest delay it can set; at 1 s fewer kicks fire and the bound above is 1 s.

Crimson's EC backend shares `RMWPipeline`; it does not set the hook and keeps the immediate kick.

### Testing

- `-Wall -Werror` syntax check of the 11 translation units that include the changed headers against main's headers (last run on main `2e8a3d289c2`); a planted error in `ECBackend.h` is rejected. I do not have a build of main, so CI on this PR is the first real build.
- No qa suite sets `pct_update_delay` on an erasure-code

73126.title: crimson/osd: check seastore merge shards before sending READY
73126.author: shreya-subramanian
73126.body:
On seastore, a PG merge whose source and target live on different shards is not supported. The cross-shard check only ran in PGAdvanceMap::merge_pg, i.e. after the monitor had already committed the pg_num decrement. By then the NOT READY / stop-merge sent by abort_seastore_cross_shard_merge() was too late: the pool was left with pg_num already decremented, merging disabled, and the source PG still running on the OSD as an orphan.

Run the same check before READY is sent. Add
ShardServices::seastore_pending_merge_shards_ok(). Given a PG and the pool's current and pending pg_num, it works out the merge target and sources and runs the existing shard check on them. Both PG::set_ready_to_merge_source() and set_ready_to_merge_target() now call it first and only send READY if it passes.
On failure, seastore_merge_shards_ok() already aborts the merge (clears ready state, sends NOT READY and stop-merge), so the monitor never commits the decrement. The check in merge_pg is kept as a safety net.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/77481

73133.title: qa/cephfs: ignore late cap release warnings in fs:thrash/quarantine
73133.author: vshankar
73133.body:
Enabling quarantine revokes all caps except PIN from clients without quarantine access. To release Fb, a client must first write back its dirty data. With a buffered write heavy workload (e.g. ffsb laying out its fileset) and msgr fault injection, that writeback can take longer than session_timeout, so the MDS warns that the client isn't responding to the revoke. The client does release the caps eventually, so this is expected.

Fixes: http://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82120

73134.title: rgw: stop the realm reloader before destroying the pausers
73134.author: sunyuechi
73134.body:
A period commit schedules a realm reload, which takes seconds. If
radosgw gets SIGTERM meanwhile, `AppMain::shutdown()` destroys
`rgw_pauser` and `fe_pauser` before `reloader`, and the running
`reload()` calls `pause()`/`resume()` on freed objects and segfaults.

Reset the realm watcher and the reloader first. The reloader's
destructor joins its timer thread, so it waits for a reload in
progress. This order was changed in e70d9328fc7.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80488

73141.title: mgr/dashboard: fix stale bucket details after editing a tenanted bucket
73141.author: aaSharma14
73141.body:
RgwBucketService caches bucket details per bucket id. The class is decorated with @cdEncode, which runs encodeURIComponent on every string argument of every method, including the private invalidateBucketCache().

**Issue:** get('abcd/bucket') therefore caches under 'abcd%2Fbucket'. update() receives the already-encoded id and calls invalidateBucketCache(), which encoded it a second time to 'abcd%252Fbucket'. That key is never in the map, so the stale entry survived the edit. Reopening the edit form or the details page replayed the old GET response, so changes such as versioning, encryption or replication looked as if they had not been applied, although the backend had applied them. Buckets without a tenant were not affected because their id has nothing to encode.

**Fix:** Mark the argument of invalidateBucketCache() with @cdEncodeNot so the encoded id is used as-is. setLifecycle() built its key as 'tenant/bucket' and only matched because of the second encoding, so it
now builds 'tenant%2Fbucket' explicitly.

Add unit tests that edit a tenanted bucket (and set its lifecycle) and check that the next get() hits the backend again.

**Before:**


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5588f7e0-27c5-4520-8372-ef3659119337



**After:** 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4278e10-7bc8-4d9c-8137-55122ede003a





Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82142
Signed-off-by: Aashish Sharma <aasharma@redhat.com>

73142.title: spdk: update SPDK to v26.05 and build packages with SPDK
73142.author: fultheim
73142.body:
Follow-up to #69516 (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/69516#issuecomment-6334819848), where we agreed to update the bundled SPDK. This PR moves the bundled SPDK to v26.05 and builds the packages with SPDK.

At review this PR was split in three, which can merge independently:
- This PR: SPDK build and packaging.
- #73197: crimson SPDK qpair lifetime fix.
- #73198: crimson-rados-experimental/spdk teuthology suite. Its jobs pass only once this PR and #73197 are in.

## Commits

1. **ceph.spec.in,debian/control: add SPDK build deps for make check.**
   - make check builds WITH_SPDK (`src/script/run-make.sh`), with or without WITH_CRIMSON.
   - SPDK v26.05 builds DPDK with meson, which needs pyelftools.
   - SPDK generates code with a script that imports jinja2 and tabulate.
2. **spdk: update submodule to v26.05**
   - Moves `src/spdk` from v20.07 to `ceph/spdk` `ceph-nvmeof-v26.05`, the branch the NVMe-oF gateway already uses.
     - That branch is upstream v26.05 plus target-side patches.
     - The only initiator change is wildcard-listener matching in `spdk_nvme_transport_id_compare()`.
   - DPDK 25.11 has no legacy make build, so SPDK's configure now builds its bundled DPDK.
   - SPDK's apps, tests, examples and optional target/bdev modules are left out.
   - Links the static closure of `spdk_nvme`, `spdk_env_dpdk` and `spdk_sock_posix`, plus ISA-L.
   - Passes the C++ compiler to SPDK's configure along with the C compiler. v26.05 has a C++ library (`lib/trace_parser`) that would otherwise build with the system `c++` in a clang build.
   - `BuildDPDK.cmake` now only builds Seastar's DPDK. `WITH_DPDK` (async messenger) needs a system DPDK.
   - BlueStore's `NVMEDevice` and crimson's SPDK driver already build against both APIs.
3. **cmake/modules/BuildSPDK: run make by path in the SPDK build step**
   - Fixes a bug already on main.
   - With a Makefile generator, `LOG_BUILD` runs the command from a script where `$(MAKE)` is not expanded: `env: '$(MAKE)': No such file or directory`.
   - It went unnoticed because ninja is fine and no package was built WITH_SPDK.
4. **ceph.spec.in,debian: build with SPDK on x86_64 and aarch64**
   - RPM: `%bcond spdk`, on for x86_64 and aarch64. Opt out with `--without spdk`.
   - Debian: amd64 and arm64.
   - The SPDK build deps become regular build deps.
   - This also enables BlueStore `spdk:` devices in classic ceph-osd, since WITH_SPDK is one option.

## Testing

All on x86_64 (Rocky 10 host, kernel 7.2). The tests ran on main at 2e8a3d289c2, together with #73197 and #73198 in one branch.

- **Packages**:
  - RPM (Rocky 10) and DEB (Ubuntu 24.04) build with SPDK.
  - `ceph-osd-crimson` links SPDK v26.05 with the NVMe/TCP transport in both. Classic `ceph-osd` does too in the RPM.
- **make check** (WITH_CRIMSON, clang 21): 355/362 pass, including all 21 crimson, SeaStore and Seastar unit tests.
  - Not passing, none related to this PR:
    - 5 dashboard/grafana/promql tox jobs: old pinned deps on the host's Python 3.12.
    - `run-promtool-unittests`: promtool 3.15 on the host.
    - `unittest_objecter_direct_reads`: did not build on main at the time; fixed since by 9b82b84a844.
  - Built without `-Werror`: clang 21 with libstdc++ 15 warns in code this PR does not touch.
- **Not tested**:
  - aarch64.
  - The `WITH_DPDK` async messenger.

Signed-off-by: Shai Fultheim <shai.fultheim@gmail.com>

73143.title: test/osd: do not expect the size-optimal score to differ from the fair one
73143.author: tchaikov
73143.body:
`rb_osdsize_opt_score` fails now and then, since `calc_pg_upmaps()` shuffles with an unseeded engine, so `balance_capacity()` leaves a different map on each run. The fair score is computed from primaries and the size-optimal one from loads, and both are rounded to two decimals, so they can be equal: with 15 primaries on the busiest of 5 OSDs, both round to 1.15.

Check that the score is the busiest OSD's load relative to the average load instead, which holds for any map.

73145.title: [DNM]Crimson: route repops to the replica PG's reactor, optionally with aligned PG placement
73145.author: mohit84
73145.body:
Stacked on #72975 and #72581 (reuses the reactor-port listener); only the last 4 commits are new.
### Problem
With cluster lanes the primary sends a repop from the PG's reactor, but the replica accepts it
on any reactor and forwards ~88% of repops to the reactor that runs the PG.

### Changes (both options default off)
- `crimson_osd_cluster_shard_ports`: the replica names its PG reactor's cluster port in
  MOSDRepOpReply (v3, byte-identical v2 when unset); the primary sends that PG's later repops
  there. Repops forwarded 88% -> 0%. No osdmap change; peers need not have the same reactor count.
- `crimson_osd_align_pg_cores`: a new PG is placed on reactor (ps + pool) % reactors on every
  OSD, so cross-reactor traffic concentrates on matching reactor pairs. Applies to PGs created
  with the option on.

### Results (16 img 4k randwrite QD8, 3 OSDs x 8 reactors, client routing on, primaries balanced)
| placement | replica routing | IOPS | CPU/op | p99 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| default | off | 23,190 | 868 us | 14.9 ms |
| default | on  | 23,882 (+3.0%) | 850 us (-2.1%) | 15.7 ms |
| aligned | off | 23,973 (+3.4%) | 851 us (-2.0%) | 15.0 ms |
| aligned | on  | **25,062 (+8.1%)** | **828 us (-4.6%)** | 15.9 ms |
