73147.title: rgw/s3select: reject invalid CLI scan ranges without throwing
73147.author: yixiaodan
73147.body:
## Summary

`RGWSelectObj_ObjStore_S3::handle_aws_cli_parameters()` parsed the
user-controlled `<Start>`/`<End>` tags of an S3 Select query with
`std::stol()`. Invalid values throw `std::invalid_argument`, which is not
caught on the request path: the exception escapes the asio coroutine and
terminates the radosgw process. Because parsing ran before the
`rgw_disable_s3select` check, the crash is reachable even when S3 Select is
disabled.

## Changes

- Parse the tags with `ceph::parse<int64_t>()`, which rejects non-numeric
  input and trailing characters without throwing; reject negative values
  and `end < start` explicitly.
- Move the `rgw_disable_s3select` check ahead of `get_params()`.
- Propagate `get_params()` failures instead of ignoring the return value.
- Return proper RGW error codes (`-EINVAL`, `-ERR_INVALID_REQUEST`,
  `-ERR_TOO_LARGE`) instead of a bare `-1`/`-ERANGE`.

## Testing

Verified on a single-node v21.3.0 build (`vstart.sh` with mon + osd + mgr +
radosgw):

- Before the fix, a malformed scan range aborts radosgw in the
  `io_context_pool` thread.
- After the fix, malformed values are rejected with `-EINVAL` when S3 Select
  is enabled, and with `-ERR_INVALID_REQUEST` when it is disabled; the
  process stays up in both cases.
- Valid scan ranges still process normally (200, no error).
- `make check` was not run locally; the touched target built successfully
  with `-DWITH_TESTS=OFF`.

Note on the tracker: `tracker.ceph.com` is unreachable from this environment,
so a tracker ticket could not be opened. The commit references the commit that
introduced the regression, as described in `SubmittingPatches.rst`. I can open
a tracker ticket and add a `Fixes:` URL if maintainers prefer that.

73148.title: os/bluestore: Add alloc_tag_t tagging support to Allocator allocate and init_rm_free interfaces.
73148.author: Jayaprakash-ibm
73148.body:
Extended the `Allocator::allocate` and `Allocator::init_rm_free` base class interfaces to accept a new data tag parameter, `alloc_tag_t` (defaulted to unknown), to enable tag-aware spatial partitioning and accounting.

`alloc_tag_t` Bit Layout & Encoding

```

  63      60 59      56 55                  32 31                             0
 +----------+----------+----------------------+--------------------------------+
 |   kind   | subkind  |     reserved/zero    |         reserved/zero          |
 +----------+----------+----------------------+--------------------------------+

 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  BIT LAYOUT BY KIND
 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  1. UNKNOWN (Default / Safe State)
  63      60 59                                                               0
 +----------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
 |  0x0000  |                         all bits are 0                           |
 +----------+------------------------------------------------------------------+


  2. BLUESTORE_META (Labels / Reserved Boot Regions)
  63      60 59                                                               0
 +----------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
 |   0x1    |                         all bits are 0                           |
 +----------+------------------------------------------------------------------+

  3. PG (RADOS Object User Data)
  63      60 59      52 51                  32 31                             0
 +----------+----------+----------------------+--------------------------------+
 |   0x3    |  zeros   | pool_id (low 20 bits)|       pg_seed (32 bits)        |
 +----------+----------+----------------------+--------------------------------+

  4. BLUEFS (RocksDB / Journal)
  63      60 59      56 55                                                    0
 +----------+----------+-------------------------------------------------------+
 |   0x2    | subkind* |                         zeros                         |
 +----------+----------+-------------------------------------------------------+
              *subkind: OTHER (0x0) | WAL (0x1) | SST (0x2) | LOG (0x3)
 
 ```
 Current Layout :
 
1.  kind (bits [63:60])
`0x0` : `UNKNOWN`: Default zero-initialized state; safely ignored by non-tag-aware allocators.
`0x1` : `BLUESTORE_META`: Space reserved for OSD Label.
`0x2` : `BLUEFS`: Space belonging to the BlueFS and RocksDB files.
`0x3` : `PG`: Space belonging to PG collections (standard object data).
`0x4..0xF`: Reserved for future top level kinds.

2. Kind-Specific Layouts (bits [59:0])
   Depending on the value of `kind`, the remaining 60 bits are interpreted differently:
   1. When `kind` is `BLUEFS` (`0x2`)
      1. bits [59:56] (4 bits) :  `subkind` :
         1. `0x0` : `OTHER`: Default.
         2. `0x1` : `WAL`: RocksDB WAL.
         3. `0x2` : `SST`: RocksDB SST files.
         4. `0x3` : `LOG`: log (`ino == 1`).
         5. `0x4`–`0xF` : Reserved.
      2. bits [55:0] (56 bits) : Reserved and padded with zeros.
   2. When `kind` is `PG` (`0x3`)
       1. bits [59:52] : Reserved and padded with zeros.
       2. bits [51:32] : `pool_id`: Stores the lowest 20 bits of the pool identifier (pg_t::m_pool).
       3. bits [31:0]  : `pg_seed`: Stores the 32-bit placement group seed hash (pg_t::m_seed).

Propagated  `PG`, `BLUESTORE_META`, and `BLUEFS` subkind tags (`WAL` / `SST`/ `LOG` / `OTHER`) through all runtime allocation, append, preallocation, and mount/boot initialization paths in `BlueStore` and `BlueFS`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80808

73154.title: mon: osd pool migrate takes the defaults, gains --inherit-params and is safe to run again
73154.author: aainscow
73154.body:
Stacked on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/69112 (pool migration, at 566b09e1de6): only the last five commits are new.

`osd pool migrate` with no options created a copy of the source pool and needed `--yes-i-really-mean-it`, while a
migrate with any option took the defaults for every option not given. `pools.rst` said the opposite: that options
not given came from the source pool. Even the copy lost the settings that `osd pool create` does not take, such as
EC optimizations, min_size, flags, pool options, applications and quotas.

With this PR:

- `ceph osd pool migrate <pool>` with no options creates the pool that `ceph osd pool create` would create with no
  options, as for any other migrate, and needs no confirmation.
- `ceph osd pool migrate <pool> --inherit-params` gives the new pool all of the source pool's settings, so the
  migration copies every object to a new pool without changing it. This is usually needed only by support or by
  test tools. For now it cannot be combined with any other pool parameter (EINVAL).
- `ceph osd pool migrate` is safe to run again. The monitors run a command again when an election cancels its
  reply, and the rerun used to fail with EINVAL although the migration had started. On a pool that is already
  being migrated:
  - with `--inherit-params`, it succeeds without changing anything, whatever the pool is being migrated to (on a
    pool that is not being migrated, `--inherit-params` always starts a new migration);
  - otherwise, it succeeds without changing anything if it asks for the settings that the pool is being migrated
    to (the pool type, erasure code profile, CRUSH rule, size and EC optimizations that its arguments and the
    defaults give, and each other argument given), and is refused, as before, if not.
- A migrate of a pool prepared in the same pending update as an earlier migrate of it now waits for that update.
  It used to rename the pool a second time, find the earlier migration's target under the pool's name, answer
  that the pool already exists and drop the pool's pending rename, so the update made two pools of the same name.

`ceph_test_rados` and the librados and standalone tests that relied on the old copy now pass `--inherit-params`. The
dashboard's migrate call is unchanged: with no options it now gets the defaults, as its help text already says.

`ceph_test_rados --migration-pg-count` and `--migration-enable-ec-optimizations` sent only that option, so every
other setting took its default: an EC pool was migrated to a replicated one and `ceph_test_rados` aborted, or the
migrate was refused for asking for EC optimizations on a replicated pool. They now send the pool's own type, erasure
code profile, EC optimizations and, for a replicated pool, size with the change.

The commit "qa/standalone: fix TEST_osd_pool_create_migrate_from" fixes that test, which could not pass: it slept
10 s for a merge from 32 PGs to 2, so the migration was refused with EBUSY, and it looked up the source pool's id in
the plain `ceph osd dump`, which does not list the source of a migration.

Tested: full build (gcc, Debug) on top of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72977. The new mon-only
`TEST_pool_migrate_inherit_params`: a migrate with no options turns an EC pool into a replicated one;
`--inherit-params` with `--size` is refused and leaves the pool alone; `--inherit-params` of an EC pool with EC
optimizations, overwrites, min_size, nodelete, noscrub, compression, an application and a quota gives a new pool
whose `ceph osd dump` entry matches the source's except for its id, name, creation and migration fields.
`TEST_pool_migrate_again`: a rerun of a migrate succeeds and starts nothing, a migrate asking for something else is
refused, `--inherit-params` on a migrating pool succeeds and starts nothing whatever the migration is to, and
`--inherit-params` with another parameter is refused with "cannot be combined". `TEST_pool_migrate_twice_in_one_update`:
two migrates of one pool 1 s apa

73160.title: osd/PeeringState: do not backfill the last recovery sources
73160.author: aainscow
73160.body:
An up OSD that has fallen behind the authoritative log is made a backfill target, and `activate()` resets it to
`last_backfill` MIN. From then on `missing_loc` does not count it as a location of any object, in that or any later
interval, although it still holds the objects. When such OSDs hold the only copies of objects that the acting set is
missing, or for EC the chunks that it needs, those objects become unfound and stay unfound. In
https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82013 two strays held the only copies while recovery was pending, the log was trimmed
past them, and the thrasher's reweights moved them back into the up set one epoch apart.

The fix: once `GetMissing` has the missing sets of the acting set, a backfill target that may hold an object the acting
set cannot recover by itself is kept out of backfill, as a stray that remains a recovery source. When recovery
completes, the primary reverts to the up set to start a new interval in which the deferred OSDs are backfilled,
together with any other backfill targets.

The first three commits let the peering test fixture run replicated pools: a pool-independent `PeeringTestFixture` is
split out of `ECPeeringTestFixture` (mostly moved code), and `ReplicaPeeringTestFixture` is added next to it. The tests
in the last commit fail without the fix.

Straight `git cherry-pick -x` of the single commit in #70127; it applies cleanly to current squid and also to the head of #72985, which touches a different arm of the same `case` statement. squid never used `llvm.sh` at all (`run-make.sh` installs the distro `clang` package via install-deps.sh and `lib-build.sh` picks the newest `clang-N` present), so on squid the only effect of this change is to stop requesting `software-properties-common` where it does not exist; the `clang-19` it installs instead is what trixie ships natively.

73164.title: [draft] OSD Direct OOB RDMA
73164.author: mmgaggle
73164.body:
## Summary

This pull request carries the complete S3 over RDMA series in one branch. Reviewers can review and test the feature as a whole. RFC [#71209](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71209) holds the design discussion. The parts can also go in one at a time, in the order of the table below.

A client with RDMA sends a normal S3 GET or PUT, plus an `x-amz-rdma-token` header that names a window of its memory. The gateway puts the token in the RADOS ops that it sends. For a GET, the OSDs write the object data straight into the client's window. For a PUT, the primary OSD pulls the payload out of the client's window. The object data does not go through the gateway. The client and the gateway agree on the result with the `x-amz-rdma-reply` header and a CRC-64/NVME or CRC-32C checksum of the bytes that moved.

The transports are libfabric (through the ofi-rma library), cuObject, and an RC service in the gateway for clients without libfabric. The feature is off by default, because `oob_client_transports` is empty by default. The libfabric transport also needs the build option `WITH_OOB_OFI`, which is off by default. The RC service builds with `WITH_RDMA_RC`, and `WITH_RDMA` turns that option on by default. Stock clients never send a delivery descriptor. An OSD without a transport declines each delivery, and the client then uses the normal path.

## Parts

| Part | Last commit | What it adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #70458 | `025cb44b927` | Mark Kogan's experimental cuObject S3 RDMA server, the 206 reply to a ranged GET, and the optional cuObject build. |
| P0 | `062c5548be3` | Eight fixes. Seven apply to main alone, and P0.7 needs P0.3. See the list below. |
| P1 | `8bdd50b29a1` | CRC-64/NVME with ISA-L, and the combination of CRCs. |
| P2 | `172bceb4d52` | The common out-of-band layer: configuration, the locked memory arena, and the token parsers. |
| P3 | `3a115c2f02e` | The ofi-rma submodule and the `WITH_OOB_OFI` build option, off by default. |
| P4 | `6435e34989b` | Delivery descriptors on `MOSDOp` and results on `MOSDOpReply`, with the librados and Objecter calls and the pool options. |
| P5 | `ee31c1164d4` | The OSD writes a read's data into the client's window. |
| P6 | `5ab325f28d7` | The primary OSD pulls a write's payload out of the client's window. |
| P7 | `87940807745` | The gateway: OSD-direct GET and PUT, checksum headers, window fences, and rate limits. |
| P8 | `1479944bd9b` | BlueStore reads straight into the out-of-band arena, with no copy. |
| P9 | `7f33e7aaaf6` | The RC service for clients without libfabric. |
| P10 | `1971d0c3f82` | Teuthology suites, tasks and workunits. |
| cephadm | `0e0be3200c2` | An `oob` section in the RGW and OSD specs: RDMA devices, memlock and raw sockets, with the deployment doc. |

Each P0 fix also has a pull request of its own, on main:

1. #73172: `blk/spdk: return NVMe I/O errors and do not use a freed IOContext`
2. #73173: `test/osd: build MockPeeringListener.cc into pg_backend_test_fixture`
3. #73193: `osd: free the stack of an EC coroutine op and keep its sync reads in it`
4. #73175: `osd: repair an EC shard whose read failed with a media error`, with the new option `osd_ec_repair_on_read`
5. #73176: `osd: count and log the EC direct reads that bounce to the primary`
6. #73177: `osd: do not answer an op twice when a nested read goes to repair`
7. #73178: `osd: give the ops of a nested do_osd_ops() call finishers of their own`, on top of #73193
8. #73179: `osd: wait for the last commits of the PGs before the op threads stop`

`doc/radosgw/s3-rdma.rst` describes the design, the deployment and the operation. The cephadm docs, `pools.rst`, `health-checks.rst` and `PendingReleaseNotes` have the other changes.

## Testing

On October 27, I rebased the branch onto main `169a0fb3a86`. The tests ran on Fedora with `WITH_OOB_OFI` on. On the rebased branch, the results are as follows:

- 32 test binaries pass with 1841 tests. These include `uni

73166.title: crimson/os/seastore: add timers for OOL and journal write phases
73166.author: shreya-subramanian
73166.body:
When SeaStore submits a transaction, most of the time goes into two
disk writes: the OOL write (the data itself) and the journal write (a
record of what changed). Until now each of these was one number, so
there was no way to tell how much was waiting, how much was our own
code, and how much was the disk.

This PR adds timers that split both writes into parts. They are
reported as new labels on the existing per-stage latency
histograms.

## New stages

OOL write (part of `submit_ool_write`):
- `submit_ool_throttle`: waiting for the throttle before writing
- `submit_ool_prepare`: building the list of writes and merging buffers
- `submit_ool_disk_write`: sending the writes until they all finish

Journal write (part of `submit_journal`):
- `submit_journal_batch_wait`: waiting for a free journal write slot
- `submit_journal_disk_write`: the journal write itself, split into:
  - `submit_journal_pre_dma`: our code before `dma_write` is called
  - `submit_journal_dma`: the device doing the write
  - `submit_journal_post_dma`: after the device is done, before we notice
- `submit_journal_finalize_wait`: waiting for earlier records to finish
- `submit_complete_commit`: making the changes visible in the cache

Ticket:[[IBMCEPH-16236] Investigate Transaction Phases: Submit Path Breakdown - Jira](https://ibm-ceph.atlassian.net/browse/IBMCEPH-16236)

gist example: findings [SeaStore submit path breakdown (OOL + journal) on NVMe with crimson-store-bench: 4 KiB random write, 30 s](https://gist.github.com/shreya-subramanian/19ca802927e9c1d06a0f6f210d21c1f8)

73171.title: mds: flush the journal when a rename waits for an unjournaled update
73171.author: dvanders
73171.body:
Renaming a file that a client has just written, into a directory on another active rank, waits a full `mds_tick_interval` (5 s). Workloads that write output and move it into a tree pinned to another rank pay this on every file.

Each of the waits is for an update that has been submitted to the journal but not flushed. Nothing asks for a flush, so it waits for the tick. A rename can hit more than one of them, one tick each:

- `handle_peer_rename_prep()` freezes the renamed inode on the rank that owns it. The client's flush of its dirty caps on the file holds an auth pin on the inode in `_do_cap_update()` until it is journaled, and the freeze waits for that. Now the log is flushed when the freeze has to wait, and `_do_cap_update()` asks for a flush when the inode is being frozen, in case the cap flush arrives after the freeze started.
- The destination rank also discovers the just-created source dentry, and `handle_discover()` blocks on its xlock, which the create holds until it is journaled. The log is nudged there too.
- A rename whose leader replies early leaves its log unflushed, while a witness keeps the rename's locks until the leader commits. A request on the witness's rank that needs one of those locks, such as the client's lookup of the new name, waits for that commit, and `nudge_log()` there only flushes the witness's own log. The leader now flushes after an early reply when the request has witnesses. (Found by @xiubli.)

Two active ranks, `/src` on rank 0 and `/dst` pinned to rank 1; write 4 KiB or 1 MiB, close, rename into `/dst`, on a vstart cluster:

| | before | after | same-rank rename |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, ceph-fuse | 4.9-5.0 s | 16-110 ms | 19 ms |
| main, ceph-fuse, `mds_tick_interval` 10 | 10 s | 80-100 ms | |
| Reef 18.2.8, kernel client | 2.8-5.0 s (p90 up to 8.3 s) | 140-155 ms | 3 ms |
| Reef 18.2.8, ceph-fuse | 3.5-4.6 s | 170-210 ms | 37 ms |

@xiubli's runs on kernel 7.2 and ceph-fuse saw two tick waits per rename, about 10 s, and 130-190 ms median with these changes (see his review).

For the early-reply flush: clients rename their oldest file into another client's directory, with the client directories pinned alternately to the two ranks (libcephfs, memstore, 8 clients set up). Three runs before and two after:

| active clients | | renames/s | p50 | p99 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | before | 3.7-7.7 | 7.0-7.4 ms | 5.1 s | 5.1 s |
| | after | 162-166 | 6.5-6.7 ms | 11 ms | 20-26 ms |
| 4 | before | 284-364 | 8.4-8.7 ms | 18-19 ms | 4.5-4.9 s |
| | after | 517-520 | 7.4 ms | 15-16 ms | 28-32 ms |
| 8 | before | 1780-1845 | 4.6-4.8 ms | 8.4-9.1 ms | 40-45 ms |
| | after | 1666-1732 | 4.8-5.0 ms | 10-11 ms | 47 ms |

Writing a file and renaming it straight into the other rank's directory is unchanged by it (130 renames/s with 1 client, max 21-34 ms).

(The kernel client couldn't mount the main vstart cluster: its AES-256 cephx keys, and with an AES-128 key the 6.8 kernel saw no active MDS. The code the first two items change is the same on Reef and main.)

The new `TestExports.test_rename_just_written_file_across_ranks` sets `mds_tick_interval` to 10 and fails if any of ten such renames takes 5 s or more. I ran its steps by hand against both builds (10 s before, 0.1 s after); I couldn't run it under vstart_runner, which needs teuthology.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82190

73172.title: blk/spdk: return NVMe I/O errors and do not use a freed IOContext
73172.author: mmgaggle
73172.body:
## Summary

`io_complete()` asserted that every NVMe completion succeeded, so a media error crashed the OSD. Now `read()` returns -EIO, and an aio fails an IOContext that allows EIO, as `KernelDevice` does.

The last aio callback can free the IOContext. A write released its buffers after that callback, and `_aio_handle()` read `num_running` after it. Now neither does.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82191

## Testing

I did not build this change with `WITH_SPDK=ON`. No automated test covers this path, because it needs an NVMe device bound to SPDK.

73173.title: test/osd: build MockPeeringListener.cc into pg_backend_test_fixture
73173.author: mmgaggle
73173.body:

`OsdTestFixture` owns a `MockPeeringListener`, and `PGBackendTestFixture.cc` destroys it. Only `ec_peering_test_fixture` built `MockPeeringListener.cc`, so `unittest_backend_basics` did not link (no vtable for `MockPeeringListener`).

This builds it in `pg_backend_test_fixture`, which every user of `ec_peering_test_fixture` also links.

73174.title: osd: free the stack of an EC coroutine op and keep its sync reads in it
73174.author: mmgaggle
73174.body:
## Summary

An op that ended without a yield dropped the last reference to its coroutine inside the coroutine, so its 128 KiB stack leaked. Now `resume_coroutine()` holds a reference across the resume.

The op also kept handles into the freed stack, and a later sync read yielded on them. Now the coroutine clears them, and waits for the op's async reads itself. If an op before the CALL started those reads before any sync read, the coroutine waits for them too. At shutdown, the PG now also frees a suspended coroutine.

The open #72704 fixes the first leak in the same way. Its tracker is [81777](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81777). #72704 does not fix the handles, the async reads or the shutdown. The two conflict in `Coroutines.h`, `PrimaryLogPG.cc` and `src/test/osd/CMakeLists.txt`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82192

## Testing

On main 169a0fb3a86, with the other seven P0 fixes, the new `unittest_ec_coroutines` passes its 5 tests:

- `FinishWithoutYieldFreesStack`
- `FinishAfterYieldFreesStack`
- `StoppedWhileSuspendedFreesStack`
- `ManyOpsKeepNoStacks`
- `NoHandlesOutliveTheCoroutine`

73175.title: osd: repair an EC shard whose read failed with a media error
73175.author: mmgaggle
73175.body:
## Summary

The EC primary decoded a client read around a shard that failed with EIO, and only logged a warning. Now a clean PG marks the object missing on that shard and recovers it.

- A new option, `osd_ec_repair_on_read`, turns it on. It is on by default, as read repair is in a replicated pool.
- Only a PG with k+1 shards that the read did not find damaged repairs.
- The new counter `ec_read_repair` counts the repairs.
- A shard that finds a corrupt object info now sends its EIO with no data. The primary asserts on an object with an error and data.
- `PendingReleaseNotes` names the option.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82193

## Testing

These tests pass on main 169a0fb3a86, with the other seven P0 fixes:

- `test-erasure-eio.sh`: the new `TEST_ec_repair_on_read` passes.
- `TestBackendBasics.cc`: four new `TestECFailover` cases pass: `MediaErrorIsReportedForRepair`, `MediaErrorOnThePrimaryShardIsReported`, `OtherReadErrorsAreNotReportedForRepair` and `FastReadLateMediaErrorIsReported`.

73176.title: osd: count and log the EC direct reads that bounce to the primary
73176.author: mmgaggle
73176.body:
## Summary

Since #72292, an EC direct read that fails with EIO on its shard goes back to the client with EAGAIN. The client then sends the read to the primary, which decodes the data from the other shards. Only a debug log line shows such a bounce, so a damaged shard that clients read again and again stays hidden.

- The shard counts each bounce in the new perf counter `ec_direct_read_redirect_eio`, and writes it to the OSD log.
- The cluster log gets a warning at the 1st, 2nd, 4th and 8th bounce of each PG, and at each later power of two. A damaged shard thus does not flood the cluster log.
- If `fiemap` fails with EIO, a sparse direct read also bounces.
- A sparse direct read skips the whole-object digest check, because the digest does not cover the chunks of one shard.

The answer to the client still comes from `rep_repair_primary_object()`, as in #72292. `direct_reads.rst` describes the bounce.

## Testing

With only this change on main 169a0fb3a86, the new tests in `test-erasure-eio.sh` pass, and so does `TEST_ec_direct_read_eio` from #72292:

- `TEST_rados_get_direct_read_eio_shard_0`
- `TEST_rados_get_direct_read_eio_shard_1`
- `TEST_rados_get_direct_read_eio_single_chunk`
- `TEST_rbd_export_direct_read_eio_sparse`

The tests inject the error into the data of a shard. No test covers the `fiemap` case.

73177.title: osd: do not answer an op twice when a nested read goes to repair
73177.author: mmgaggle
73177.body:
## Summary

`rep_repair_primary_object()` answers EAGAIN to a failed read on a replica or, since #72292, on an EC shard. On the primary, it makes the op wait for the repair. A read in a CALL does not always return the EAGAIN, so `execute_ctx()` answered the op again.

Now the replica or the shard marks its reply as sent, and `execute_ctx()` does not answer an op that has its reply. On the primary, a waiting op drops the result of its run (`parked_for_repair`). A second failed read in the same run does not put the op in a second wait list.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82194

## Testing

This pull request adds no test of its own. With only this change on main 169a0fb3a86, the EIO tests of `test-erasure-eio.sh` pass.

73178.title: osd: give the ops of a nested do_osd_ops() call finishers of their own
73178.author: mmgaggle
73178.body:
## Summary

`do_osd_ops()` numbered the ops of a nested call, such as the reads of a CALL's method, from 0, as for the request. On an optimized EC pool, the nested read of a CALL after a READ or a CHECKSUM ran the finisher of the request's op 0. The method then got no data.

A nested call now keeps its finishers for the op that made it, and gives the caller's loop its op number back.

This pull request is on top of #73174, because its test also needs that fix. Only the last commit is new here.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82195

## Testing

The new librados test `LibRadosMiscECPP.ClassReadAfterAsyncRead` in `ceph_test_rados_api_misc_pp` runs a CHECKSUM and then a CALL that reads the object. These runs were on a vstart cluster with 3 OSDs, on main 169a0fb3a86:

- With this branch, the test passes on both pools with EC optimizations.
- With all eight P0 fixes, it also passes.
- With only the last commit, without #73174, two of the three OSDs stopped with SIGSEGV in `jump_fcontext`. The CALL's read yielded on the handles of a coroutine that already finished, which #73174 fixes.

73179.title: osd: wait for the last commits of the PGs before the op threads stop
73179.author: mmgaggle
73179.body:
## Summary

In a slow shutdown (`osd_fast_shutdown=false`), a PG was sometimes still referenced at its detach in `OSD::shutdown()` ("has ref count of 2"). `BlueStore::umount()` then failed its assert on the reference count of the PG's collection.

The map that marks the stopping OSD down starts a new interval in each PG, just as the shutdown begins. The on-commit callback of that peering transaction holds a FlushState, and the FlushState holds the PG. `PG::shutdown()` waits until the transactions of the PG are submitted, not until they commit.

The store queues the on-commit callbacks of a PG to the context queue of its shard. The op threads of a stopping OSD delete them. When the commit came after the op threads stopped, its callback stayed in the queue and kept the PG and its collection past the umount.

Now `OSD::shutdown()` waits until the transactions of each PG committed, after it shut the PGs down and while the op threads still run. The op threads delete the waiter instead of running it, so the waiter signals at its release. The wait takes as long as the last commits, a few milliseconds.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82196

## Testing

The assert showed in the slow-stop standalone tests of the S3 over RDMA series (#73164). Before the fix, 3 of 20 runs of one of these tests hit the assert at umount. After it, all 60 runs of three such tests passed. Those runs were on an older main. This pull request adds no test.

73186.title: mds: prepare fresh stray dentry instead of asserting on stale one
73186.author: xiubli
73186.body:
prepare_stray_dentry() caches the stray dentry it prepares in
  mdr->straydn before all the locks of the request are held.  If the
  request is then deferred through one of the drop-locks paths in
  Locker::acquire_locks() (for example an auth pin that fails because the
  source dirfrag is being fragmented), all its locks, including the xlock
  on the destination dentry, are dropped while mdr->straydn stays.  When
  a concurrent rename replaces the destination inode in the meantime, the
  retried request calls prepare_stray_dentry() for the new victim, finds
  the cached stray dentry named after the old victim's inode number and
  hits:

      FAILED ceph_assert(straydn->get_name() == straydname)

  This is reachable with fully synchronous client dirops (wsync), since
  all the deferral points are inside the MDS.  It was reported on 20.2.x
  in production (many clients renaming onto the same target names in one
  directory) and reproduced on 18.2.8.

  Instead of asserting, unpin and clear the stale cached stray dentry and
  prepare a fresh one for the current victim, the same way
  handle_client_rename() already drops mdr->straydn when the destination
  is gone.

  A qa test is added to tasks.cephfs.test_strays: 4 clients run 16
  writers each, renaming new files onto 8 shared names in one directory,
  plus readers of those names, for 300 seconds while the directory keeps
  being split and merged (mds_bal_split_size 10, mds_bal_merge_size 2,
  mds_bal_fragment_interval 1) with 2 active MDS.

  Testing (vstart_runner, local):
  - without the fix: rank 0 aborted on the assert after about 70 seconds
    (backtrace via Locker::handle_client_caps -> Locker::eval, as in the
    tracker), and the standby that took over aborted the same way;
  - with the fix: the test passes, about 100k renames, 251 directory
    splits, and the stale stray dentry was replaced 21 times.

  The fix was also tested on 18.2.8 with the reproducer from the tracker
  (16 kernel mounts, 64 writers): 20 minutes, 53,677 renames, 331 splits
  and 1,036 merges, no crash; unpatched it crashed after 12 s and after
  8 min in two runs.

  Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79321

73190.title: mds: do not start a segment at a test subtree map
73190.author: xiubli
73190.body:
With `mds_debug_subtrees` set, `MDLog::_segment_upkeep()` journals an
`ESubtreeMap` of type `EVENT_SUBTREEMAP_TEST` after every event so that
replay can check the subtree state.  It is meant not to be a segment
boundary, and it was not one until a76421a9beb ("mds: add minor
LogSegment boundaries") made the boundary test a
`dynamic_cast<SegmentBoundary*>`, which every `ESubtreeMap` passes.
Since then each test map starts a new major segment, so the MDS opens a
segment for every second event, falls behind on trimming and keeps
growing the journal.  The squid `vstart.sh` still sets
`mds_debug_subtrees=true` unconditionally, so every squid vstart cluster
hits this.

### Testing

vstart, two active ranks plus a standby, memstore,
`mds_debug_subtrees=true`, 1500 mkdir/create/rename rounds on rank 0:

| rank 0 | events | segments | major segments |
|--------|-------:|---------:|---------------:|
| before | 22018  | 11010    | 10971          |
| after  | 22016  | 27       | 3              |

Journal replay (all MDSs killed with `kill -9`, then restarted) followed
by a rank 0 failover:

| journal written by → replayed by | result |
|---|---|
| new → new | OK, data intact, HEALTH_OK |
| old → new (upgrade) | OK, data intact; the old segments are trimmed afterwards |
| new → old (downgrade) | old MDS asserts in `EPurged::replay` (only with `mds_debug_subtrees`) |

qa run locally with `vstart_runner.py`:
- `test_misc.TestDebugSubtreesSegments` fails without the fix
  (`201 not less than 4`) and passes with it.
- All six tests that use `gen_health_warn_mds_trim()` pass:
  `TestFSFail.test_with_health_warn_trim`,
  `TestFSFail.test_when_other_FS_has_warn_TRIM`,
  `TestMDSFail.test_with_health_warn_trim`,
  `TestMDSFail.test_when_other_MDS_has_warn_TRIM`,
  `TestFSSetMaxMDS.test_when_mds_trim_without_confirm`,
  `TestFSSetMaxMDS.test_when_mds_trim_when_with_confirm`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82207

73196.title: crimson/net: don't write an ack frame for every received message
73196.author: mohit84
73196.body:
Acks aren't on the IO path. On a lossless connection the sender keeps each sent message until the peer acks it, so it can resend it after a reconnect; receiving an ack only frees those kept messages. Nothing waits for one: no op completion, throttle or send window depends on acks, so a later ack adds no latency.

Every outgoing message already carries the ack in its header (ack_seq = in_seq), yet each received message also woke the out dispatcher to write a standalone ack frame. On OSD-OSD connections about 4 of the 9 socket writes per replicated client write were ack-only, each also paying the receiver's TCP work on loopback.

Write a standalone ack only once ACK_BATCH (64) messages are unacked. With request/reply traffic (repop, then its reply) the next message carries the ack within a round trip, as before.

DNM:

* test_v2_lossless_connected_fault2 injects faults on ack frames and expects them to be written. Make ACK_BATCH a config option that the test reads, so it can set it to 1.

* if traffic stops with fewer than ACK_BATCH unacked, no ack is sent until the next message or a reconnect, so the peer keeps those messages with no time bound. Add a delayed ack: a short timer that writes the ack if no message carried it.

* add metrics once dep PR is merged.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82223

73197.title: crimson/os/seastore: keep SPDK io qpairs until the controller detaches
73197.author: fultheim
73197.body:
Split out of #73142 at review (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73142#pullrequestreview-5681722101), as the crimson runtime part.

The crimson-rados-experimental/spdk suite (#73198) found this bug, and its jobs cannot pass without the fix.

## The bug
- The device is opened and closed several times per shard during mkfs and mount. Each open allocated an io qpair in `start_shard()`, and each close freed it in `stop_shard()`.
- SPDK hands out the lowest free queue ID. So a freed queue ID went straight to the next qpair allocated, possibly on another shard.
- The kernel NVMe-oF target tears a queue down asynchronously, and meanwhile rejects a CONNECT for that queue ID (`nvmet: qid 1 has already been created`).
- crimson-osd then aborts on `ceph_assert(qpair)` in `start_shard()`, typically at mkfs. SPDK's own nvmf target did not show this.

## The fix
- One qpair per shard per controller, kept in the controller registry and shared by the `spdk_nvme_io` instances on the shard.
- Its completion poller runs while any of them uses it, and `spdk_nvme_detach()` frees it along with the controller.
- A reattach gets a new controller from the target, whose queue IDs cannot collide with a queue still being torn down.

## Testing
- x86_64, Rocky 10, 2 OSDs, `--smp 4`, NVMe/TCP to kernel nvmet: the four crimson-rados-experimental/spdk jobs (RANDOM_BLOCK and SEGMENTED × readwrite and rados_api_tests) pass with this fix and abort at mkfs without it.
- Those runs were on #73142's full branch, with SPDK v26.05. The fix only uses SPDK calls that are also in the v20.07 bundled on main (`spdk_nvme_ctrlr_alloc_io_qpair`, `spdk_nvme_qpair_process_completions`, `spdk_nvme_detach`).

Signed-off-by: Shai Fultheim <shai.fultheim@gmail.com>

73198.title: qa: add crimson SeaStore SPDK suite and spdk_nvmet_tcp task
73198.author: fultheim
73198.body:
Split out of #73142 at review (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73142#pullrequestreview-5681722101), as the crimson QA part.

Adds a teuthology suite that runs crimson SeaStore through SPDK's userspace NVMe/TCP initiator, against the kernel NVMe-oF target, so it runs on the usual nodes with LV scratch devices.

This PR does not depend on the others to merge, but its jobs only pass once both are in:
- #73142: packages built WITH_SPDK, with SPDK v26.05.
- #73197: the crimson SPDK qpair lifetime fix. Without it crimson-osd aborts at mkfs.

## Changes
- The `spdk_nvmet_tcp` task exports each OSD's scratch device through the kernel NVMe-oF target (`nvmet-tcp`) on 127.0.0.1. crimson-osd connects with SPDK's NVMe/TCP initiator.
  - No NVMe is detached from the kernel and no SPDK target app is needed.
  - The task reserves hugepages. Teardown removes the exports and restores hugepages.
- `ceph.py` skips the xfs mkfs for those OSDs and sets `seastore_spdk_transport_id`.
  - With no fresh fs mounted on the OSD data dir, it empties that dir before mkfs. Otherwise a node reused without a reimage keeps the last job's `mkfs_done`, and SeaStore skips mkfs and fails on the superblock.
- Suite `crimson-rados-experimental/spdk`: RANDOM_BLOCK and SEGMENTED × readwrite and rados_api_tests, on rocky_10.
  - RANDOM_BLOCK pins `seastore_cbjournal_size` to 1G. Each shard gets a journal of that size, and the 5G default outgrows small scratch devices.

## Testing
All on x86_64 (Rocky 10 host, kernel 7.2), with 2 OSDs, `--smp 4`, and NVMe/TCP to kernel nvmet on loop-device scratch disks, on #73142's full branch (this suite, the fix, and SPDK v26.05 packaging together).

- **Teuthology**: the four suite jobs, run with teuthology itself against a local Rocky 10 node:
  - SEGMENTED readwrite: pass, `rados` 4000 ops with 0 errors, scrub check OK.
  - RANDOM_BLOCK readwrite: pass, same.
  - SEGMENTED rados_api_tests: pass, all `rados/test.sh` suites including the valgrind leak test.
  - RANDOM_BLOCK rados_api_tests: pass, same.
  - The nodes kept the previous job's OSD data dirs, so each run also exercised the `ceph.py` cleanup.
  - Teardown left no nvmet subsystems or ports and gave back all hugepages.
  - These runs used 40G scratch devices and the 5G journal default; the 1G pin came after them.
- **vstart-driven task runs** (the `spdk_nvmet_tcp` task against a vstart cluster, RANDOM_BLOCK with `seastore_cbjournal_size=1G`):
  - readwrite: 6/6 RANDOM_BLOCK, 6/6 SEGMENTED.
  - rados_api_tests: pass on both.
- **Not tested**: aarch64, a Sepia lab run.

Signed-off-by: Shai Fultheim <shai.fultheim@gmail.com>

73199.title: [RFC] mon: do not drop or widen caps for existing entites in `fs authorize`

73200.title: rgw: send Content-Range with 416 InvalidRange responses
73200.author: RaminNietzsche
73200.body:
A GetObject whose `Range` cannot be satisfied is answered 416 with no `Content-Range`. RFC 9110 [14.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-14.4) and [15.5.17](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-15.5.17) say a server answering 416 to a byte-range request should send the complete length as `Content-Range: bytes */<length>`, and AWS S3 does; clients that resume downloads read the object size from it.

The S3 and Swift `send_response_data()` return on error before they dump the range. When the range parsed and the object turned out too short or empty, this sends the unsatisfied-range form with the object size. A range that did not parse also ends in `-ERANGE` (with `rgw_ignore_get_invalid_range=false`), but the object has not been read at that point, so no size is sent for it.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82229

## Testing

On a single-host vstart cluster built from this branch (on main, the 416 answers carry no `Content-Range`; see the tracker):

| Request | Answer |
|---------|--------|
| S3, 10-byte object, `Range: bytes=100-200` | 416, `Content-Range: bytes */10` |
| S3, empty object, `Range: bytes=0-1` | 416, `Content-Range: bytes */0` |
| S3, `Range: bytes=5-9` | 206, `Content-Range: bytes 5-9/10` |
| S3, `Range: bytes=9-3` (does not parse) | 416, no `Content-Range` |
| Swift, 10-byte object, `Range: bytes=100-200` | 416, `Content-Range: bytes */10` |
| Swift, `Range: bytes=2-3` | 206, `Content-Range: bytes 2-3/10` |

s3-tests: `test_ranged_request_invalid_range` and `test_ranged_request_empty_object` now assert the header; `-k test_ranged_request` passes (5 tests).

73201.title: rgw: answer 412 when a CopyObject source precondition fails
73201.author: RaminNietzsche
73201.body:
A CopyObject whose `x-amz-copy-source-if-none-match` matches the source, or whose `x-amz-copy-source-if-modified-since` finds it unmodified, is answered 304 Not Modified. AWS answers 412 PreconditionFailed, and RFC 9110 [13.1.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-13.1.2) and [13.1.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-13.1.3) define 304 only for GET and HEAD.

- The driver evaluates the copy-source conditions with the read prepare used by GET, where these failures are `-ERR_NOT_MODIFIED`. `RGWCopyObj` now maps that to `-ERR_PRECONDITION_FAILED`, so every SAL driver and both the S3 and Swift copy paths answer 412. A system request with `copy-if-newer` still gets 304, which tells it the destination is already current.
- The D4N filter remapped this case itself, but assigned `ERR_PRECONDITION_FAILED` without the minus sign, so its copy returned a positive value. That remap is dropped.
- s3-tests: `fails_on_rgw` is removed from `test_copy_object_ifnonematch_good` (now passes) and `test_copy_object_ifmatch_failed` (already passed on main); new cases cover `If-None-Match: *` and `If-Modified-Since`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82230

## Testing

On a single-host vstart cluster:

| Condition | main | this branch |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `CopySourceIfNoneMatch=<etag of src>` | 304 | 412 PreconditionFailed |
| `CopySourceIfNoneMatch=*` | 304 | 412 PreconditionFailed |
| `CopySourceIfModifiedSince=2100-01-01` | 304 | 412 PreconditionFailed |
| `CopySourceIfModifiedSince=2000-01-01` | 200 | 200 |
| `CopySourceIfUnmodifiedSince=2000-01-01` | 412 | 412 |
| `CopySourceIfMatch="bad"` | 412 | 412 |
| `CopySourceIfNoneMatch="other"` | 200 | 200 |

s3-tests on this branch:
- `-k test_copy_object`: 7 passed (on main, `test_copy_object_ifnonematch_good` fails with 304).
- `-m "not fails_on_rgw" -k "(copy or ifmatch or ifnonematch or ifmodified or ifunmodified) and not enc"`: 59 passed.
- The SSE variants of `test_copy_enc` / `test_copy_part_enc` were not run meaningfully: the test cluster has no SSE-S3/KMS backend, so they fail with `InvalidArgument` before any precondition is evaluated.

The test build has D4N disabled, so the D4N change (removing three lines) was not compiled there.

73204.title: blk/spdk: restrict PCI device selection to PCIe transports
73204.author: next0262
73204.body:
https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82234

Replaces #63527, which was automatically closed as stale and cannot currently be reopened.

`spdk_pci_addr_parse()` accepts some IPv4 addresses, including `127.0.0.1`. When used with a TCP target, this sets `local_pci_device` and causes `spdk_nvme_probe()` to receive `NULL` instead of the TCP transport ID. OSD startup then fails to find the target.

Only parse PCI addresses for PCIe transports. The documented TCP example also needs `adrfam:IPv4`.

The original reproducer used three local SPDK NVMe-oF TCP targets and failed during OSD mkfs before the fix. OSD startup succeeded with the fix in the original 2025 run.

```
../src/vstart.sh --debug --new -x --localhost --bluestore \
--bluestore-spdk "trtype:tcp adrfam:IPv4 traddr:127.0.0.1 trsvcid:4420 subnqn:nqn.2019-02.io.spdk:cnode0,\
trtype:tcp adrfam:IPv4 traddr:127.0.0.1 trsvcid:4420 subnqn:nqn.2019-02.io.spdk:cnode1,\
trtype:tcp adrfam:IPv4 traddr:127.0.0.1 trsvcid:4420 subnqn:nqn.2019-02.io.spdk:cnode2"
```

Updated against current main, retaining the SPDK version guards and the corrected environment initialization order.

For this update, a standalone C++ check used the bundled SPDK address parser and the selection block extracted from NVMEDevice.cc. 73205.title: rgw: evaluate If-Match before If-Modified-Since on GET
73205.author: RaminNietzsche
73205.body:
## Summary

RFC 9110 [13.2.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-13.2.2) evaluates `If-Match` before `If-Modified-Since`. RGW checked date preconditions first in `Object::Read::prepare`, so GetObject with a failing `If-Match` and a future `If-Modified-Since` was answered **304** instead of **412**.

- Swap the entity-tag and date precondition blocks in the RADOS and POSIX read prepare paths. Guards that skip `If-Modified-Since` when `If-None-Match` is present (and `If-Unmodified-Since` when `If-Match` is present) are unchanged.
- s3-tests: `test_get_object_ifmatch_failed_with_ifmodifiedsince` (412) and `test_get_object_ifmatch_good_with_ifmodifiedsince_future` (304 when ETag matches).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82233  
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/19965

Probe script (case `T4 If-Match fails + If-Modified-Since future`): https://gist.github.com/RaminNietzsche/818ad8dd6b8d8093560183cd09d2b169

## Testing

On a single-host vstart cluster built from this branch (tree at `5ab2b0ddb70` + this commit):

| Request | main | this branch |
|---------|------|-------------|
| `If-Match: "ABCORZ"` + `If-Modified-Since: 2100-01-01` | 304 | 412 PreconditionFailed |
| `If-Match: <etag>` + `If-Modified-Since: 2100-01-01` | (304) | 304 |

s3-tests: `-k "test_get_object_ifmatch_failed_with_ifmodifiedsince or test_get_object_ifmatch_good_with_ifmodifiedsince_future"` — 2 passed.

73207.title: qa: tolerate concurrent distro logrotate run
73207.author: djgalloway
73207.body:
The ceph task's log rotater runs `logrotate /etc/logrotate.d/ceph-test.conf` every 30 seconds on every host. The distro's own daily `logrotate.service` includes `/etc/logrotate.d` too, so when it runs during a job it rotates and compresses the same ceph logs under the default state file. If the task's run starts while that lock is held, logrotate exits 3 with `state file /var/lib/logrotate/logrotate.status is already locked`. The rotater only tolerated the "renaming temp state file" message, so the greenlet died and the error was re-raised from `Rotater.end()` at teardown, failing jobs whose tests had passed.

Two triggers were seen on trial nodes:
- the 00:00 UTC daily run (all the Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 failures cluster between 00:00:11 and 00:01:41)
- a `Persistent=true` catch-up run on Rocky 10.2 hosts, whose image ships a stale `/var/lib/systemd/timers/stamp-logrotate.timer` (dated 2026-08-19), so the timer fires 3–60 minutes after boot, inside the first job after a reimage. On trial192 the system run held the lock for 71 seconds.

Only configs with a `log-rotate` key (fs/bugs clusters and `qa/clusters/2-node-mgr.yaml`, which rados/mgr symlinks) are exposed. 15 jobs in 676 runs between Oct 15 and Oct 28 hit this.

Skip the round when the lock is held; the system run rotates the same files, so nothing is lost. Exit code and message verified as root on a Rocky 10.2 trial node (logrotate 3.22.0).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82197

73208.title: [WIP][agent] mgr/cephadm: check hosts in parallel when a spec adds several hosts
73208.author: rkachach
73208.body:
## Problem

Adding hosts with a single spec file (`ceph orch apply -i hosts.yaml`) runs `cephadm check-host` on each host **one after the other**, and the orchestrator module's command thread waits for each one. On a 300-host scale test this apply took **~25 minutes**. Because a mgr module runs its commands one at a time on a single thread, every other `ceph orch` command waited behind it for the whole duration: `ceph orch ls` took 24m48s to return.

`dump_ops_in_flight` on the active mgr showed exactly this: the `orch apply` was running (`flag_point: orchestrator`, age 909s), and every other orch command was queued behind it (`flag_point: queued for module`), with their ages increasing:

| command | age | flag_point |
|---|---|---|
| `orch apply` | 909s | orchestrator |
| `orch host ls` | 898s | queued for module |
| `orch ls` | 890s | queued for module |
| `orch ls` | 204s | queued for module |
| `orch apply` | 69s | queued for module |

`py-spy` showed the thread running the apply waiting on a single host's check:

    _apply (cephadm/module.py) -> _add_host -> _check_valid_addr -> wait_async -> get_result

A slow or unreachable host made it worse: it held up every host after it, for up to `default_cephadm_command_timeout` (900s).

## Change

When the specs passed to `apply()` add **more than one host**:

1. **Resolve** each host's address synchronously, as today.
2. **Check** all of them **concurrently** on cephadm's event loop: at most `mgr/cephadm/max_parallel_host_checks` (default **10**) at a time, each bounded by the usual per-host timeout.
3. **Add** the hosts **one by one, in the original order**, as today. Each `_add_host()` receives its precomputed check result (the resolved address or the error) instead of running the check again.

Only the checks run concurrently. Everything that changes cluster state (inventory, crush buckets, offline hosts, sudo hardening, health checks) stays sequential and unchanged.

The batch has no overall timeout: each check is already bounded by its own `asyncio.wait_for()`, so a large batch is never cut short. The code uses `event_loop.get_result(..., None)` rather than `wait_async()`, because `wait_async()` would apply `default_cephadm_command_timeout` to the whole batch.

### Behaviour kept as before
- Results are returned in spec order, with the same messages.
- `continue_on_error` behaves the same. Without it, the apply stops at the first failing host, in spec order.
- Check failures, DNS failures and timeouts produce the same errors, including the `CEPHADM_HOST_TIMEOUT_ERROR` health warning.
- Re-adding a host with a new address still resets the cached SSH connection before it's checked, and again if the check fails.
- **Single-host specs and `ceph orch host add` don't change**: they never take the parallel path.
- **Hostnames listed more than once** and **invalid specs** are left out of the parallel checks and checked one by one, as before.

### New module option
| option | type | default | min |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mgr/cephadm/max_parallel_host_checks` | int | 10 | 1 |

It sets how many `check-host` calls run at the same time during a bulk host add. A limit is needed so we don't open hundreds of SSH sessions at once. Making it configurable lets admins lower it in environments where many concurrent new SSH connections are a problem, for example hosts reached through a jump host, whose sshd `MaxStartups` (default `10:30:100`) starts dropping connections beyond 10.

## Commits

1. **mgr/cephadm: split host address resolution from check-host.** Pure refactor: `_check_valid_addr()` is split into `_resolve_host_addr()` and an async `_check_host()`. No behaviour change.
2. **mgr/cephadm: check hosts in parallel when a spec adds several hosts.** The change described above, plus the new option.
3. **mgr/cephadm: fix "orch apply --no-overwrite" with hosts not yet added.** An independent, pre-existing bug found by the new tests. With `--n

73210.title: Rgw objects migration headers
73210.author: arttor
73210.body:
## Summary
Issue: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80329.

The PR adds a new system query param to RGW, `rgwx-mtime`, similar to the
existing `rgwx-version-id`. The goal is to help users migrate their S3 data
into Ceph. Keeping the original object timestamp is important for lifecycle
rules, which work on object age.

The second commit adds RGW regression tests for the new and the existing
system params.

Notes on the implementation:
- Works on PutObject and CompleteMultipartUpload, for system users only.
- The format is `<secs>[.<fraction>]`, the same as the `Rgwx-Mtime` response
  header. A malformed value returns InvalidArgument.
- `parse_rgwx_mtime` moved from `rgw_rest_client.cc` to `rgw_common` and is
  now stricter, so requests and sync responses share one parser.
- For multipart, the mtime is passed on the MultipartUpload object, like
  object lock and checksum settings. No SAL interface or on-disk change.
- Object lock default retention counts from this mtime, the same as
  lifecycle. An explicit retain-until date still wins.
- Multisite (raised on the tracker): sync only applies a remote object if its
  mtime is newer, so an object with an old mtime loses to newer copies.
  cc @mheler 

## Testing
Tested on a vstart cluster: the new workunit, lifecycle expiration and object
lock with old mtimes, and the s3-tests multipart, versioning, object_lock and
lifecycle tests.

73213.title: doc/rados: explain which daemons use the cluster network
73213.author: anthonyeleven
73213.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/58687

The tracker asks whether Monitors and MDSes also use the cluster network to reach OSDs. The diagram in the Network Configuration Reference shows only OSDs on it, and that is correct: `cluster_network` applies only to the osd service, and only ceph-osd picks a cluster address. The diagram's caption, though, says the cluster network offloads heartbeat traffic from the public network. OSDs send heartbeats over both networks, and a ping counts as answered only when replies arrive on both, so heartbeats are not offloaded.

- The caption now says the cluster network is optional and carries OSD replication and recovery traffic.
- A new paragraph after the diagram says which daemons use the cluster network, that OSD heartbeats must succeed on both networks, and that a cluster network failure while the public network still works can make OSDs flap.

73214.title: rgw/s3: honor object lock fields in POST object and validate CopyObject
73214.author: jzhu116-bloomberg
73214.body:
On a bucket with object lock enabled, POST object (browser-based upload) ignores the `x-amz-object-lock-mode`, `x-amz-object-lock-retain-until-date` and `x-amz-object-lock-legal-hold` form fields. The object is stored with only the bucket's default retention, or with no protection at all if the bucket has no default, and the request still returns 204. A client that asks for a retention period or a legal hold gets an object with no or wrong protection silently.

AWS does not document object lock fields for POST object, however, RGW accepts the same values as headers on PutObject, CopyObject and CreateMultipartUpload. This PR changes the POST object behavior to match with what PutObject, CopyObject and CreateMultipartUpload do.

This PR moves the object lock header parsing for PutObject, CopyObject, CreateMultipartUpload and POST object into a shared helper. CopyObject then gets the same InvalidRequest check as PutObject and CreateMultipartUpload when copying to an unlocked bucket with object lock headers.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82248
Signed-off-by: Jane Zhu [jzhu116@bloomberg.net](mailto:jzhu116@bloomberg.net)

73215.title: rgw/iam: emit ResponseMetadata after the Result element
73215.author: BenoitKnecht
73215.body:
`GetRole`, `GetRolePolicy`, `ListRolePolicies`,
`ListAttachedRolePolicies` and `GetAccountSummary` wrote `<ResponseMetadata>` before `<XResult>` inside the `<XResponse>` element. AWS always emits the result first, and SDKs with generated `awsQuery` deserializers (e.g. the Rust `aws-sdk-iam`) require the first child of `<XResponse>` to be `<XResult>`, so these calls fail with:

```
invalid result, expected GetRoleResult got StartEl { ... "ResponseMetadata" ... }
```

`botocore` tolerates either order, which is why the AWS CLI is unaffected.

Move `ResponseMetadata` after the Result section, matching the other IAM handlers.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82250

73216.title: rgw: add radosgw-admin bucket check olh-list
73216.author: k-keshava
73216.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82247

Problem

Racing PUT and DELETE requests on null versions (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81603) corrupt the bucket index of versioning-suspended buckets:

- versioned list entries (<key>\0v<epoch>\0i<instance>) that belong to no instance entry, many still flagged CURRENT, so ListObjectVersions reports several versions with IsLatest=true;
- the version marker (the plain <key> entry) overwritten by a suggested update from a bucket listing, or deleted;
- in some cases, the instance entry of the version the OLH points to is missing.

PR #72554 stops new corruption, but no existing command repairs buckets that are already affected. On a vstart cluster, none of these did:

- "bucket check" and "bucket check --fix" only recalculate stats.
- "bucket check --check-objects --fix" sends suggested updates for null versions that target the plain key, overwriting the marker again.
- "bucket check olh --fix" only handles OLH entries with exists=false and pending_removal=true.
- "bucket check unlinked --fix" only handles instance entries with versioned_epoch=0 that are not listable.
- "bucket reshard" copies the corrupted entries to the new shards.
- "object unlink" removes the _:<instance>_<name> key, not list entries.
- S3 DeleteObject with VersionId=null removes one list entry and deletes the marker, leaving the rest.

Changes

New command "radosgw-admin bucket check olh-list [--fix] [--dump-keys]", modelled on "bucket check olh". For each object in a versioned bucket it checks that:

1. Every versioned list entry belongs to an instance entry, as given by that entry's versioned_epoch. Other entries are orphaned and removed.
2. Only the version the OLH points to is CURRENT, in both its list and instance entries. If the OLH does not exist, none are.
3. While the OLH exists, the plain <key> entry is a version marker. An overwritten or missing marker is restored.
4. If the instance entry of the version the OLH points to is missing, the version is still identified: link_olh sets a version's versioned_epoch to the OLH epoch when it becomes current, so the list entry with that epoch is it, and the instance entry is restored from it. If no list entry matches, the object is reported as unresolved and that version's list entries are left alone.

Commits:

- cls/rgw: bucket_check_olh_list (read-only, returns a report) and bucket_fix_olh_list (re-checks and repairs in the same cls call, so a repair is serialized with normal index operations on that shard). An object with a pending index op, or an OLH log entry newer than rgw_pending_bucket_index_op_expiration, is reported as busy and left alone. Older ones are treated as abandoned, so a crashed RGW cannot block repairs forever.
- rgw: the radosgw-admin command. It walks each shard's OLH entries in parallel coroutines (--max-concurrent-ios) and refuses unversioned buckets and non-Normal index layouts. It counts busy and unresolved objects, and fails with a clear error on OSDs without the new cls methods. --dump-keys prints orphaned_list_entries, wrong_current_flags, bad_version_marker, restored_instance and unresolved per object. After --fix it tells users to run "bucket check --fix" to recalculate the stats. Also updates the usage text (help.t), the man page and PendingReleaseNotes.
- test/cls_rgw: 6 tests: healthy objects, orphaned entries plus a wrong CURRENT flag plus an overwritten marker, a missing marker, busy objects, restoring a missing instance entry (a later null PUT then replaces it cleanly), and unresolved objects.
- qa/rgw: test_rgw_bucket_check.py injects orphaned entries and overwritten markers with "radosgw-admin bi put" and checks that olh-list finds and fixes them.

Testing

On a vstart cluster (Ubuntu 24.04 arm64), on this branch rebased onto main at c57633a64a2. There was one rebase conflict: upstream moved the OPT enum into radosgw-admin.h, so BUCKET_CHECK_OLH_LIST was added there.

- Build: cls_rgw, radosgw-admin, the vstart daemons

73220.title: mds: do not merge a small dirfrag that is still hot
73220.author: xiubli
73220.body:
`MDBalancer::maybe_fragment()` splits a dirfrag when it is hot (`pop_me` above `mds_bal_split_rd/wr`), whatever its size, and merges a dirfrag when it is small (`CDir::should_merge()`, below `mds_bal_merge_size`), whatever its load. A small directory that many clients use, such as a shared `__pycache__` or a lock or publish directory, is split because it is hot, its frags are merged because they are small, the merged frag is hot again and is split again, and so on.

Every split and merge freezes the dirfrags. Each cycle, requests in the directory wait for the freeze ("failed to authpin, dir is being fragmented"), and for a few seconds after it the MDS serves a fraction of its normal rate.

A small hot directory is then split at most once, and stays that way until it cools down, when it is merged as before.

- a memstore OSD, so that the MDS is the bottleneck;
- a fresh cluster per run, 3 runs per build, interleaved, 20 s per client count;
- ops/s is the op count divided by the step length, and latencies are in ms, pooled over the runs;

73223.author: shraddhaag
73223.body:
This PR ensures that `attr_cache` is always valid for erasure coded pools. While in most places it was valid, the following two are fixed with this PR:

73225.title: rgw: restrict SSE-KMS key ids to their tenant or bucket owner
73225.author: vupn0712
73225.body:
## Summary

https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82278

For SSE-KMS, RGW takes the key id straight from the client's
`x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id` header (or the bucket's
`PutBucketEncryption` default) and hands it to whichever KMS backend is
configured, without checking that the key actually belongs to the
caller's tenant or to the bucket owner.

That matters because RGW talks to the KMS backend under one shared,
RGW-wide credential -- a single Vault token, or a single Keystone user
for Barbican -- not the caller's own identity. So if tenant A knows (or
guesses) a key id that belongs to tenant B, nothing stops them from
using it to encrypt their own objects. B's key policy never gets
consulted, because the request RGW sends doesn't carry A's identity at
all.

This adds an off-by-default option, `rgw_crypt_s3_kms_key_scope`
(`none`/`tenant`/`owner`), that makes RGW require the key id to start
with an owner prefix before it'll use it -- the check runs inside RGW,
in `rgw_s3_prepare_encrypt()`, before any KMS backend is contacted, and
also in `RGWPutBucketEncryption::execute()` so a bad default key id gets
rejected when it's set, not just at first use. It covers every write
path (PUT, POST, multipart init, copy destination) since they all go
through the same code before encrypting.

For `owner` scope, tenant and user id get joined with the same
separator you configure (e.g. `tenant.user`) rather than Ceph's usual
`tenant$user` notation, because `$` turns out to be one of several
characters Vault's transit engine rejects in a key name (along with
`/`, `:`, `,`, `~`, and `+` -- only `.`, `-`, and `_` actually work, and
`-` is a bad choice if your key ids are UUIDs since the matching logic
would grab the UUID's own dashes instead of the real boundary).

None of this touches decryption or SSE-S3 -- an object's stored key id
is never re-validated after it's written, and SSE-S3 has its own,
separate key-management path entirely.

### Backend compatibility

I didn't want to just assume this works the same everywhere, so I
actually checked each backend:

- **Vault** -- works. Verified end to end on a real single-node Ceph
  cluster against a real Vault 1.15.6 transit backend (compat=0), with
  two tenants: using your own (correctly prefixed) key works and
  decrypts fine, using the other tenant's key gets 403 AccessDenied, and
  a key id with no recognizable prefix gets rejected too.
- **KMIP** -- also works, though for a less obvious reason: RGW's KMIP
  client does a LOCATE by name before it ever fetches a key, which only
  works if whoever created the key already gave it a real, chosen name
  (see the key-creation example already in `doc/radosgw/kmip.rst`).
  Verified the same two-tenant test against a real PyKMIP 0.10.0 server,
  same outcome as Vault.
- **Barbican** -- doesn't work. Barbican assigns its own UUID to every
  secret when it's created and gives you no way to prefix it yourself,
  so turning this option on with `rgw_crypt_s3_kms_backend = barbican`
  would just deny every SSE-KMS request. Noted with warnings in
  `rgw.yaml.in` and `doc/radosgw/barbican.rst`, which also gets into why
  Barbican needs a different fix altogether: RGW authenticates to it as
  one shared Keystone user for every tenant, so Barbican's own
  per-secret ACLs can't tell RGW's tenants apart either.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests in `src/test/rgw/test_rgw_kms.cc` for the prefix-matching
      logic itself (disabled by default, matching prefix, mismatched
      prefix, missing separator, empty expected owner).
- [x] Built the full RPM set and deployed it to a real Ceph cluster;
      manually tested against a real Vault 1.15.6 server and a real
      PyKMIP 0.10.0 server (details above).
- [ ] Haven't submitted an s3-tests case for the cross-tenant-key
      rejection yet.

73226.title: mgr/tests: give the cephfs mock real exception classes
73226.author: tchaikov
73226.body:
Starting with pytest 9.2, monkeypatch.setattr() looks up the value to restore in the target's `__dict__` (pytest-dev/pytest#10644). But Mock stores the attributes it creates on first access in `_mock_children`, not in `__dict__`. So when test_mocked_fs_path_resolver finishes, undo() finds nothing to restore and deletes cephfs.ObjectNotFound, and Mock won't recreate an attribute once it has been deleted. If `test_caching_fs_path_resolver` runs later on the same xdist worker, its `monkeypatch` fails with:
```
  AttributeError: 'Mock' object at cephfs has no attribute 'ObjectNotFound'
```
The smb tests patched these attributes only because the mocked cephfs module had no exception classes that could go in an except clause. Mock the cephfs exceptions the same way the rados ones are mocked, and remove the monkeypatch calls.

73232.title: crush,osd: do not bias upmap remaps towards position 0 (primary / EC shard 0)
73232.author: FredNass
73232.body:
The upmap balancer moves the shard at position 0 (the primary, shard 0 on EC pools) much more often than any other shard. When the balancer has to fill a CRUSH bucket from other buckets, the OSDs of that bucket end up with several times the average number of primaries, even though PG counts look perfectly balanced. In production we saw this on a Reef EC 6+2 pool: ~50 primaries per OSD on two hosts against a pool mean of 10, 94% of them placed by `pg_upmap_items`.

**Cause:** two scans in the upmap code always start at position 0 and keep the first candidate:
- `CrushWrapper::_choose_type_stack()`: when a bucket has overfull leaves but no underfull candidates, the first alternative bucket goes to the lowest eligible position.
- `OSDMap::find_best_remap()`: it keeps the most overfull source OSD with a strict `>`, so the frequent ties go to the lowest position.

**Fix:** seed both scans with `pg.ps()`, so they start at `seed % size` and wrap around. The balancer still does not consider primaries, but remaps are spread evenly over positions, so the primary distribution follows CRUSH. The amount of balancer work and the resulting PG distribution are unchanged. Existing `pg_upmap_items` are not touched, so upgrading causes no data movement.

**Testing:**
- New test `OSDMapTest.calc_pg_upmaps_no_primary_bias`: 20 racks x 2 hosts x 4 OSDs, size-8 EC pool, rack-0 at 1/4 of its weight.
  - Without the fix it fails: 34.6% of remapped shards at position 0, and 19.4 primaries per rack-0 OSD against a mean of 6.4.
  - With the fix: 13.8% at position 0, and 7.5 primaries per rack-0 OSD.
- `unittest_osdmap` and `unittest_crush_wrapper` pass.
- Offline osdmaptool reproduction, 320 OSDs, 3 seeds: primaries per OSD in the under-weighted rack drop from 23-36 to 3-14 (pool mean 8), with identical PG balance. Details in the tracker.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82280

73233.title: mgr/cephadm: migrate user-provided grafana certificates from tentacle
73233.author: rkachach
73233.body:
Tentacle stored per-host grafana certificates in certmgr as grafana_cert and grafana_key. These are now grafana_ssl_cert and grafana_ssl_key, and the certificate used by the service is selected through the spec's certificate_source. The old entries are no longer loaded by the TLSObjectStore, so after upgrading a user-provided grafana certificate is silently replaced by a cephadm-signed one.

Add migration 11 -> 12 which reads the legacy entries straight from the mgr store and copies every valid user-provided cert/key pair to the new names as an editable, user-made pair. A certificate is considered cephadm-generated when it was not marked user-made and its issuer is either the cephadm root CA (tentacle) or the legacy Ceph/cephadm self-signed issuer (squid and earlier); squid custom certificates were carried into the tentacle store without user_made, so the issuer check is needed to classify them correctly. When every host running grafana ends up with a user-provided pair, the grafana spec is switched to certificate_source 'reference'.

Expired, unparsable or key-less certificates are not migrated, and entries already present under the new names are kept. The legacy entries are left in the mgr store.



Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01NXbd15da9Dswe3G4Dygg6x

73234.title: mgr/cephadm: fix certmgr reference certificates for grafana
73234.author: rkachach
73234.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82283

On Umbrella, a user-supplied per-host grafana certificate set with `certmgr` could not be made to work:

- With `certmgr cert set` + `certmgr key set`, the key was removed as soon as grafana reconciled its certificates, so certmgr reported `missing key` and grafana fell back to a self-signed certificate.
- With `certmgr cert-key set --hostname <host>`, the key stayed but the certificate was still not found when the host name in `orch host ls` differs from the host FQDN.
- In both cases, grafana with ssl enabled was deployed with empty cert/key files instead of failing, replacing a working daemon with a broken one.

## Changes

- **`certmgr key set` stores keys as editable, user-made objects**, the same as `cert set` and `cert-key set`. Previously they matched the marking used for inline-saved credentials and were removed by `rm_inline_saved_cert_key_pair()` on reconcile.
- **Per-host `reference` certificates are looked up by orchestrator host name**, falling back to the FQDN so certificates registered under the FQDN (as the docs used to recommend) keep working. Grafana docs updated.
- **Grafana is not deployed without its TLS certificate/key** when ssl is enabled. A new placement fails with `CEPHADM_DAEMON_PLACE_FAIL`; a reconfig/redeploy of an existing daemon is aborted and it keeps its current config.
- **The apply-time warning for per-host `reference` certificates** now recommends `certmgr cert-key set` instead of separate `cert set`/`key set` (it also passed the cert name as `--key-name`).

## Tests

- `test_grafana_reference_per_host` is no longer an expected failure; moved to `TestCertMgrHostScope`, and the dedicated facet and its ignorelist are removed.
- New QA tests:
  - per-host reference cert provisioned with `cert set` + `key set`: grafana serves it, the stored cert/key are unchanged after deploy, and the cert check is clean;
  - grafana applied before its reference cert exists: not deployed, `CEPHADM_DAEMON_PLACE_FAIL` raised, then deployed and cleared once the cert is set (own facet, since the warning is expected);
  - cert registered under the FQDN still served (skipped when FQDN == host name).

## Backport

Umbrella is affected; all commits are intended for backport.

73239.title: log: report failure to open the log file on stderr
73239.author: mkhon
73239.body:
`Log::reopen_log_file()` ignores a failed `open()` of the log file. A daemon that cannot create its log file, for example because `/var/log/ceph` does not exist in a read-only container, then silently loses everything below the `err_to_stderr` level, with no hint why its log is empty.

This prints the error on stderr, the same way a failed `fchown()` of the log file is already reported right below:

```
failed to open log file /var/log/ceph/ceph-osd.0.log: (2) No such file or directory
```

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82296

Nothing is printed when file logging is off: with `log_to_file=false` the log file path is cleared before the reopen, so `open()` is not attempted.

73240.title: DNM: qa_triage: the shared library of what it learned
73240.author: aainscow
73240.body:
jenkins do not test

**Do not merge.** This holds the shared library of [qa_triage](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73070), the tool that triages the failed jobs of teuthology runs, on a branch that anyone with write access to ceph/ceph can push to: a pull request lets maintainers push to its branch. It is here so that what the tool learns from everyone's reviews is shared, until the library has a home of its own.

It is everything in `src/script/qa_triage/library/`:

- `problems/`: the records of known problems, one per tracker issue, or per pull request for a problem nobody filed an issue for: where each hangs in the tool's decision tree, and the log checks that confirm it.
- `nodes/`: the questions the decision tree learned, as Python that the tool checks before it runs it, and `wording.yaml`, how the tree's answers read.
- `labels/`: the jobs people settled: what each failure is, as a reviewer said.
- `memory/`: what people answered for each kind of failure, from the RADOS wiki of reviewed runs and the tracker.
- `scripts/`: scripts people wrote to pull debug data out of a job's logs.

To use it, set this in `~/.config/qa_triage/config.yaml`:

```yaml
db: https://github.com/aainscow/ceph.git#wip-qa-triage-db:src/script/qa_triage/library
```

The tool then fetches only this directory of this branch, keeps it up to date, and pushes what is learned back here, once it passes the tool's checks and the person approves it. Each change is a commit on this branch, so it can be reviewed and reverted here.

The CI that runs for ceph pull requests is not for this: "jenkins do not test" above keeps Jenkins off it.

73241.title: include/scope_guard: make scope_guard non-movable
73241.author: tchaikov
73241.body:
The defaulted move constructor left the moved-from guard armed, so a guard that was moved ran its action twice, once from each object. The defaulted move assignment threw away the action the target was holding, and the moved-from guard still ran later. It only compiled for callables that can be assigned, which rules out any lambda with
captures.

No caller moves or assigns a guard, and `make_scope_guard()` doesn't need to move one either: since C++17, both its return statement and "auto g = make_scope_guard(...)" construct the guard in place. So instead of fixing the move constructor, drop it. Deleting the copy constructor and copy assignment also suppresses the implicit move operations, so a guard can be neither copied nor moved.

`make_scope_guard()` didn't compile when given an lvalue: with `F = T&`, the `const F&` and `F&&` constructors end up with the same signature. Decay F, so the guard keeps its own copy of the callable.

While at it, mark the constructors `[[nodiscard]]`, and drop the `in_place_type` overload of `make_scope_guard()`, which nobody calls.

73242.title: rgw/cloud-sync: keep the tenant out of the destination bucket name
73242.author: supriti
73242.body:
get_path() joined the tenant and the bucket name with a '-', so the tenanted bucket proj1/data and an untenanted bucket called proj1-data both expanded to "proj1-data" and overwrote each other at the destination.

Use get_namespaced_name() instead. It joins with a '/', which is never legal in a bucket name, so the tenant stays in the object key and the two cannot collide.

That only holds while something in target_path comes before ${bucket}. get_target() splits the path at the first '/' to get the destination bucket name, so a template starting with ${bucket} would hand it the tenant on its own. Refuse that case and log what to change.

73246.title: mds: drop stopped ranks from the resolve and rejoin gathers
73246.author: anthonyeleven
73246.body:
When max_mds is reduced and other ranks restart while the top rank is still in up:stopping, a recovering rank can wait forever in up:resolve or up:rejoin for a message from the rank that has since stopped.

resolve_gather and rejoin_gather are seeded from the recovery set, which includes up:stopping ranks. Once such a rank finishes stopping, it never sends its resolve or rejoin, and its late messages are dropped as stale. Nothing removes it from the gathers. handle_mds_map() handles a newly stopped rank only while this rank is clientreplay, active or stopping, and MDCache::set_recovery_set() only replaces the set, even when the set is recalculated after a restart.

Following the review on #38328, set_recovery_set() now drops ranks that left the recovery set from resolve_gather, rejoin_gather and rejoin_ack_gather, and finishes the gather if that was the last outstanding member. handle_mds_map() recalculates the recovery set when it shrinks while this rank is in resolve, reconnect or rejoin. A failed or restarting rank stays in the recovery set, so only ranks that have finished stopping, and so hold no subtrees or cache, are dropped.

Reproduced on 18.2.8 with three active ranks: lower max_mds to 2, fail rank 1, and once a standby has taken it, mark the fs not joinable and fail rank 0. After rank 2 stops and the fs is joinable again, stock ranks 0 and 1 stay in up:rejoin indefinitely, with rank 1's rejoin_gather still holding rank 2. With this change backported, both ranks go active within seconds. A qa test with the same steps is included in test_failover.py; it has not run under teuthology yet.

This supersedes #37701 and #38328. #71644 also edits set_recovery_set(), to add ranks that newly join the recovery set. The two are complementary, and whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase that keeps both loops.
