73254.title: pool migration: fixes and reproducers for trackers 82289-82295
73254.author: aainscow
73254.body:
Stacked on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/69112 (pool migration, at 3d0fac933b8): only the last seven commits are
new. Each commit fixes one tracker, carries its reproducer and stands alone, so any of them can be taken into #69112.

- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82291 mgr: `adjust_pgs()` stopped recording pool names when it learned to skip
  nopgchange pools, so the `osd rm-pg-upmap-primary-all` that a merge waits for was never sent and pg_num decreases
  of pools with a pg_upmap_primary entry stalled. The names are recorded again.
- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82290 mon: a create of a pool that was still pending answered "already exists" at
  once, so a client that resent its create could find no pool on its next command. It now waits for the update and
  runs again, as on main.
- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82292 osd: the OSD read the source of a client's `copy_from` at the migration target
  the client had addressed, so an object whose PG had not migrated was not found (ENOENT). The source is now read
  from the migration's root, which the OSD's Objecter routes to the pool that has the object.
- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82293 mon, mgr: a migration no longer sets the target's autoscale mode to off and
  nopgchange on, or forces autoscale on and clears nopgchange when it finishes. Instead the monitor refuses pg_num and
  pgp_num changes to any migrating pool, and the autoscaler skips migrating pools. The source pool keeps the freeze
  as before.
- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82294 mon: a snap removal is recorded against the migration target of its time.
  After a later migration the monitor no longer found it, so a resent removal was queued again, also for the source
  whose OSDs had already purged the snap, and they aborted in the snap trimmer
  (`interval_set.h: 568: FAILED ceph_assert(false)` in `adjust_purged_snaps`). The monitor now looks in every pool of
  the migration.
- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82289 osd: a source delete that could not get the object's write lock was retried
  only by recovery, while the object held a recovery slot until its delete completed, so a PG's migration could stall
  for good. The delete is now retried from the op queue when the lock is released. A debug option,
  `osd_debug_pool_migration_hold_source_delete`, makes the test deterministic by holding a read lock on the next
  object a migration deletes from its source.
- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82295 test/librados: `LibRadosList.PoolMigrationRadosLS*` are skipped when the
  poolmigration experimental feature is off, and stop when their setup fails, instead of crashing.

The 82293 commit also updates `TEST_osd_pool_create_migrate_from` (osd-pool-create.sh), which checked the old
nopgchange messages. That test cannot pass on #69112 alone; https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73154 fixes it, and these
two PRs touch neighbouring lines of it and of the pool create handler.

Tested: full build (gcc, Debug) of this branch and of #69112 at 3d0fac933b8. Each reproducer fails without its fix
and passes with it:

- 82291, `TEST_merge_with_upmap_primary` (qa/standalone/mgr/balancer.sh): without the fix pg_num stayed at 4 for the
  whole 120 s and the mgr logged "merge target 1.1 has upmap" every 2 s; with it the pool reached pg_num 2 and the
  entry was removed.
- 82290, `TEST_replicated_pool_create_resent` (osd-pool-create.sh): without the fix the second create answered "pool
  'resent' already exists" and the `osd pool get` after it failed with ENOENT.
- 82292, osd-pool-migration-copy-from.sh: without the fix `rados cp` failed with ENOENT while a get of the same object
  worked; with it the copy matches.
- 82293, osd-pool-migration-autoscale.sh: without the fix the migrated pool's autoscale mode was `on` instead of the
  `warn` it was created with. pg_num and pgp_num changes are refused during the migration with and without it.
- 82294, osd-pool-migration-snap-remove.sh: without the fix the second removal queued th

73255.title: mon/MonmapMonitor: tell the peon when a forwarded mon_join is ignored
73255.author: aainscow
73255.body:
A monitor that needs to join, or to change its location for `--set-crush-location`, sends a mon_join to the leader rank from a peer's probe reply. When that rank is its own, for example a restarted leader whose peers still follow it, the join goes to the monitor itself and is forwarded to the leader once the monitor is back as a peon. By then the leader has usually applied the join, and `preprocess_join()` dropped it without `no_reply()`, so the peon kept the routed request, resent it after every election and reported SLOW_OPS until it restarted.

`preprocess_join()` now calls `no_reply()` when it drops a join, as the other services do for messages they ignore.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82307

73256.title: mon/MonmapMonitor: make mon set_new_tiebreaker idempotent
73256.author: aainscow
73256.body:
Replacing the stretch mode tiebreaker with a new monitor in the same zone, as Rook does when it fails over the arbiter monitor, succeeded the first time and failed with EINVAL ("... matches mons <old tiebreaker>") when the command ran again, because the old tiebreaker is still in the monmap and is no longer skipped by the location check. The command can run twice without the user repeating it: an election can lose its reply (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81930), and clients resend commands after a reconnect. Rook then got an error for a change that had been made, and its failover stopped before removing the old monitor.

`mon set_new_tiebreaker` now replies success without a change when the named monitor is already the tiebreaker, as `mon add disallowed_leader` does for a monitor that is already disallowed.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82308

73264.title: mds: don't ack dirfrag replicas whose inode isn't replicated to the peer
73264.author: anthonyeleven
73264.body:
A surviving (active) MDS can abort in `MDCache::handle_cache_rejoin_ack()` on `ceph_assert(isolated_inodes.empty())` while peer ranks are in up:rejoin. This is tracker 80407, the same assert as 62036 and 50821, and distinct from 80402 and 54840.

The crash starts on the recovering rank. When it processes a surviving peer's strong rejoin for a fragmented directory that it does not have in cache, it invents a single `frag_t()` dirfrag and records the peer as a replica of it. After it fetches the inode, `opened_undef_inode()` → `CInode::force_dirfrags()` splits that dirfrag, and `CDir::split()` copies the replica map onto every leaf, so the peer is now recorded as a replica of leaves it never held. If the peer then trims the directory and sends a cache expire before the recovering rank sends its acks, the expire removes the peer from the inode and from the leaves it actually had, but the remaining leaves keep the stale replica. The 2014 sweep in `handle_cache_expire()` only runs when the named dirfrag is missing, so it doesn't catch this. `rejoin_send_acks()` then acks those leaves to the peer without the inode, the peer builds an unconnected dirfrag that nothing in the ack links, and the assert fires. The deferral from #52648 doesn't help, because it keys on `rejoin_done`, which is null on an active survivor.

A dirfrag replica cannot exist without an inode replica, so acking a dirfrag to a peer we don't record as a replica of its inode is never correct. This drops such stale replicas in `rejoin_send_acks()` instead of acking them, for inodes we are authoritative for. Base inodes, inodes we are not authoritative for (the subtree-root case the in-tree FIXME describes) and subtree-root dirfrags are left alone. Subtree roots are known from the subtree map after replay and are never invented and split, and the walk can reach one before the "peer missed MDentryLink" fix-up has run for its inode. The check doesn't rely on replica nonces, which are unreliable after a split.

The race window is short, so this also adds a dev-only option, `mds_debug_rejoin_ack_delay` (default 0), that defers `rejoin_send_acks()` with a timer while the rank keeps processing messages. The new test in `qa/tasks/cephfs/test_rejoin.py` uses it: a fragmented directory one level below an export-pinned directory, a survivor holding its inode and one leaf, fail the auth rank, and drop the survivor's cache during the delay. It has not run under teuthology yet.

Reproduced on 18.2.8 with three active ranks and the delay backported. Stock crashed the survivor on the assert. With the fix, the recovering rank logged dropping 26 stale leaf replicas instead of acking them, the survivor stayed up, and all ranks went active.

@vshankar @batrick @xiubli

73273.title: osd, os/bluestore, kv: keep read-once data out of the OSD's caches
73273.author: ming1
73273.body:
## Motivation

On dense RGW hosts memory per OSD is a direct cost, and an OSD runs up to
its `osd_memory_target` under RGW small-object writes, deep scrub and
backfill although almost nothing it caches is used again: every onode
touched and every RocksDB block read goes to the front of its cache, and
the tuner, which looks only at recency, hands them the budget. Keeping
read-once data out of the caches halves the peak under RGW writes at the
same throughput, which makes a lower `osd_memory_target` for RGW workloads
possible without hurting performance.

## What changes

1. `osd`: recovery push reads use `FADVISE_DONTNEED`
   (`RecoveryHandle::cache_dont_need` was never set).
2. `osd`: EC recovery reads use it too, in both EC backends; the shards read
   for a reconstruction are sent once, and the sources kept them cached.
3. `os/bluestore`: an onode enters a bounded probation FIFO and is admitted
   to the LRU on its second later use. `bluestore_onode_cache_probation_ratio`
   (0.1; 0 = old behaviour); probation keeps the last four age bins of
   arrivals and at least 1024 onodes per shard, so backfill scans and hot
   sets are not evicted early. Perf counter `onodes_probation`.
4. `kv/rocksdb_cache`: the same for `binned_lru` blocks.
   `rocksdb_cache_probation_ratio` (0.1; 0 = off); probation is not binned,
   so the tuner sees it at its lowest priority. Counter `probation`.

Applies on main, no dependency on open PRs. `unittest_bluestore_types`
passes (155/155).

## Test results

A/B against the unchanged build: 2-OSD vstart cluster on two NVMe drives,
`osd_memory_target` 4 GiB, every workload on a cluster created from scratch
for each build (drives discarded first). Peak RSS of osd.0, GiB:

| Workload | Before | After | Change | Time or throughput, before -> after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Deep scrub, all PGs, osd.0 / osd.1 | 4.30 / 4.34 | 1.28 / 1.28 | **-70%** | 420 s -> 404 s |
| Recovery, source OSD | 3.72 | 2.58 | **-31%** | clean after 287 s -> 292 s |
| Recovery, target OSD | 1.97 | 1.61 | -18% | degraded 4K writes 88.2k -> 87.0k IOPS |
| RGW PUT 4 MiB | 2.12 | 1.57 | **-26%** | 1152 -> 1177 MiB/s |
| RGW PUT 4 KiB | 4.74 | 2.08 | **-56%** | 8472 -> 8459 obj/s |
| RGW GET 4 MiB | 4.37 | 4.09 | **-6%** | **2187 -> 2408 MiB/s** |
| RGW GET 4 KiB | 3.62 | 2.81 | **-22%** | 3091 -> 3091 obj/s |
| RBD write 4 MiB | 1.61 | 1.60 | -1% | 1374 -> 1406 MiB/s |
| RBD write 4 KiB | 2.34 | 2.23 | -5% | 33.9k -> 32.8k IOPS |
| RBD read 4 KiB | 3.55 | 3.57 | +1% | 174k -> 169k IOPS |
| RBD read 4 MiB | 4.35 | 4.53 | +4% | 4320 -> 4407 MiB/s |

The same with the RGW data pool erasure coded (k=4 m=2, six OSDs on the two
drives, every pool on a new cluster per run). Peak RSS of the highest OSD,
GiB:

| Workload, EC 4+2 data pool | Before | After | Change | Time or throughput, before -> after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| RGW PUT 4 MiB | 1.15 | 0.95 | -17% | 1079 -> 1079 MiB/s |
| RGW PUT 4 KiB | 4.57 | 1.63 | **-64%** | 6210 -> 7039 obj/s |
| RGW GET 4 MiB | 4.46 | 3.49 | -22% | 2058 -> 2260 MiB/s |
| RGW GET 4 KiB | 4.14 | 2.99 | -28% | 3075 -> 3076 obj/s |
| Deep scrub | 4.44 | 1.24 | **-72%** | 340 s -> 325 s |
| EC shard rebuild, source OSDs | 3.05 | **1.16** | **-62%** | 158 s -> 156 s |

The rebuild row is patch 2's: patch 1 is read by the replicated backend
only, and without patch 2 each of the five sources caches 1.9 GiB of shard
data.

Scrub is faster because the smaller onode block cache hits more (19.1 M
hits / 0.92 M misses against 12.4 M / 1.09 M). Recovery time is within 2%
over three pairs. GET 4 MiB re-reads a 2,500-object set: both builds hit
the data cache at its resident share, the patched one 10-12% faster as its
cache no longer competes with the PUT residue. RBD, the hot-set check, stays
within 3% in every phase. A second set of pairs agreed within spread.

Probation ratios swept over 0.05-0.5: 0.05 doubles the hot set's block cache
misses, 0.25 and 0.5 add 0.6 and 1.8 GiB to the scrub peak for no gain in
time;

73274.title: qa/cephfs: wait for the tick before checking phase tracker lock counters
73274.author: vshankar
73274.body:
test_enabled_under_load reads the mds_lock perf counters as soon as the tracker has seen 100 client requests. Unlike the per-phase counters, which are updated as each phase ends, those counters are only fed by update_lock_stats() from MDSRank::tick(), and enabling the tracker resets them. A busy workload can cross the request threshold well within one mds_tick_interval of the reset, leaving lock_acquisitions at 0 while `dump phase times`, which computes the lock stats on the spot, already reports thousands of acquisitions.

Wait for the first tick to publish the lock stats before asserting on them.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82353

73276.title: crimson/osd: OperationThrottler should not sleep on a future mClock tag
73276.author: mohit84
73276.body:
Reduce admission latency in OperationThrottler by having background_task wait on its condition variable instead of sleeping when the head mClock item is not yet due.When dequeue() returns a future tag background_task runs seastar::sleep() until that time. Ops that arrive meanwhile including immediate ops (RepRequest, LogMissingRequest, etc), which are served before mClock’s classes wait out the whole sleep.

Fix: co_await cv.wait(timeout) in place of the sleep.
     Enqueue, release_throttle() and stop() then wake it
     and dequeue() runs again immediately.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82357

73277.title: mgr/dashboard: draw cd-usage-bar without Carbon Charts
73277.author: vobruba-martin
73277.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82358

`cd-usage-bar` drew every usage bar as a Carbon meter chart (`ibm-meter-chart`). In tables, where one bar is rendered per row, this blocks the browser: on the OSDs page of a cluster with 444 OSDs and 50 rows per page, rendering the table took about 8 seconds.

Each meter chart measures its DOM while it is being built, and the component read the threshold color with `getComputedStyle()`. Every measurement forces a style recalculation of the whole page, and each recalculation gets more expensive as the table grows, so the cost grows quadratically with the number of rows.

This PR draws the usage bar with plain HTML and CSS instead, keeping the look of the meter chart (labels, status colors and indicator, range indicator) and shows the used/available/total values in a Carbon tooltip styled like the meter chart tooltip. The bar needs no layout measurements while the table is rendered. The tooltip measures only when it is opened.

### Measurements

Trace of the OSDs page with 444 OSDs, 50 rows per page:

| | Carbon meter chart | HTML/CSS bar |
|---|---|---|
| Rendering 50 rows | 8089 ms | 1356 ms |
| Forced style recalculations | 950 | 300 |
| of them caused by the usage bars | 650 (~6.2 s) | 0 |

The remaining 300 recalculations come from the Read/Write bytes sparklines, which are out of scope here.

### Other changes in behaviour

- The tooltip opens when hovering anywhere over the bar or its labels. The meter chart showed it only over the used (filled) part, so at 0 % usage the user had to hit a single pixel.
- The meter chart took values and thresholds only once in `ngOnInit()`, so table refreshes and thresholds loaded later (e.g. the OSD nearfull/full ratios) were ignored.
- A usage of 100 % and more is consistently shown as danger (the meter chart drew 100 % in the primary color with a danger icon and no label).
- The bar shrinks with narrow columns instead of painting over the neighbouring cells.
- The status colors no longer depend on the theme custom properties being defined on the element.
- The inputs which only configured the chart (`height`, `totalUnit`, `animations`, `legendEnabled`, `toolbarEnabled`, `tooltipOptions`, `customColorScale`) are dropped; none of them is used.

### Screenshot

Carbon meter chart (left) and the new bar (right):

![usage bar comparison](https://tracker.ceph.com/attachments/download/8694/usage-bar-compare.png)

73286.title: messages/MOSDPGPush: send the pushed data in the data segment
73286.author: ming1
73286.body:
Recovery and backfill targets copy every pushed byte, because `PushOp` data travels in the message payload, which msgr2 does not page align. Send it in the data segment instead: MOSDPGPush v5 (compat 5) for peers with `SERVER_VAMPIRE`; older peers still get v4.

Note: OSDs built from main before this change advertise `SERVER_VAMPIRE` but cannot decode v5; do not mix the two.

Tested on vstart: recovering a 4 MiB object made 64 aligned 64 KiB copies on the target; with this change, none. New unit test: `MOSDPGPush.data_segment` in `unittest_osd_types`.

73287.title: rgw: honor Object Lock and keep cloud transition metadata consistent
73287.author: viduship
73287.body:
Cloud transition was skipping the Object Lock check for current versions. This fix checks all versions and keeps locked objects in Ceph without creating delete markers. Unlocked objects and objects whose retention has expired can still transition.

Updating retention also changed the object’s modification time without updating its bucket listing entry. This mismatch could cause transitions to fail with ECANCELED. The fix updates both entries together while keeping the version order and current-version status unchanged.

The PR has two commits: one for the bucket index update and one for the Object Lock check. It also includes tests and documentation.

resolves https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82371

73288.title: crimson/osd: fix hanged ops in EC due to incorrect attr_cache
73288.author: shraddhaag
73288.body:
## Issue

This PR fixes 3 hangs due to obc not containing one or the other key in the attr_cache. The following cases are solved here: 

1. When an obc is reloaded from disk, in `attr_cache`, the object info with key `_` and the snapset is not loaded. In `get_write_plan()`, when `object_info_t(attr_cache.at("_"))`  tries to decode `_` key, zero bytes are decoded and it throws `end_of_buffer`. Since nothing is looking for this error, we get `Exceptional future ignored`, and the op hangs forever. 
2. After a snapshot, when an object receives a write, it should first clone the existing head obc. In `translate_transaction()`, the clone is not added to the `obc_map`. When `get_write_plan()` tries to decode the clone, its throws `std::out_of_range`, and the operation hangs forever. 
3. When the client sends a snap rollback request, both the existing head and the snap clone (which is the source for the new head), should be added to the obc_map. But only the head is added, not the snap clone. When `get_write_plan()` tries to decode the new source, it throws `std::out_of_range` and the operation hangs forever. 

## Fix
For each of the above cases, the following fixes have been made: 
1. the object info and the snapset are set when the obc is reloaded from disk. 
2. In the `obc_map`, the clone obc is also added. 
3. In the `obc_map` the source obc (the obc to rollback to) is also added. 

## Testing
QA: 
* https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/runs/shraddhaag-2026-10-30_07:41:49-crimson-rados:basic-main-distro-debug-trial 
* https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/runs/shraddhaag-2026-10-30_07:43:17-crimson-rados:thrash-main-distro-debug-trial 
* https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/runs/shraddhaag-2026-10-30_12:40:43-crimson-rados-main-distro-debug-trial

73290.title: doc/rados: add object size, I/O rate, and omap guidance
73290.author: anthonyeleven
73290.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/20215

The tracker asks for librados guidance on the trade-offs of object size, I/O rate, and omap versus regular data. Introduction to librados has none, so this adds an Object Size, I/O Rate, and Omap section at the end of the page.

- Object size: the `osd_max_object_size` limit and its scrub check, the 4 MiB objects that RBD, CephFS, and RGW use, the `min_alloc_size` cost of very small objects, and EC optimizations removing small-object padding in Tentacle and later.
- I/O rate: writes and default reads go through the primary; `LIBRADOS_OPERATION_BALANCE_READS` and `LOCALIZE_READS` let replicas serve reads, and since Umbrella balanced reads on erasure-coded pools go to the shard holding the data. Links to the read balancer and primary affinity.
- Omap: stored in RocksDB, supported on replicated pools and, since Umbrella, on erasure-coded pools with EC optimizations (#66726); the `LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS` thresholds.

73292.title: [mgmt-gateway] qa/cephadm: shared base class for cephadm_cases suites
73292.author: rkachach
73292.body:
Move the generic helpers of the certmgr teuthology suite (#72243) into a
shared base class, `CephadmTestCase` in `qa/tasks/cephadm_cases/base.py`,
so the upcoming cephadm service suites (mgmt-gateway first, #72872) build
on the same code instead of carrying another copy.

### Changes

- **qa/cephadm: add a shared base class for cephadm_cases suites**
  `CephadmTestCase(MgrTestCase)` holds what any cephadm integration suite
  needs: running `ceph` commands in `cephadm shell`, waiting for the
  orchestrator and for services, applying specs and confirming they were
  stored, polling and holding conditions, health checks and mgr failover.
  A suite sets `WORKDIR` (recreated on the admin host and mounted in
  `cephadm shell`), copies its helper scripts with `install_file()`, and
  may override `POLL_TRANSIENT` and `check_stored_spec()`. `setUpClass()`
  saves the cephadm root CA to `WORKDIR` so clients can verify what the
  daemons serve.
- **qa/cephadm: build the certmgr tests on the shared base class**
  `CertMgrTestCase` now derives from `CephadmTestCase` and keeps only the
  certmgr-specific parts (test PKI, certificate helpers, module options
  reset at teardown, TLS checks in `check_stored_spec()`). No behaviour
  change: against a recording fake cluster, the old and new classes issue
  the same commands for `apply()` (including both rejection paths),
  `wait_health()`, `wait_service()`, `rm_service()`, the certificate
  helpers and teardown.

Only helpers certmgr uses are added here; the ones needed by the service
suites come with #72872, together with their first user.

### Testing

- `orch:cephadm:certmgr` run: <link>
- flake8 / mypy clean on the changed files

73293.title: [mgmt-gateway] qa/cephadm: add orch/cephadm/services/mgmt-gateway teuthology suite
73293.author: rkachach
73293.body:
Add `orch/cephadm/services/`, meant to hold one teuthology suite per
cephadm service, and `orch/cephadm/services/mgmt-gateway` as its first
suite. It covers mgmt-gateway, oauth2-proxy and `secure_monitoring_stack`
in their different combinations, cephadm's HA setup, and what clients get
when a component goes down.

Depends on #73292 (shared `CephadmTestCase` base class); until it merges
its two commits also show up here.

The tests check what clients actually get from the daemons (status codes,
redirects, TLS and client-certificate behaviour, Prometheus scrape
targets) rather than the config cephadm writes. Requests go through
`probe.py`, run inside `cephadm shell`. The OIDC identity provider is
`oidc_idp.py`, a minimal provider run as a cephadm custom container with
the cluster's own Ceph image, so the suite pulls nothing from outside the
Ceph registries.

### Facets

| Facet | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `gateway` | one gateway, no SSO: mTLS on backends and the internal endpoint, routes and basic auth, `/health`, dashboard standby handling across a mgr failover, credential rotation, `ssl: false` (custom and default port), removal; a backend down, the gateway down |
| `oauth2` | gateway + oauth2-proxy + the test IdP: every route behind the IdP, callback URL, browser login, session across redeploy and mgr failover, dashboard SSO lifecycle; oauth2-proxy down fails closed, a backend down with a session |
| `ha` | cephadm's HA setup: 2 gateways behind a VIP (keepalive-only ingress), 2 of every service behind them; access and URLs through the VIP, keepalived failover, port left free on host addresses, session across oauth2-proxy instances; one instance of each layer down (active gateway, oauth2-proxy, prometheus, alertmanager, grafana, active mgr) unnoticed by a logged-in user |
| `transitions` | plain -> secure -> gateway -> gateway+SSO and back, gateway straight from plain, `secure_monitoring_stack` ignored with a gateway |
| `open-issues` | reproducers for bugs not fixed yet, marked `@unittest.expectedFailure`: green while the bug is there, red ("unexpected success") once fixed, as a reminder to move the test to its facet |

### cephadm bugs found by the suite

Fixed in separate PRs (needed for the `gateway`, `ha` and `transitions`
facets to pass):
- <PR C>: mgmt-gateway records and advertises port 443 with `ssl: false` and no port, while nginx listens on 80
- <PR D>: Prometheus gets `username: None` service discovery credentials when security is turned on before the SD server restarts
- <PR E>: keepalived's health check of a VIP mgmt-gateway fails on every host since #67344, so a dead gateway never loses the VIP

Still open (`open-issues` facet):
- without a VIP, internal URLs (dashboard API hosts, grafana datasource, prometheus discovery) stay on the first gateway even when it is stopped
- after an oauth2 login users land on `/` instead of the requested page (oauth2-proxy allowlist vs. the FQDN/port in the callback)

### Testing

`orch:cephadm:services:mgmt-gateway`, with the three fixes: <link>

    teuthology-suite --suite orch:cephadm:services:mgmt-gateway \
        --ceph <testing-branch> --machine-type <type> \
        --filter-out rocky -k distro

(The quay.ceph.io images are tagged `<sha1>-centos-stream9`: pass
`overrides: cephadm: distro-suffix: centos-stream9` if the default tag is
missing.)

73295.title: osd: let clients with no osd caps get EPERM instead of hanging
73295.author: anthonyeleven
73295.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/23765

A librados or librbd client whose key has only mon caps hangs on its first OSD op instead of getting EPERM.

Since the fix for https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/62382 (#52939 on main, #59307 for reef, #59306 for squid), MonClient honors the return value of `ms_handle_fast_authentication`. For a key with no osd caps at all, `OSD::ms_handle_fast_authentication` returns false, so the OSD rejects the session. The client sees a connection fault, reconnects, and never gets a reply; with `rados_osd_op_timeout` at its default of 0 it waits forever. Before that change the OSD returned 0 ("no action") here, the session stayed up with no grants, and `PrimaryLogPG::do_op` denied each op with EPERM.

Reproduced on Reef 18.2.8: with a key that has only `mon 'allow r'`, `rados -p <pool> ls` and `rbd ls <pool>` block, and the client log shows repeated `AUTH_CONNECTING` and `_fault` on the OSD connection. With `osd 'allow r pool=<other>'` added, both fail at once with `Operation not permitted`.

- Keep the session with an empty `OSDCap` when the key has no osd caps, so each op fails with EPERM. The Manager already accepts a session without caps the same way. Caps that fail to decode or parse are still rejected.
- Add a check to `qa/workunits/rados/test_pool_access.sh` that a key with only mon caps gets `Operation not permitted`, time-boxed so that a hang fails the test.

73296.title: [mgmt-gateway] python-common: default mgmt-gateway port to 80 when ssl is off
73296.author: rkachach
73296.body:
With `ssl: false` and no `port`, nginx listens on 80
(`external_server.conf.j2` uses `spec.port or 80`), but
`MgmtGatewaySpec.get_port_start()` returned 443 whatever the ssl setting.
cephadm records, port-checks and opens in the firewall the port from
`get_port_start()`, and builds the gateway's external URL from it. So it
advertised `http://<host>:443` (used e.g. for the oauth2-proxy redirect URL
and the dashboard links) while nothing listened there, and opened the
wrong firewall port.

Default to 443 with ssl and 80 without, the same rule as the template.

Found by the new `orch/cephadm/services/mgmt-gateway` teuthology suite
(#72872, gateway facet, `test_ssl_disabled_default_port`), which passes with
this fix.

73297.title: mgr/cephadm: give prometheus valid service discovery credentials
73297.author: rkachach
73297.body:
When security gets enabled at runtime (`secure_monitoring_stack` set, or
the first mgmt-gateway deployed) on a mgr that started without it,
Prometheus can end up with no scrape targets at all.

The service discovery server only sets its basic-auth credentials
(`enable_auth()`) when it restarts with security on, and that restart is
asynchronous: `config_update()` just signals the http server thread. In
the same serve loop pass, `_check_daemons()` redeploys prometheus for the
new security setting, and its config read the credentials straight from
the `ServiceDiscovery` attributes. Before the restart they are still
`None`, so `prometheus.yml` got `username: None` / `password: None`. Every
discovery request was then rejected once the server restarted with auth,
and nothing reconfigured prometheus again, since the credentials are not
one of its dependencies.

Add `ServiceDiscovery.get_credentials()`, which returns the credentials
clients must use, loading them from the mgr store (or creating them
there) when the server has not set them yet, and use it when generating
the prometheus config. `enable_auth()` loads the same stored credentials,
so both sides agree whatever the order.

Found by the new `orch/cephadm/services/mgmt-gateway` teuthology suite
(#72872, transitions facet: `test_full_cycle` saw no prometheus targets
after enabling `secure_monitoring_stack`); the facet passes with this fix.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/<id>

### Testing
- `test_prometheus_sd_credentials_before_sd_server_restart` (`test_monitoring.py`): reproduces `username: 'None'` without the fix
- `TestServiceDiscoveryCredentials` (`test_service_discovery.py`): stored credentials are created once and shared by `get_credentials()` and `enable_auth()`
- `orch:cephadm:services:mgmt-gateway` (transitions facet): <link>

73310.title: rgw/sts: use the jwks_uri host and port for thumbprint verification
73310.author: next0262
73310.body:
## Problem

With `rgw_enable_jwks_url_verification = true`, `verify_oidc_thumbprint()` opens its own TLS connection to the JWKS endpoint and compares the last certificate of the chain with the thumbprints registered on the OIDC provider. There are two defects in how it reaches the endpoint.

1. The host is taken from `jwks_uri` by stripping only the scheme and the path. An explicit port stays attached, so `https://host:6443/openid/v1/jwks` becomes `host:6443` and `gethostbyname("host:6443")` fails. Even `https://host:443/...` fails this way, as reported in the tracker.
2. The connection port is hard-coded to 443, so a provider on another port is unreachable even if the host resolves.

### Concrete case — Kubernetes service account tokens

A Kubernetes cluster can be registered as the provider for `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`, allowing pods to authenticate to RGW with projected service account tokens. The kube-apiserver issues those tokens and can serve discovery and JWKS directly on its HTTPS port, which defaults to 6443. For example, the discovery document could contain the following fields.

```sh
curl -sk https://kube-apiserver:6443/.well-known/openid-configuration
```

```json
{
  "issuer": "https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local",
  "jwks_uri": "https://kube-apiserver:6443/openid/v1/jwks"
}
```

For this setup, `jwks_uri` carries an explicit `:6443`. With endpoint verification enabled and thumbprints registered, `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` fails at the thumbprint check because RGW tries to resolve `kube-apiserver:6443` as a hostname.

The JWKS download itself (`RGWHTTPTransceiver`, curl) handles the port correctly. The failure is in the separate certificate check. Users connecting directly to a provider on a non-default port cannot enable that check and may have to leave `rgw_enable_jwks_url_verification` off, which is its default value.

## Fix

- Add `rgw::parse_url_host_port()` next to the existing Boost.URL helpers in `rgw_url.cc` and use it in `verify_oidc_thumbprint()`, with a default port of 443. A `jwks_uri` that does not parse now fails verification with a log message instead of proceeding to DNS lookup.
- Resolve the host with `getaddrinfo()` instead of the IPv4-only `gethostbyname()`, trying each returned address so IPv6 literals and AAAA records work too.
- Drop `get_top_level_domain_from_host()`, which has no other caller.

Behaviour for a `jwks_uri` without an explicit port, served on 443, is unchanged.

## Tests

`unittest_rgw_url` gains six cases for the new parser covering the default port, an explicit port, explicit 443, an IPv6 literal with a port, userinfo and invalid inputs. All 20 tests pass. Also compiled `rgw_rest_sts.cc` with the existing build dependencies.

The connection and thumbprint functions were exercised standalone against a local TLS server on ports 443 and 6443 over IPv4 and IPv6. Matching and non-matching thumbprints, a closed port and an unparsable URL behaved as expected. The pre-patch code fails the same setup with `gethostbyname failed for host: localhost:6443`. The local build has `WITH_RADOSGW=OFF`, so the full `rgw_common` build still needs CI.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74001

73312.title: doc/cephfs: describe when other clients see changes
73312.author: anthonyeleven
73312.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/24642

The tracker asks what CephFS guarantees about when a change made on one mount becomes visible on another mount, in what order, and whether files, directories, kernel clients, and FUSE clients differ. `doc/cephfs/posix.rst` says CephFS keeps strong cache coherency across clients but answers none of that, so this adds a "Visibility to other clients" section after "Bottom line".

- Namespace changes: other clients see a change only after the MDS has journaled it. After an early reply, `set_xlocks_done()` leaves the xlocks readable only by the requesting client (`LOCK_XLOCKDONE` can_read is `XCL` in `src/mds/locks.c`), and lease and `Fs` revocation happens before the change.
- `wsync`, ceph-fuse, and libcephfs return only after the MDS has made the change. libcephfs never sends async creates (`src/client/Client.cc`, the delegated_inos comment in `Client::verify_reply_trace`).
- `nowsync`, the kernel default since 5.16: only create (`try_prep_async_create`, which needs `Fx` and `Dc` on the directory) and unlink (`get_caps_for_async_unlink`, which needs `Fx` and `Du`, and not rmdir) go async. `fsync(2)` on the directory waits for them on both the kernel client (`flush_mdlog_and_wait_inode_unsafe_requests` over `i_unsafe_dirops`) and ceph-fuse (`Client::_fsync` over `unsafe_ops`).
- File data: the filelock `LOCK_MIX` state grants `Fr`, `Fw`, and `Fl` but not `Fc` or `Fb`, so while clients on several hosts have a file open for writing every read and write goes to the OSDs, and the move out of `LOCK_EXCL` makes the writer flush its buffered data first.
- Exceptions: shared writable mmap, already listed above, and LazyIO. @xiubli's #69754 adds a LazyIO bullet to the divergence list in the same file. The two changes touch different parts of the file and don't conflict.

@vshankar @xiubli, could you confirm these guarantees, in particular these two points:

1. With `wsync`, an observer on another host never sees a later namespace change from one process before an earlier one, including across directories on different MDS ranks.
2. With `nowsync`, an observer may not yet see an async create or unlink whose call has already returned. The text says it "might", and also that it might see a later change in another directory first.

73313.title: [managment-gateway] mgr/cephadm: fix keepalived health check of a VIP mgmt-gateway
73313.author: rkachach
73313.body:
Since the fix for https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74929 (#67344), an SSL
mgmt-gateway with a `virtual_ip` listens on `<vip>:<port>` only, so other
services can use that port on the host's other addresses. keepalived's
check was not adapted: it still probed `https://<host addr>:<port>/health`,
which nothing answers. The check failed on every gateway host, so all
priorities dropped by the same 20 (100/90 -> 80/70) and the VIP holder kept
the VIP when its gateway died; only keepalived or the host itself going
down moved it.

- Give nginx a second server, in that mode only, listening on
  `127.0.0.1:<port>` and serving `/health` only (404 otherwise). It binds a
  specific address, so the port stays free elsewhere as 74929 requires,
  and it is not reachable from outside the host.
- Make keepalived check the gateway on `127.0.0.1`, with the gateway's
  scheme (the check used https even with `ssl: false`, where nginx serves
  plain HTTP). keepalived and nginx both use the host network.
- Use `curl -fs --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 3` for the gateway and
  haproxy checks: without `-f` curl exits 0 on HTTP errors, and a check
  must not hang.

The template change only renders with ssl and a `virtual_ip`; without a
`virtual_ip` the nginx configuration is byte-identical to before.

Found by the new `orch/cephadm/services/mgmt-gateway` teuthology suite
(#72872). Verified on a cluster: keepalived's check passes on both gateway
hosts, and stopping the gateway on the VIP holder moves the VIP to the
other host within ~12s (ha facet, `test_active_gateway_down`).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/<id>

### Testing
- `test_keepalived_checks_mgmt_gateway_on_loopback` (`test_mgmt_gateway.py`, ssl on/off): keepalived check and the loopback `/health` server
- `test_ingress.py`: haproxy check expectations updated for the new curl flags
- `orch:cephadm:services:mgmt-gateway` (ha facet): <link>

73314.title: qa/valgrind: suppress librgw_lancedb static-init leaks by object
73314.author: djgalloway
73314.body:
Since https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73063 lancedb is built as a Rust cdylib and shipped as `librgw_lancedb.so.1`. rustc hides the crate's internal symbols in a cdylib and the package build strips `.symtab`, so valgrind only sees `obj:` frames for that library and the existing `fun:*opendal*register_default_operator_registry*` suppression no longer matches. Every rgw valgrind job then fails on 13 `Leak_PossiblyLost` records allocated from the library's ELF constructors (`call_init` / `_dl_init`), e.g. [this run](https://qa-proxy.ceph.com/teuthology/anuchaithra-2026-10-29_04:19:23-rgw-wip-anrao4-testing-2026-10-28-0758-main-distro-default-trial/689436/remote/trial097/log/valgrind/).

This adds a second suppression keyed on `obj:*/librgw_lancedb.so*` plus `fun:call_init*`, scoped to the same static-init path the original rule covered. The original rule is kept for builds with symbols.

Verified by replaying valgrind's suppression matching rules over the XML log from the failing job: all 13 errors match the new rule.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82395

73316.title: os/bluestore: declare intrusive_ptr hooks ahead of their use
73316.author: wjwithagen
73316.body:
BlueStore_fwd.h forward-declares Blob, Onode, SharedBlob and OpSequencer together with their boost::intrusive_ptr typedefs, and code such as Extent and TransContext uses those *Ref types in inline constructors before the types are complete. Their refcounting hooks are either hidden friends (Blob, Onode, SharedBlob) or come from RefCountedObject (OpSequencer); neither is found before the type is complete, so clang fails with

  error: use of undeclared identifier 'intrusive_ptr_release'

Declare the hooks in namespace bluestore next to each typedef. The friend definitions stay as they are and now define these declarations; OpSequencer gets inline definitions right after the class.

73321.title: doc/cephfs: explain large omap objects in the metadata pool
73321.author: anthonyeleven
73321.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/43034

No CephFS page says what to do when `LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS` names an object in a metadata pool. The entry in `doc/rados/operations/health-checks.rst` covers only RGW bucket index objects. This adds a "Large omap objects in the metadata pool" section to `doc/cephfs/health-messages.rst` and links it from that entry.

- Cause: with the defaults, a fragment splits at `mds_bal_split_size` (10000 head and snapshot entries, `CDir::should_split()`) and stops taking creates at `mds_bal_fragment_size_max` (100000), both well below the 200000-key threshold. In practice, the warning comes from the 1 GiB value threshold, as in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/77513.
- Object to path: dirfrag objects are named `<ino>.<frag>` (`InodeStoreBase::get_object_name`). A directory's backtrace is stored in the metadata pool on `<ino>.00000000` (`CInode::get_backtrace_pool`), and `ceph-dencoder` decodes it as `inode_backtrace_t`.
- Fix: `scrub start <path>` scrubs every fragment of the directory and calls `maybe_fragment()` afterward (`ScrubStack.cc:559`). That splits on entry count only, so for a fragment that is too large only in bytes, the section gives `dirfrag ls` and `dirfrag split`. Both need the directory in the cache of its auth MDS (`MDSRank::_command_dirfrag_get`).
- Directories the MDS won't fragment: root (`1.00000000`), stray directories (`MDBalancer::maybe_fragment`), mdsdir, and anything inside a stray directory (`MDCache::can_fragment`).
- RGW bucket index objects point to the dynamic resharding page.

A second commit adds to `LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS` in `doc/rados/operations/health-checks.rst` what the object usually is, by pool. It only adds lines after the existing paragraph, whose wording differs on tentacle, so both commits cherry-pick cleanly to umbrella and tentacle.
- In an RGW log pool, it's usually an untrimmed log. Usage logs (`usage.<n>`) need `usage trim`. `RGWSyncLogTrimThread` trims the metadata log, the data log, and bucket index logs every `rgw_sync_log_trim_interval`, but never the sync error log (`sync error trim` is manual).
- In an RGW index pool, it's a bucket index shard. Those need resharding, or, in multisite deployments, `bilog trim` after sync catches up. Beginning with the Vampire release, new buckets use FIFO bilogs in the log pool (`rgw_default_bucket_bilog_type`, `rgw_bilog.h`).
- In a CephFS metadata pool, it links the new section.
- It also says that changing `pg_num` doesn't help, since an object and its omap stay in one PG, and that the warning can outlast a split or merge until the next deep scrub.

It adds the `rgw-trim-usage` and `rgw-multisite-check-the-logs` labels so those sections can be linked.

@dparmar18's #72152 "mds: consider dirfrag size when splitting a dir" adds `mds_bal_split_bytes` and documents byte-based splits in `dirfrags.rst`. Once it merges, the "too large only in bytes" paragraph here can say that a scrub splits those fragments too. This PR doesn't touch `dirfrags.rst`, to stay clear of that one.

@vshankar @dparmar18, could you check the procedure, in particular that `dirfrag split` is the right tool for a byte-heavy fragment on current releases, and the advice for stray directories?

73322.title: mds: fix rejoin when a dirfrag holding replicated inodes is missing
73322.author: xiubli
73322.body:
When a dirfrag object is missing from the metadata pool and a surviving
rank holds replicas of inodes in it, the rank taking over the failed rank
never leaves `up:rejoin`.  The survivor rejoins those inodes, the
recovering rank invents them as REJOINUNDEF and has to load the dirfrag
in `open_undef_inodes_dirfrags()`, the object is gone, and:

- with `mds_dir_prefetch = true`, `go_bad()` marks the dirfrag complete,
  but the inodes stay undef; the next `rejoin_gather_finish()` fetches
  the complete dirfrag again and hits `ceph_assert(!is_complete())` in
  `CDir::fetch()` (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/54205), on every
  standby that takes the rank over;
- with `mds_dir_prefetch = false`, the keyed fetch leaves the dirfrag
  incomplete, and since 97e43ee7956 wakes the parked dentry waiters, so
  `rejoin_gather_finish()` fetches the same missing object again, about
  once per millisecond, for ever.

Reproduction steps and logs are in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82399.

This PR:

- marks a dirfrag BADFRAG and complete in `go_bad()` after a keyed fetch
  too, so that the woken waiters find nothing left to fetch;
- skips complete dirfrags in `open_undef_inodes_dirfrags()` and
  `open_ino_traverse_dir()`;
- drops the undef inodes that cannot be loaded from the cache of the
  recovering rank (`rejoin_trim_undef_inodes()`, which had no caller), so
  that the rejoin ack does not carry their empty inode bases, and makes
  the surviving ranks drop the replica dentries left out of the ack.
  Without this, the survivor overwrites its replica with the empty inode
  and, for a hard-linked file, crashes on the snaprealm assert in
  `CInode::decode_snap()`.  A remote link to a dropped inode is left
  dangling and returns ENOENT;
- adds `TestDamageRejoin` to `qa/tasks/cephfs/test_damage.py`.

Testing (vstart_runner, release build):

| test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `TestDamageRejoin.test_rejoin_undef_inode_missing_dirfrag` | assert in `CDir::fetch()` | ok |
| `TestDamageRejoin.test_rejoin_undef_inode_missing_dirfrag_no_prefetch` | stuck in `up:rejoin` | ok |
| `TestDamageRejoin.test_open_file_missing_dirfrag{,_no_prefetch}` | ok | ok |
| `TestDamage` | 4 ok | 4 ok |
| `TestDamageExport` | | ok |

`TestDamage.test_dentry_first_{preflush,precommit}` fail the same way on
main and with this PR in my local setup (the `ceph -w` watcher does not
reach the vstart cluster).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82399

73323.title: doc/radosgw: document lifecycle scheduling and multisite behavior
73323.author: anthonyeleven
73323.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/46992

The Lifecycle Settings section in `doc/radosgw/config-ref.rst` doesn't say when lifecycle runs or what each zone does in a multisite deployment. This adds two paragraphs and an `rgw_lifecycle_work_time` confval after `rgw_enable_lc_threads`.

- Scheduling: `LCWorker::entry()` calls `should_work()` only before it calls `RGWLC::process()`, so a run that outlasts `rgw_lifecycle_work_time` keeps going, and `schedule_next_start_time()` waits until the next window start, in local time. That matches the option's `long_desc`.
- Multisite: since 2ee22667692 "rgwlc: activate lifecycle processing on non-master zones" (tracker 44268, in Reef and Quincy 17.2.8), the bucket instance metadata handler calls `RGWLC::set_bucket_config()` when a bucket's lifecycle configuration syncs to a zone (`rgw_bucket.cc:3233`). Each zone then has the bucket in its `lc list`, so a promoted zone keeps processing. That was the failover problem in the tracker.

It only adds lines, so it cherry-picks cleanly to umbrella, tentacle, and squid, which all have `rgw_lifecycle_work_time` and the multisite fix.

@mattbenjamin, could you check the multisite paragraph, in particular that users can rely on each zone processing lifecycle on its own after a failover?

73324.title: common: count all slow ops across OpTracker shards
73324.author: anthonyeleven
73324.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/67317
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/45871

The SLOW_OPS health check often reports fewer slow ops than an OSD has, frequently 0, next to a plausible oldest op age: "0 slow ops, oldest one blocked for 129 sec, osd.285 has slow ops". `ceph daemon osd.N dump_blocked_ops` on the same OSD lists the slow ops.

`OpTracker::visit_ops_in_flight` copies every shard's in-flight list into one vector and visits it. The slow op counters in `OSD::get_health_metrics` and `OpTracker::with_slow_ops_in_flight` return false at the first op younger than the complaint time. Before 57ebdc2a77e merged the shards into one vector to fix a deadlock, tracker 42780, that ended only the walk of the current shard. Now it ends the whole walk. Ops are dealt to the shards round robin, so on a busy OSD the first shard nearly always holds a young op, and the count covers about one of the `osd_num_op_tracker_shard` shards. The MDS uses the same shard count and takes its slow request count from `check_ops_in_flight`, so `MDS_SLOW_REQUEST` can be missed as well. The mon uses one shard and is not affected.

This sorts the gathered ops by initiation time before visiting them, after the locks are released, so a visitor that stops at the first young op has seen every older one. The sort runs only when the oldest op is already past the complaint time.

The new `unittest_tracked_op` puts a young op in shard 0 and slow ops in the other shards. On unpatched main all three cases fail, with a count of 0 instead of 3. With this change they pass.

A later note on 45871 describes a down OSD that keeps showing "0 slow ops" with a frozen age. That is a separate stale metric on the mgr side, and this PR does not change it.

Question for reviewers: is sorting inside `visit_ops_in_flight` preferred over changing each visitor to skip young ops instead of stopping? Sorting keeps the early-exit contract for every caller.

73326.title: osd/PrimaryLogPG: take an op's PG log version after its ops have run
73326.author: aainscow
73326.body:
On a pool with EC optimizations, an op with a CALL runs in a coroutine, and a cls read in it yields until the EC read completes. `execute_ctx()` took the op's PG log version before running the ops. While the CALL waits, the PG lock is free, and work that does not go through `do_op()` can take versions: the snap trimmer, watch timeouts, and ops whose async reads complete. The CALL then submits a version that is already used, and the primary aborts in `issue_repop()`, on `at_version >= projected_last_update` or on PGLog's `e.version > head`.

The version is now taken in `prepare_transaction()` after `do_osd_ops()` returns, where the op can no longer yield.

The new `TestClsRbd.object_map_update_while_a_write_reads` reproduces it: on main its FastEC case aborts the primary at `PGLog.h:675`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82471
